63019.e: The Japanese SCMaglev floats on a magnetic field without wheel contact. It is planned to run in future on the Chūō Shinkansen between Tokyo and Nagoya.
63019.m: Maglev trains are faster than trains with wheels.

63020.q: Which country in South-East Asia opened the region's first high-speed railway in 2023 with Chinese involvement?
63020.e: The line connects Jakarta with Bandung over about 140 km. It was built as a project of the New Silk Road.
63020.m: Since 2023 Indonesia has had a high-speed train from Jakarta to Bandung.

63021.q: Why do high-speed trains often replace domestic flights over distances of about 300 to 800 km?
a: The travel time from city centre to city centre is similar
Trains are faster than planes over all distances
Airports may not offer such routes
63021.e: Stations are in the centre, while air travellers have to allow for getting to the airport, security checks and waiting. Over medium distances the train is therefore often just as fast or faster overall.
63021.m: Over medium distances the total travel time is what counts.

63022.q: What is the network model called in which airlines bundle their connections through a central airport?
63022.e: In the hub-and-spoke system the “spokes” lead to the “hub”, where passengers change planes. This allows many pairs of cities to be connected with few flights.
63022.m: A hub bundles connections like the hub of a wheel.

63023.q: Which airport had the most passengers in the world in 2024?
63023.e: Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta is the hub of Delta Air Lines and counted over 100 million passengers in 2024. It has topped the ranking for many years.
63023.m: Atlanta is the busiest airport in the world.

63024.q: Which airport counted the most international passengers in the world in 2024?
63024.e: Dubai International is the hub of Emirates and has practically only international flights. Atlanta has more passengers in total, but mainly on US domestic flights.
63024.m: Dubai is the largest international hub in the world.

63025.q: Why are cities such as Dubai, Doha and Istanbul especially well suited as hubs for transfer traffic?
a: They lie between Europe, Asia and Africa
They have the coolest climate for aircraft
They lie exactly on the equator
They are the most populous cities in the world
63025.e: From where they are, aircraft can reach large parts of the world's population in a few hours of flying. This allows long-haul routes to be connected with a single change.
63025.m: Their position between continents makes Gulf states into hubs.

63026.q: Which airport replaced Atatürk Airport as the hub of Turkish Airlines in 2019?
63026.e: The new Istanbul Airport on the Black Sea took over passenger traffic in 2019. It is designed for a very large capacity.
63026.m: Since 2019 Turkish Airlines has flown from the new Istanbul Airport.

63027.q: Which airline uses Hamad International Airport in Doha as its hub?
63027.e: Qatar Airways connects Europe, Asia, Africa and Oceania via Doha. Emirates flies via Dubai, Etihad via Abu Dhabi.
63027.m: Doha is the hub of Qatar Airways.

63028.q: At hubs, what is the bundling of many arrivals and departures into short time windows called?
63028.e: First many flights land shortly after one another, then many flights take off. This gives transferring passengers short waiting times and many connections.
63028.m: Waves of arrivals and departures make changing planes easier.

63029.q: What does the voyage of the converted tanker Ideal X from Newark to Houston in 1956 stand for?
a: The beginning of modern container shipping
The first passage through the Panama Canal
The first transport of oil by pipeline
63029.e: The Ideal X carried 58 containers on deck. The voyage in April 1956 is considered the beginning of modern container shipping.
63029.m: Container shipping began with the Ideal X in 1956.

63030.q: How long is a standard container that equals two TEU?
63030.e: One TEU equals a 20-foot container. A 40-foot container is twice as long and therefore counts as two TEU.

63031.q: Roughly how many TEU do the largest container ships in the world hold (as of 2024)?
63031.e: The Irina-class ships of the MSC shipping line hold 24,346 TEU. They are about 400 m long.
63031.m: The largest container ships carry more than 24,000 standard containers.

63032.q: What is the locking device at the corners called that connects containers to each other and to the ship?
63032.e: The twistlock is inserted into the standard corner fittings and turned. The spreader, on the other hand, is the gripping frame on the crane.
63032.m: Twistlocks hold stacked containers firmly together.

63033.q: In freight transport, what is meant by intermodal transport?
a: Changing the means of transport without unloading the goods
63033.e: The container is moved as a whole from the ship to a train or lorry. The goods themselves stay in the container.
63033.m: In intermodal transport the means of transport changes, not the load.

63034.q: What are containers with built-in cooling, for example for bananas, called?
63034.e: Reefer containers have a cooling unit and are supplied with electricity on board. This means perishable goods can be transported for weeks.
63034.m: In shipping, refrigerated containers are called reefers.

63035.q: Which English port rose to become Britain's largest container port thanks to early container terminals, while the London docks fell into decline?
63035.e: Container terminals need deep water and a lot of space, which the old city ports lacked. Felixstowe seized this opportunity early.
63035.m: Containers moved ports out of the cities to large terminals.

63036.q: What share of intercontinental data traffic runs through undersea cables?
63036.e: Satellites carry only a tiny fraction, because fibre-optic cables carry much more data with shorter delay. The internet between continents therefore depends almost entirely on undersea cables.
63036.m: Almost all data traffic between continents runs through cables in the sea.

63037.q: How long did the first transatlantic telegraph cable of 1858 work?
63037.e: The cable was in operation from August 1858 but failed after about a month. Too high a voltage had damaged the insulation.
63037.m: The first Atlantic cable only lasted a few weeks.

63038.q: Which steamship laid the first permanently working transatlantic cable in 1866?
63038.e: The Great Eastern was the largest ship in the world at the time and could carry the whole cable. It later also laid cables to India.
63038.m: The Great Eastern linked Europe and America by cable.

63039.q: How have modern undersea cables transmitted their data since the late 1980s?
a: As light signals in glass fibres
As radio waves in the water
As sound waves in a pipe
63039.e: In 1988 TAT-8, the first transatlantic fibre-optic cable, went into operation. Light in glass fibres carries much more data than electrical signals in copper.
63039.m: Undersea cables now transmit data as light.

63040.q: What is the most common cause of damage to undersea cables?
63040.e: Most damage is caused accidentally by bottom trawl nets and anchors in shallow coastal waters. That is why cables there are often buried in the seabed.
63040.m: Fishing and anchors damage most undersea cables.

63041.q: Roughly how thick is a modern fibre-optic undersea cable in the deep sea?
63041.e: In the deep sea the cable needs little protection and is about as thick as a garden hose. Near the coast it is additionally armoured with steel wires and thicker.
63041.m: A deep-sea cable is hardly thicker than a garden hose.

63042.q: Which island nation in the Pacific was almost cut off from the internet for weeks after a volcanic eruption in January 2022?
63042.e: The eruption of Hunga Tonga-Hunga Ha'apai tore the country's only international undersea cable. The repair took several weeks.
63042.m: Countries with only one undersea cable are especially vulnerable.

63043.q: What is the section of the Northeast Passage called that Russia manages as its own shipping route?
63043.e: The Northern Sea Route stretches roughly from the Kara Sea to the Bering Strait. Russia regulates permits and icebreaker escorts there.
63043.m: Russia calls its Arctic route the Northern Sea Route.

63044.q: Which port is free of ice all year thanks to offshoots of the Gulf Stream and is considered the western starting point of the Northeast Passage?
63044.e: Murmansk lies on the Kola Peninsula on the Barents Sea. Warm Atlantic water keeps the port free of ice despite its position north of the Arctic Circle.
63044.m: Murmansk stays free of ice thanks to warm Atlantic water.

63045.q: What did a Soviet icebreaker achieve for the first time on the Northeast Passage in 1932?
a: The passage in a single season
The first passage with nuclear power
The first passage in the middle of winter
The first passage with passengers on a cruise
63045.e: In 1932 the icebreaker Sibiryakov sailed from Arkhangelsk to the Bering Strait without spending the winter in the ice. After that the Soviet Union systematically developed the Northern Sea Route.
63045.m: In 1932 the Sibiryakov proved that the passage was possible in one summer.

63046.q: Why did early ships on the Northeast Passage often have to spend the winter in the ice?
a: The ice-free period in summer was too short for the whole route
The ports were closed to foreigners in summer
There was constant darkness in the Arctic in summer
Ships were only allowed to sail in winter
63046.e: The sea ice only freed the route for a few weeks a year. Some ships were even crushed, such as the Chelyuskin in 1934, whose crew was flown out from an ice camp.
63046.m: The short ice-free window made the Northeast Passage dangerous.

63047.q: Which marginal sea does the Northeast Passage cross east of the Taymyr Peninsula?
63047.e: From the west come the Barents Sea, Kara Sea, Laptev Sea, East Siberian Sea and Chukchi Sea. The Laptev Sea lies between Taymyr and the New Siberian Islands.
63047.m: East of Taymyr lies the Laptev Sea.

63048.q: What especially limits the size of ships on the Northern Sea Route?
a: The shallow water of some straits
Strong tides of up to 15 m
An international ban on large ships
63048.e: Some straits off the Siberian coast are in places only about 10 to 20 m deep. Very large container ships and tankers draw too much water there.
63048.m: Shallow straits limit ship size in the Arctic.

63049.q: How did the Franklin expedition, which searched for the Northwest Passage from 1845, end?
a: The ships froze in, and all the men died
The crew reached Asia and stayed there
The crew mutinied and settled in Greenland
The ships returned undamaged after a year
63049.e: The Erebus and the Terror froze in off King William Island in 1846. All 129 men died, and the wrecks were only found in 2014 and 2016.
63049.m: The wrecks of the Franklin expedition were only found in the 21st century.

63050.q: Which Norwegian was the first to sail through the entire Northwest Passage by ship, from 1903 to 1906?
63050.e: Amundsen sailed through the Canadian archipelago in the small ship Gjøa. Robert McClure had already made the passage from 1850 to 1854, but partly on foot over the ice.
63050.m: Amundsen was the first to sail the whole Northwest Passage by ship.

63051.q: Which country regards the waterways of the Northwest Passage as its own internal waters?
63051.e: Canada sees the straits between its Arctic islands as internal waters. The USA, on the other hand, considers them an international strait. The voyages of the St. Roch from 1940 already underlined Canada's claim.
63051.m: Canada claims the Northwest Passage as its own waters.

63052.q: Why is oil from northern Alaska transported by pipeline rather than by tanker through the Northwest Passage?
a: The ice makes the sea route too unsafe and too expensive
The Northwest Passage was still unknown at the time
Oil may not be shipped internationally
The passage is too short for ships
63052.e: In 1969 the ice-strengthened tanker Manhattan tested the route but only got through with the help of icebreakers. After that the Trans-Alaska Pipeline was built.
63052.m: The Manhattan test showed the limits of the Arctic route.

63053.q: Through which area does the Northwest Passage mainly run?
a: Through the islands of northern Canada
Along the northern coast of Siberia
Right across the interior of Greenland
Through the Baltic Sea and the White Sea
63053.e: The routes run from Baffin Bay westwards through the Canadian Arctic Archipelago to the Beaufort Sea north of Alaska.
63053.m: The Northwest Passage runs through the islands of northern Canada.

63054.q: Into which sea does the Northwest Passage open at its western end, north of Alaska?
63054.e: The Beaufort Sea lies north of Alaska and the Canadian Yukon. From there the route leads through the Bering Strait into the Pacific.
63054.m: In the west the Northwest Passage ends in the Beaufort Sea.

63055.q: What is the technical English term for a strait or canal through which a large part of world trade has to pass?
63055.e: A chokepoint is a bottleneck that is difficult to avoid. A disruption there can interrupt supply chains worldwide.
63055.m: Chokepoints are the bottlenecks of world trade.

63056.q: Why did the Panama Canal have to limit the number of daily passages in 2023?
a: A drought lowered the water level of Gatún Lake
A strike brought operations to a standstill
A shipping accident blocked the entrance
63056.e: The locks are operated with fresh water from Gatún Lake. Because of the drought there was not enough water, so draught and passages were restricted.
63056.m: The Panama Canal needs a lot of rainwater for its locks.

63057.q: Which treaty signed in Switzerland has regulated passage through the Bosporus and Dardanelles since 1936?
63057.e: The Montreux Convention guarantees merchant ships free passage and gives Turkey control over the straits. Restrictions apply to warships.
63057.m: The straits at the Bosporus are governed by a treaty from Montreux.

63058.q: Roughly what share of the oil consumed worldwide passes through the Strait of Hormuz?
63058.e: According to the US Energy Information Administration (EIA), about a fifth of world oil consumption flows through the strait. There are only a few pipelines that bypass it.
63058.m: About a fifth of the world's oil flows through the Strait of Hormuz.

63059.q: Through which straits must ships pass between the Baltic Sea and the North Sea if they do not use the Kiel Canal?
63059.e: The Øresund and the Great and Little Belts connect the Baltic Sea with the Kattegat. They are the most important access to the Russian and Baltic ports on the Baltic Sea.
63059.m: The Baltic Sea is connected to the oceans via the Danish straits.

63060.q: Roughly how wide is the Strait of Gibraltar at its narrowest point?
63060.e: At the narrowest point only about 14 km separate Spain and Morocco. All shipping between the Mediterranean and the Atlantic passes through the strait.
63060.m: At Gibraltar, Africa and Europe are only 14 km apart.

63061.q: Which country captured the city of Malacca from the Portuguese in 1641?
63061.e: The Dutch East India Company took Malacca in 1641 after a long siege. This gave it control of the important sea route to the Spice Islands.
63061.m: In Malacca the Dutch took over from the Portuguese.

63062.q: What consequence does the 1824 treaty between Britain and the Netherlands still have today?
a: It shapes the border between Malaysia and Indonesia along the strait
It made Singapore part of Indonesia
It opened the Suez Canal to all ships
63062.e: Britain received the Malay Peninsula with Malacca, the Netherlands received Sumatra. This division still shapes the border between Malaysia and Indonesia today.
63062.m: A treaty of 1824 made the strait the border between two colonial empires.

63063.q: Which strait between Sumatra and Java is a possible alternative route to the Strait of Malacca?
63063.e: The Sunda Strait connects the Indian Ocean with the Java Sea. Because of currents and shallow depth, it is less suitable for large ships.
63063.m: The Sunda Strait lies between Sumatra and Java.

63064.q: Which sea does the Strait of Malacca connect to in the north-west?
63064.e: The Andaman Sea is a marginal sea of the Indian Ocean west of Thailand and Myanmar. From there the routes continue to India and Europe.
63064.m: In the north-west the Strait of Malacca opens into the Andaman Sea.

63065.q: Through which strait does the sea route continue into the South China Sea at the southern end of the Strait of Malacca?
63065.e: The Singapore Strait lies between Singapore and the Indonesian Riau Islands. It is the bottleneck where traffic turns towards East Asia.
63065.m: At the southern end the route passes through the Singapore Strait.

63066.q: Which three bordering states began coordinated naval patrols in the Strait of Malacca in 2004?
63066.e: The three states border the strait directly and wanted to act together against attacks. Thailand joined later.
63066.m: The bordering states protect the strait together.

63067.q: Why was Malacca an ideal trading place in the 15th century?
a: Traders waited there for the monsoon winds to change
It had the only gold mines in Asia
The city lay at the mouth of the Mekong
The overland Silk Road started there
63067.e: Sailing ships from India and China depended on the seasonally changing monsoons. In Malacca, traders from both directions met and exchanged their goods.
63067.m: The monsoon winds set the rhythm of trade in Malacca.

63068.q: What does the name of the Druzhba pipeline, which carries Russian oil to Central Europe, mean?
63068.e: “Druzhba” is Russian for friendship. The pipeline was built in the 1960s and supplied the Eastern Bloc states of the time.

63069.q: To which port does the Trans-Alaska Pipeline run from the oil fields at Prudhoe Bay?
63069.e: The pipeline is about 1,300 km long and ends at the ice-free port of Valdez. There the oil is loaded onto tankers.
63069.m: Oil from northern Alaska flows to Valdez.

63070.q: What happened to the Nord Stream pipelines in the Baltic Sea in September 2022?
63070.e: Underwater explosions damaged three of the four lines of Nord Stream 1 and 2. Large amounts of gas escaped.
63070.m: The Nord Stream pipelines were destroyed by explosions in 2022.

63071.q: Over which pass does the Transitgas pipeline leave Switzerland towards Italy?
63071.e: The pipeline starts at Wallbach on the High Rhine and crosses the Alps in tunnels. Near the Gries Pass it is connected to the Italian network.
63071.m: Transitgas flows to Italy over the Gries Pass.

63072.q: What does the reverse-flow conversion of the Transitgas pipeline, completed in 2017, make possible?
a: Gas can also flow from south to north
The pipeline now also carries oil
Gas is extracted directly in Switzerland
63072.e: Before, gas only flowed from northern Europe to Italy. Now it can also flow north from Italy, which improves security of supply.
63072.m: The Transitgas pipeline now works in both directions.

63073.q: From which country has the Trans Adriatic Pipeline brought natural gas to Italy since 2020?
63073.e: TAP is part of the Southern Gas Corridor from the Caspian Sea via Turkey, Greece and Albania to Apulia. It is meant to reduce dependence on individual suppliers.
63073.m: Gas from the Caspian Sea reaches Italy through TAP.

63074.q: To which country does the “Power of Siberia” pipeline, opened in 2019, deliver natural gas?
63074.e: The pipeline brings gas from eastern Siberia to north-east China. For Russia it is an alternative to the markets in Europe.
63074.m: The “Power of Siberia” pipeline links Russia with China.

63075.q: How long is the Gotthard Base Tunnel?
63075.e: At 57 km it is the longest railway tunnel in the world. It runs from Erstfeld to Bodio.
63075.m: The Gotthard Base Tunnel is 57 kilometres long.

63076.q: Which base tunnel completed the flat railway through the Alps on the Gotthard axis in 2020?
63076.e: The Ceneri Base Tunnel in Ticino is about 15 km long. With it, the line between Uri and Lugano is flat all the way.
63076.m: With the Ceneri, the Gotthard axis has been a flat railway since 2020.

63077.q: Roughly how high is the highest point of the Gotthard Base Tunnel?
63077.e: The summit point is only about 550 m above sea level, hardly higher than the Swiss Plateau. That is why heavy goods trains can run without extra locomotives.
63077.m: The base tunnel turns the Gotthard into a flat railway.

63078.q: Which popular initiative, accepted in 1994, demands that goods traffic crossing the Alps be moved onto the railway?
63078.e: The Alpine Initiative was accepted by the people and the cantons in 1994. The task of shifting traffic has been in the Federal Constitution ever since.
63078.m: Switzerland wants to move transit goods traffic onto the railway.

63079.q: Why is a second bore of the road tunnel being built at the Gotthard?
a: So the old tunnel can be renovated without a full closure
So that twice as many lanes can be used
So that goods trains can use the tunnel
To take pressure off the railway tunnel
63079.e: The road tunnel from 1980 needs a complete renovation. Afterwards each bore is to have only one lane, because by law the capacity must not increase.
63079.m: The second Gotthard bore is for renovation, not expansion.

63080.q: Which two countries does the Brenner Base Tunnel connect?
63080.e: The tunnel runs from Innsbruck to Fortezza in South Tyrol. It passes under the Brenner Pass at the border.
63080.m: The Brenner Base Tunnel connects Tyrol with South Tyrol.

63081.q: Roughly how high is the Brenner Pass?
63081.e: At about 1,370 m, the Brenner is one of the lowest crossings of the Alps. That is why a railway and a motorway already cross the pass today.
63081.m: The Brenner is a comparatively low Alpine pass.

63082.q: Which tunnel will the Brenner Base Tunnel, together with the Innsbruck bypass, overtake as the world's longest underground railway link?
63082.e: The main tunnel is 55 km long; with the existing Innsbruck bypass, the underground route is over 60 km. That is more than the 57 km at the Gotthard.
63082.m: With the Innsbruck bypass, the Brenner will be longer than the Gotthard.

63083.q: When is the Brenner Base Tunnel expected to open according to current plans (as of 2025)?
63083.e: An earlier opening was originally planned, but geological difficulties delayed construction. Today an opening around 2032 is expected.
63083.m: The Brenner Base Tunnel is due to be finished in the early 2030s.

63084.q: What is the exploratory tunnel below the two main tubes of the Brenner Base Tunnel for?
a: To explore the rock and later for drainage
As a third lane for lorries
63084.e: The tunnel lies a few metres below the main tubes. During construction it shows the geology, and later it drains water away.
63084.m: An exploratory tunnel makes tunnel building safer.

63085.q: Which oasis city in the far west of China was a hub where the routes north and south of the Taklamakan met again?
63085.e: Kashgar lies on the western edge of the Tarim Basin, in front of the Pamirs. From here the routes continued to Samarkand, India and Persia.
63085.m: Kashgar was China's western gateway on the Silk Road.

63087.q: Which railway line in the Balkans is being upgraded with Chinese funding as part of the New Silk Road?
63087.e: The line is meant to bring goods from the port of Piraeus to Central Europe faster. The Serbian section between Belgrade and Novi Sad has been running since 2022.
63087.m: China wants to link Piraeus with Central Europe via the Balkans.

63088.q: How are trains on the Trans-Siberian Railway powered along the whole line today?
63088.e: Electrification began in 1929 and was only completed in December 2002. Since then trains can run electrically all the way from Moscow to Vladivostok.
63088.m: The Trans-Siberian has only been fully electrified since 2002.

63089.q: Through which region did a shortcut of the Trans-Siberian to Vladivostok run from 1903?
63089.e: The Chinese Eastern Railway through Manchuria was much shorter than the route along the Amur. It was built and run by Russia.
63089.m: The Chinese Eastern Railway cut the route to Vladivostok short through Manchuria.

63090.q: Which Russian state corporation has been responsible for the infrastructure of the Northern Sea Route since 2019?
63090.e: Rosatom operates Russia's fleet of nuclear-powered icebreakers. That is why it was also given responsibility for the route's infrastructure.
63090.m: The nuclear agency Rosatom manages Russia's Arctic route.

63091.q: Why have even large cruise ships been able to sail through the Northwest Passage in recent years?
a: The sea ice shrinks a lot in summer
Canada has dug a canal through the islands
Cruise ships now have nuclear propulsion
The passage is artificially heated in summer
63091.e: Because the Arctic is warming, the summer ice has decreased sharply. In 2016 the Crystal Serenity became the first large cruise ship to sail through the passage, escorted by an icebreaker.
63091.m: Melting ice makes the Northwest Passage possible even for cruises.

63092.q: What does the “Minimum Connecting Time” at a hub airport state?
a: The shortest allowed transfer time between two flights
The longest allowed waiting time at the gate
The time between a plane's landing and take-off
How long the security check takes
63092.e: The airport and airlines decide how much time a transfer needs at least, including moving the luggage. Shorter connections may not be sold as a connection.
63092.m: A short minimum connecting time makes a hub attractive.

63093.q: What is the facility on the coast called where a submarine cable is connected to the network on land?
63093.e: In the cable landing station the optical fibres and the power supply for the repeaters end. From there the data run into the land network.
63093.m: Submarine cables come ashore at cable landing stations.

63094.q: What is the device called that is sent through pipelines to clean and inspect them?
63094.e: The pig is pushed through the pipeline by the flow of liquid or gas. Intelligent pigs measure wall thickness and damage as they go.
63094.m: A pig cleans and inspects pipelines from the inside.

63095.q: In the Christmas story, what does the angel call the newborn child?
63095.e: The angel says that the Saviour has been born. Older Bibles in German use the word Heiland for this.
63095.m: The angel calls the child the Saviour.

63096.q: According to the Bible, where did Mary lay the newborn baby Jesus?
63096.e: The Gospel of Luke says that Mary laid the child in a manger. A manger is a feeding trough for animals.
63096.m: Baby Jesus lay in a manger.

63097.q: Why did Mary and Joseph travel to Bethlehem?
63097.e: Everyone was to be counted and had to register in the town of their ancestors. That is why Mary and Joseph had to go to Bethlehem.
63097.m: Mary and Joseph went to Bethlehem because of a census.

63098.q: According to the Bible, which Roman emperor ordered the census?
63098.e: The Gospel of Luke says that Emperor Augustus ordered everyone in his empire to be counted.
63098.m: According to the Bible, Emperor Augustus ordered the census.

63099.q: Why could Mary and Joseph not find a room in Bethlehem?
63099.e: The Bible says that there was no room for them at the inn. That is why the child was born among the animals.
63099.m: There was no room at the inn for Mary and Joseph.

63100.q: What does the name “Bethlehem” mean in English?
63100.e: Bethlehem comes from Hebrew and means “house of bread”. The town is south of Jerusalem.

63101.q: Which Gospel writer tells of the shepherds in the field?
63101.e: The story of the shepherds is in the second chapter of this Gospel. It also says there that Mary laid the child in a manger.
63101.m: Luke tells the story of the shepherds.

63102.q: According to the Bible, in which town was Jesus born?
63102.e: Mary and Joseph had to travel to Bethlehem. There Jesus was born in a stable.

63103.q: What is the name of the mother of Jesus?
63103.e: The Bible calls the mother of Jesus Mary. She is one of the most important women in Christianity.
63103.m: The mother of Jesus is called Mary.

63104.q: In which place did Mary live before she travelled to Bethlehem?
63104.e: According to the Gospel of Luke, Mary lived in Nazareth in Galilee. That is why Jesus is later also called Jesus of Nazareth.

63105.q: In many pictures, on which animal does Mary ride to Bethlehem?
63105.e: The Bible does not name an animal, but in many pictures and nativity plays Mary rides a donkey. Donkeys were common pack animals at that time.
63105.m: In many pictures Mary rides a donkey.

63106.q: Which relative did Mary visit before Jesus was born?
63106.e: The Gospel of Luke tells that Mary visited her relative. This woman was also soon expecting a child.

63107.q: Which feast of Mary falls during Advent?
63107.e: The Immaculate Conception is celebrated on 8 December. In some Catholic cantons of Switzerland it is a public holiday.
63107.m: The Immaculate Conception is celebrated in Advent on 8 December.

63108.q: What is the name of Mary’s husband?
63108.e: Mary was engaged to Joseph and became his wife. Joseph looked after Mary and baby Jesus.

63109.q: What are Mary, Joseph and Jesus called together?
63109.e: Mary, Joseph and baby Jesus are called the Holy Family. You can see them together in many nativity scenes.
63109.m: Mary, Joseph and Jesus are called the Holy Family.

63110.q: According to the Bible, which king’s family did Joseph come from?
63110.e: The Bible says that Joseph was a descendant of King David. That is why he had to go to Bethlehem for the census.
63110.m: Joseph came from the family of King David.

63111.q: In the Bible, how did Joseph receive a message from an angel?
63111.e: In the Gospel of Matthew, an angel appears to Joseph in a dream. The angel tells him to take Mary as his wife.
63111.m: Joseph received the angel’s message in a dream.

63112.q: To which country did Joseph flee with Mary and Jesus?
63112.e: Joseph was warned in a dream that King Herod wanted to harm the child. That is why the family fled to Egypt.
63112.m: Joseph fled to Egypt with Mary and Jesus.

63113.q: Where did Joseph move with his family after their time in Egypt?
63113.e: After King Herod died, the family returned. They settled in Nazareth in Galilee, where Jesus grew up.
63113.m: Jesus grew up with Joseph in Nazareth.

63114.q: Which angel brought Mary the message about Jesus?
63114.e: In the Gospel of Luke, God sends this angel to Mary. He is seen as God’s messenger.
63114.m: The angel Gabriel came to Mary.

63115.q: What did the angel Gabriel say to Mary?
a: She would be the mother of Jesus
63115.e: Gabriel told Mary that she would have a son. This child would be the Son of God.
63115.m: Gabriel told Mary that she would be the mother of Jesus.

63116.q: According to the angel’s words, what name was the child to be given?
63116.e: The angel told Mary to call her son Jesus. The name means “God saves”.
63116.m: The angel said the child should be called Jesus.

63117.q: On which day is the angel’s visit to Mary celebrated?
63117.e: The feast of the Annunciation is on 25 March. That is exactly nine months before Christmas.
63117.m: The Annunciation is celebrated on 25 March.

63118.q: Apart from the birth of Jesus, whose birth did Gabriel also announce?
63118.e: Gabriel also appeared to the priest Zechariah. He told him that his son John would be born.
63118.m: Gabriel also announced the birth of John the Baptist.

63119.q: Gabriel is called an archangel. What does that mean?
a: He is a particularly important angel
63119.e: An archangel is an angel of high rank. Besides Gabriel, Michael and Raphael are examples.
63119.m: An archangel is a particularly important angel.

63120.q: Which other religion also includes the angel Gabriel?
63120.e: Gabriel appears in Judaism, Christianity and Islam. In Islam he is called Jibril.
63120.m: Gabriel is also an important angel in Islam.

63121.q: According to the Bible, who were the first to hear about the birth of Jesus?
63121.e: The Bible tells how an angel appeared to simple shepherds. They were the first to hear the good news.
63121.m: The shepherds were the first to hear about the birth of Jesus.

63122.q: Which animals do the shepherds of Bethlehem look after in many pictures and nativity scenes?
63122.e: The Bible only speaks of a flock. In pictures and nativity scenes they are almost always sheep.
63122.m: The shepherds in the nativity scene usually look after sheep.

63123.q: At what time of day did the angel come to the shepherds?
63123.e: The Bible tells how the shepherds were watching their flock at night. Then the angel appeared to them in bright light.
63123.m: The angel came to the shepherds at night.

63124.q: How did the shepherds feel when the angel suddenly appeared?
63124.e: The Bible says the shepherds were very afraid. That is why the angel first said “Fear not”.
63124.m: At first the shepherds were afraid of the angel.

63125.q: What did the many angels sing to the shepherds?
a: Glory to God in the highest
63125.e: After the first angel, a great crowd of angels joined in. They praised God with the words “Glory to God in the highest”.
63125.m: The angels sang “Glory to God in the highest”.

63126.q: What did the shepherds do after they had seen the child?
63126.e: The shepherds told everyone what they had heard about the child. People were amazed at their words.
63126.m: The shepherds told everyone about the child.

63127.q: How many angels appeared to the shepherds at first?
63127.e: First a single angel came with the message. Only after that did a great crowd of angels appear.
63127.m: At first a single angel appeared to the shepherds.

63128.q: What sign does the angel give the shepherds so they will recognise the child?
63128.e: The angel said they would find a baby wrapped in cloths. That way they could recognise the right child.
63128.m: The sign for the shepherds was a baby wrapped in cloths.

63129.q: In which Gospel is the story of the star found?
63129.e: Only the Gospel of Matthew tells of the star that showed the way to the child.
63129.m: The story of the star is in Matthew.

63130.q: According to the Bible, where did the star stop?
a: Over the place where the child was
63130.e: The star went ahead of the visitors and stopped over the place where the child was. That is how they found Jesus.
63130.m: The star stopped over the place where the child was.

63131.q: How is the Star of Bethlehem often painted?
63131.e: Many painters show the star like a comet with a glowing tail. That is why you often see it like this in nativity scenes.
63131.m: The Star of Bethlehem is often painted with a tail.

63132.q: What do some researchers think was behind the Star of Bethlehem?
63132.e: Some researchers think of Jupiter and Saturn, which appeared close together in the sky at that time. Nobody knows for sure.
63132.m: Some researchers think the star was two planets close together.

63133.q: Which city did the wise men go to first, before the star led them to Bethlehem?
63133.e: The wise men first looked for the new king in the capital, Jerusalem. From there the star went ahead of them to Bethlehem.
63133.m: The wise men came to Jerusalem first.

63134.q: What is often put on top of the Christmas tree?
63134.e: The star on top of the tree is a reminder of the Star of Bethlehem. Some people use a glass tree topper instead.
63134.m: There is often a star on top of the Christmas tree.

63135.q: How did the visitors feel when they saw the star again?
63135.e: The Bible says they were filled with great joy. The star showed them the way again.
63135.m: The visitors were overjoyed to see the star.

63136.q: What did the star do for the visitors from far away?
a: It gave them light to read by
It woke them in the morning
63136.e: The visitors followed the star on their long journey. That is how they found the child.
63136.m: The star showed the visitors the way to the child.

63137.q: What did the wise men do when they had found the child?
63137.e: The Bible tells how they bowed down before the child and honoured him. Then they gave him their gifts.
63137.m: The wise men knelt before the child.

63138.q: Why did the wise men not go back to King Herod?
63138.e: The wise men were warned in a dream not to return to Herod. So they travelled home by another route.
63138.m: A dream warned the wise men about Herod.

63139.q: On which day is Three Kings' Day celebrated?
63139.e: On 6 January people remember the visit of the wise men to the baby Jesus. The feast is also called Epiphany.
63139.m: Three Kings' Day is on 6 January.

63140.q: Why do people speak of three kings?
a: Because they travelled for three days
63140.e: The Bible does not say how many there were. Because three gifts are mentioned, people imagined three visitors.
63140.m: People speak of three kings because of the three gifts.

63141.q: According to the Bible, from which direction did the wise men come?
63141.e: The Gospel of Matthew says that wise men came from the East.
63141.m: The wise men came from the east.

63142.q: What do carol singers at Epiphany write on the front door in chalk?
63142.e: The letters stand for “Christus mansionem benedicat”, meaning “May Christ bless this house”. They are often also read as the names of the kings.
63142.m: Epiphany carol singers write C+M+B and the year on the door.

a: A resin that smells nice when burnt
63143.e: Frankincense is the dried resin of a tree. When burnt it gives off a fine scent and is used in churches.

63144.q: Which animals do the Three Kings ride in many pictures?
63144.e: The wise men came from far away through dry lands. That is why they are often shown on camels, which can go a long time without water.
63144.m: In pictures the Three Kings often ride camels.

63145.q: What is hidden in the Three Kings cake?
63145.e: One of the pieces of cake has a small figure inside, usually made of plastic. Everyone hopes to find it.
63145.m: A small king figure is hidden in the Three Kings cake.

63146.q: What does the person who finds the figure in the Three Kings cake become?
a: King or queen for a day
63146.e: Whoever gets the piece with the figure may be king or queen for a day. They are often allowed to decide things.
63146.m: Whoever finds the figure is king for a day.

63147.q: What often comes with a Three Kings cake?
63147.e: A paper crown usually comes with the cake. It is for the king or queen of the day.
63147.m: A paper crown comes with the Three Kings cake.

63148.q: What kind of dough is the Swiss Three Kings cake made from?
63148.e: The Swiss Three Kings cake is baked from sweet yeast dough. That is why it is soft like a plaited loaf.
63148.m: The Swiss Three Kings cake is made of sweet yeast dough.

63149.q: What does the Swiss Three Kings cake look like?
63149.e: Several small balls lie around one large ball in the middle. Together they look like a flower.
63149.m: The Three Kings cake is made of balls arranged like a flower.

63150.q: What is often sprinkled on the Three Kings cake?
63150.e: Pearl sugar and flaked almonds often go on top of the cake. That makes it crunchy and sweet.
63150.m: There is often pearl sugar on the Three Kings cake.

63151.q: On which day is the Three Kings cake traditionally eaten in Switzerland?
63151.e: 6 January is Three Kings' Day. Whoever finds the little king figure in the cake may be king for a day.
63151.m: The Three Kings cake is eaten on 6 January.

63152.q: What is the cake for Three Kings' Day called in France?
63152.e: In France people eat the Galette des Rois, meaning “cake of the kings”. In the north it is often made of puff pastry.
63152.m: In France the cake is called Galette des Rois.

63153.q: Which two animals usually stand by the child in a nativity scene?
63153.e: The ox and the donkey have been part of almost every nativity scene for a very long time. They stand by the child in the stable.
63153.m: The ox and the donkey usually stand in the nativity scene.

63154.q: Who set up one of the first nativity scenes with real animals in 1223?
63154.e: Francis of Assisi celebrated Christmas in Greccio in Italy with a manger, an ox and a donkey. He wanted to bring the story to life.
63154.m: Francis of Assisi set up one of the first nativity scenes.

63155.q: What is the play called in which children act out the Christmas story?
63155.e: In a nativity play, children play Mary, Joseph, the shepherds and the angels. It is often performed in church.
63155.m: In a nativity play children act out the Christmas story.

63156.q: When do many families put the baby Jesus in their nativity scene?
a: On the first Sunday of Advent
63156.e: Many set up the nativity scene in Advent but leave the manger empty. The baby Jesus is only added on Christmas Eve.
63156.m: The baby Jesus goes into the nativity scene on Christmas Eve.

63157.q: What is a nativity scene with real people and animals called?
63157.e: In a living nativity, people play Mary, Joseph and the shepherds. Often real sheep or donkeys take part too.
63157.m: A nativity scene with real people is called a living nativity.

63158.q: What material are nativity figures most often made of?
63158.e: Many nativity figures are carved from wood. But there are also figures made of clay or fabric.
63158.m: Nativity figures are often carved from wood.

63159.q: In which building do the figures of a nativity scene usually stand?
63159.e: The nativity scene usually shows a simple stable with a roof. Inside are animals, straw and the child.
63159.m: The figures of a nativity scene usually stand in a stable.

63160.q: How many doors does an Advent calendar usually have?
63160.e: You open one door every day from 1 to 24 December. That makes 24 doors.
63160.m: An Advent calendar usually has 24 doors.

63161.q: What did families in the past draw on the door or wall as a simple Advent calendar?
63161.e: For each day until Christmas Eve, a line was drawn in chalk. The children were allowed to wipe away one line each day.
63161.m: In the past, people counted the days until Christmas with chalk lines.

63162.q: What is often behind the doors of an Advent calendar?
63162.e: Many shop-bought Advent calendars have a piece of chocolate behind each door. Others have pictures or small presents.
63162.m: There is often chocolate behind the doors.

63163.q: What is an Advent calendar for?
a: To count the days until Christmas
To count the days of the holidays
63163.e: With an Advent calendar you can see every day how long it is until Christmas. It makes the waiting feel shorter.
63163.m: An Advent calendar counts the days until Christmas.

63164.q: What is an Advent window in many Swiss villages?
a: Each day a decorated window is lit up
A window in the town hall
63164.e: Families each decorate a window that lights up for the first time on a certain day in December. This makes an Advent calendar for the whole village.
63164.m: With Advent windows, a new decorated window lights up every day.

63165.q: Which country does the Advent calendar come from?
63165.e: The first Advent calendars appeared in Germany in the 19th century. Later, printed calendars became popular.
63165.m: The Advent calendar comes from Germany.

63166.e: The word comes from Latin and means arrival. During Advent, Christians wait for the arrival of Jesus.

63167.q: How many Sundays of Advent are there before Christmas?
63167.e: Advent has four Sundays. The first Sunday of Advent is at the end of November or the beginning of December.
63167.m: There are four Sundays of Advent before Christmas.

63168.q: What kind of branches is an Advent wreath usually made from?
63168.e: An Advent wreath is usually made from green fir branches. Green is a sign of hope and life.
63168.m: The Advent wreath is usually made of fir branches.

63169.q: What do you do at the Advent wreath on each Sunday of Advent?
63169.e: Each Sunday of Advent one more candle is lit. That shows Christmas is getting closer and closer.
63169.m: On each Sunday of Advent you light one more candle.

63170.q: Which tree is often used as a Christmas tree?
63170.e: A fir or spruce is usually used as a Christmas tree. These trees stay green in winter too.
63170.m: A fir is often used as a Christmas tree.

63171.q: Why is an evergreen tree a good symbol for Christmas?
a: It stands for life in winter
63171.e: When other trees are bare, the fir stays green. That is why it is seen as a sign of life and hope.
63171.m: The green Christmas tree is a sign of life in winter.

63172.q: What was used to light the Christmas tree in the past?
63172.e: In the past, real wax candles were put on the branches. Today many people use electric fairy lights because they are safer.
63172.m: In the past, wax candles lit the Christmas tree.

63173.q: What are classic Christmas baubles made of?
63173.e: Classic Christmas baubles are blown from thin glass. Today there are also plastic baubles.
63173.m: Classic Christmas baubles are made of glass.

63174.q: What are the glittery silver strands on the Christmas tree called?
63174.e: Tinsel is made of thin, shiny strips. It is hung over the branches to make the tree glitter.
63174.m: The glittery strands on the Christmas tree are called tinsel.

63175.q: When do many families decorate the Christmas tree?
63175.e: Many families only fetch and decorate the tree shortly before Christmas. Some even decorate it on 24 December.
63175.m: The Christmas tree is often decorated shortly before Christmas Eve.

63176.q: Which stars made of natural material are often hung on the Christmas tree?
63176.e: Straw stars are made from drinking straws of real straw. They are a reminder of the straw in the stable in Bethlehem.
63176.m: Straw stars are a popular Christmas tree decoration.

63177.q: What often lies under the Christmas tree on Christmas Eve?
63177.e: Many families put the presents under the tree. After the celebration they are unwrapped.
63177.m: The presents often lie under the Christmas tree.

63178.q: When do people sing “Silent Night, Holy Night”?
63178.e: “Silent Night, Holy Night” is a Christmas carol. It tells of the night Jesus was born.

63180.q: Who composed the tune of “Silent Night, Holy Night”?
63180.e: The tune was written by the teacher and organist Franz Xaver Gruber. The words were written by the priest Joseph Mohr.
63180.m: Franz Xaver Gruber composed the tune of “Silent Night”.

63181.q: Which instrument accompanied “Silent Night” the first time it was sung?
63181.e: The first time it was sung, the accompaniment was played on a guitar. Only later was the carol also played on the organ.
63181.m: “Silent Night” was first accompanied on the guitar.

63183.q: What rings in the Christmas song “Jingle Bells”?
63183.e: In the song, little bells jingle on a sleigh.

63187.q: In the German carol “Kling, Glöckchen, klingelingeling”, who wants to come into the house?
63187.e: In the song, the Christ Child asks the children to open the door. It is cold outside.
63187.m: In “Kling, Glöckchen” the Christ Child wants to come into the house.

63188.q: What is the date of Christmas Eve?
63188.e: Christmas Eve is the evening before Christmas Day. Many families celebrate together then and unwrap presents.

63189.q: What is the date of Christmas Day?
63189.e: 25 December is Christmas Day itself. It is a public holiday all over Switzerland.

63190.q: What is the holiday on 26 December called in most cantons?
63190.e: 26 December is named after Saint Stephen. In most cantons it is a day off.

63191.q: Who brings the presents on Christmas Eve in many Swiss families?
63191.e: In many families in Switzerland the Christ Child brings the presents. Samichlaus, the Swiss St Nicholas, comes earlier, on 6 December.
63191.m: In many Swiss families the Christ Child brings the presents.

63192.q: What is the church service in the night before Christmas Day called?
63192.e: Many churches hold a service at midnight on Christmas night. It is also called Christmas Matins.
63192.m: On Christmas night there is Midnight Mass.

63193.q: How do you say “Happy Christmas” in French?
63193.e: “Noël” is French for Christmas and “joyeux” means happy. You often hear this greeting in French-speaking Switzerland.

63194.q: What is the English name for the evening of 24 December?
63194.e: “Eve” means the evening before. So “Christmas Eve” is the evening before Christmas Day.
63194.m: The evening of 24 December is called Christmas Eve.

63195.q: In which months does Ash Wednesday fall?
63195.e: Ash Wednesday depends on the date of Easter. It always falls in February or March.
63195.m: Ash Wednesday is in February or March.

63196.q: What does the priest draw on many people's foreheads on Ash Wednesday?
63196.e: During the service, people receive a small cross of ash. That is where the day gets its name.
63196.m: On Ash Wednesday you receive a cross of ash on your forehead.

63197.q: What is the ash for Ash Wednesday often made from?
63197.e: Often the blessed branches from the year before are burnt. Their ash is then blessed.
63197.m: The ash often comes from burnt palm branches from the year before.

63198.q: Which fun festival ends in many places just before Ash Wednesday?
63198.e: Before the serious day of Ash Wednesday, many people celebrate merrily once more with masks and music.
63198.m: In many places people celebrate carnival before Ash Wednesday.

63199.q: When does the Basel carnival begin?
a: On the Monday after Ash Wednesday
63199.e: The Basel carnival begins on the Monday after Ash Wednesday at 4 o'clock in the morning with the Morgestraich. It is later than most other carnivals.
63199.m: The Basel carnival only begins after Ash Wednesday, with the Morgestraich.

63200.q: What is the cross of ash a sign of?
a: Turning back and a fresh start
63200.e: The ash is a reminder that you can think about your life and make a fresh start.
63200.m: The cross of ash is a sign of turning back and a fresh start.

63201.q: What do many Catholic families eat on Ash Wednesday instead of meat?
63201.e: For Catholics, Ash Wednesday is a day of fasting when no meat is eaten. Fish is allowed.
63201.m: Many Catholics eat no meat on Ash Wednesday.

63202.q: Roughly how long is Lent, which begins on Ash Wednesday?
63202.e: Lent begins on Ash Wednesday. It lasts about 40 days and ends at Easter.
63202.m: Lent lasts about 40 days until Easter.

63203.q: How many days does Lent last before Easter?
63203.e: Lent has 40 days of fasting. The Sundays are not counted.

63204.q: According to the Bible, who fasted for a long time in the desert?
63204.e: Before his ministry, Jesus went into the desert and fasted there. Lent is a reminder of this.
63204.m: Lent is a reminder of Jesus fasting in the desert.

63205.q: What do many people give up during Lent?
63205.e: Many people choose to give up something they like, for example sweets or screen time.
63205.m: During Lent many people choose to give something up.

63206.q: What colour are the priest's robes during Lent?
63206.e: In church, purple is the colour of reflection and preparation.
63206.m: During Lent the priest wears purple.

63207.q: What do many Swiss parishes eat together during Lent to raise money for poor people?
63207.e: On soup days there is a simple meal. The money saved is donated to aid projects.
63207.m: On soup day you share with poor people.

63208.q: What hangs in front of the altar in some churches during Lent?
63208.e: The Lenten cloth, also called a hunger cloth, covers the altar or hangs where everyone can see it in the church. It often has pictures painted on it.
63208.m: In some churches a Lenten cloth hangs during Lent.

63209.q: Which joyful word do Catholics not sing during Lent?
63209.e: Hallelujah is a cry of joy. It is left out during Lent and sung again at Easter.
63209.m: No Hallelujah is sung during Lent.

63210.q: What is the last week of Lent called?
63210.e: In Holy Week, Christians remember the last days of Jesus before Easter.
63210.m: The last week before Easter is called Holy Week.

63211.q: How many days after Palm Sunday is Good Friday?
63211.e: From Sunday to Friday is five days: Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday.
63211.m: Good Friday is five days after Palm Sunday.

63212.q: Which city did Jesus enter on Palm Sunday?
63212.e: Jesus came with his disciples to the city with the Temple for a great festival.
63212.m: On Palm Sunday Jesus entered Jerusalem.

63213.q: What did the people wave when Jesus arrived?
63213.e: The people welcomed Jesus with branches from palm trees. That is where the day gets its name.
63213.m: The people welcomed Jesus with palm branches.

63214.q: What did the people shout when Jesus entered the city?
63214.e: Hosanna is an old cry of joy. It originally meant “Save us!” and became a shout of joy.

63215.q: Where do many families keep the blessed branches from Palm Sunday?
63215.e: The blessed branches are often put behind a cross in the home or hung up in the stable. They are meant as a reminder of the blessing.
63215.m: Blessed palm branches often hang at home by the cross.

63216.q: For which Jewish festival did Jesus come to Jerusalem on Palm Sunday?
63216.e: Many people came to Jerusalem for Passover. This festival remembers the freedom from slavery in Egypt.
63216.m: Jesus came to Jerusalem for Passover.

63217.q: Which branches are often used in Switzerland instead of palm branches?
63217.e: Palm trees do not grow outdoors here. That is why green branches such as box are tied together.
63217.m: In Switzerland box branches are often used on Palm Sunday.

63218.e: Palm Sunday is the Sunday just before Easter Sunday.
63218.m: Palm Sunday is the Sunday before Easter.

63219.q: What did Jesus celebrate with his disciples on Maundy Thursday?
63219.e: On the evening before his death, Jesus ate with his friends one last time.
63219.m: On Maundy Thursday people remember the Last Supper.

63220.q: How many disciples did Jesus have at the Last Supper?
63220.e: Jesus had twelve apostles who sat at the table with him.

63221.q: What do children in some places use instead of church bells until Easter?
63221.e: Because the bells are silent from Maundy Thursday until the Easter Vigil, people make noise with wooden rattles or clappers.
63221.m: In some places wooden rattles replace the bells before Easter.

63222.q: What did the disciples do while Jesus prayed in the garden?
63222.e: Jesus asked them to stay awake with him. But they were tired and fell asleep.
63222.m: In the garden the disciples fell asleep while Jesus prayed.

63223.q: In which garden did Jesus pray after the Last Supper?
63223.e: Jesus went with the disciples at night to a garden outside the city and prayed there, full of fear.
63223.m: Jesus prayed in the Garden of Gethsemane.

63224.q: How did Judas show the soldiers in the garden which man was Jesus?
63224.e: Judas had agreed on a sign with the soldiers. He greeted Jesus the way you greet a friend.
63224.m: Judas betrayed Jesus with a kiss.

63225.q: According to an old custom, where do the church bells fly on Maundy Thursday?
63225.e: This is how children were told why the bells are silent until the Easter Vigil.
63225.m: According to old custom, the bells fly to Rome.

63226.q: What is often served on Maundy Thursday according to an old custom?
63226.e: In German the day is called Gründonnerstag, which contains the word for green. That is why people like to eat something green, such as spinach or herbs.
63226.m: On Maundy Thursday people like to eat something green.

63227.q: What do Christians remember on Good Friday?
63227.e: On Good Friday, Christians remember that Jesus was crucified and died.
63227.m: On Good Friday Christians remember the death of Jesus.

63229.e: Jesus was crucified by the Romans. That is why the cross is the most important symbol of Christians.

63230.q: What is the hill where Jesus was crucified called?
63230.e: Golgotha was outside the city wall of Jerusalem at that time. The name means place of the skull.

63231.q: How many stations do the Stations of the Cross usually have?
63231.e: The Stations of the Cross show in pictures the way of Jesus to the tomb. There are usually fourteen stations.
63231.m: The Stations of the Cross usually have fourteen stations.

63232.q: Who sentenced Jesus to death on the cross?
63232.e: Pilate was the Roman governor in Jerusalem. Only he could pass a death sentence.

63233.q: Who helped Jesus carry the cross?
63233.e: The soldiers forced a man coming in from the fields to carry the heavy cross.
63233.m: Simon of Cyrene carried the cross for Jesus.

63234.q: In which canton do the famous Mendrisio processions take place on Maundy Thursday and Good Friday?
63234.e: In Mendrisio people in costume walk through the town and act out the story of the Passion. The custom is part of UNESCO's cultural heritage.
63234.m: The Mendrisio processions are an Easter custom in Ticino.

63235.q: Who walks through the streets of Romont FR in black clothes on Good Friday?
63235.e: The mourning women, in French “Pleureuses”, carry objects that recall the suffering of Jesus. The custom is several hundred years old.
63235.m: In Romont the mourning women walk through the town on Good Friday.

63236.q: What do Christians celebrate on Easter Sunday?
a: That Jesus rose from the dead
63236.e: Christians believe that Jesus was raised from death to new life. This is the most important Christian festival.
63236.m: At Easter Christians celebrate the resurrection of Jesus.

63237.q: Which woman came to the tomb of Jesus on Easter morning?
63237.e: Mary Magdalene went to the tomb early in the morning with other women. They found it empty.
63237.m: Mary Magdalene found the empty tomb.

63238.q: What had been rolled away from the entrance of the tomb?
63238.e: The tomb was cut into a rock and closed with a heavy stone.
63238.m: On Easter morning the stone had been rolled away from the tomb.

63239.q: Who told the women at the tomb that Jesus is alive?
63239.e: In the Gospels, a messenger from God tells the women the good news.
63239.m: An angel told the women about the resurrection.

63240.q: What determines the date of Easter?
a: The first full moon of spring
The first new moon of the year
63240.e: Easter is on the Sunday after the first full moon of spring. That is why it falls on a different date every year.
63240.m: Easter depends on the spring full moon.

63241.q: In which months can Easter fall?
63241.e: Easter is no earlier than 22 March and no later than 25 April.
63241.m: Easter is always in March or April.

63242.q: Which day after Easter is also a day off in most cantons?
63242.e: In most cantons Easter Monday is a public holiday. That makes a long Easter weekend.
63242.m: Easter Monday is a public holiday in most cantons.

63243.q: Which disciple only believed that Jesus was alive when he saw him himself?
63243.e: Thomas was not there when Jesus appeared to the disciples. He wanted to see the wounds himself. That is why people still say “doubting Thomas” today.
63243.m: Thomas doubted the resurrection at first.

63244.q: Why were there so many eggs at Easter in the past?
63244.e: In the past, people were not allowed to eat eggs during Lent. The eggs piled up and were hard-boiled to keep them.
63244.m: In the past, eggs piled up during Lent.

63245.q: What is the Easter egg a sign of?
63245.e: A chick hatches from an egg. So the egg suits the festival of the resurrection.
63245.m: The Easter egg is a sign of new life.

63246.q: What colour do eggs turn when you boil them with onion skins?
63246.e: Onion skins give a warm brown to reddish brown colour.
63246.m: Onion skins turn eggs reddish brown.

63247.q: What can you use to dye eggs pink to red?
63247.e: Beetroot has a strong red juice that also colours the eggshell.
63247.m: Beetroot dyes eggs pink to red.

63248.q: What can you use to dye eggs blue?
63248.e: Red cabbage juice looks purple, but it turns the white eggshell blue.

63249.q: What can you use to dye eggs yellow?
63249.e: Turmeric is a yellow spice. It colours very strongly.

63250.q: How do you prepare eggs before painting or dyeing them?
63250.e: Hard-boiled eggs do not break so easily and keep longer.
63250.m: Easter eggs are hard-boiled before dyeing.

63251.q: What colour were Easter eggs most often in the past?
63251.e: Red is the oldest colour for Easter eggs. It is a reminder of the blood of Jesus and of life.
63251.m: The traditional colour of Easter eggs is red.

63252.q: How does a dyed Easter egg get a leaf pattern?
a: You tie a leaf to the egg with a stocking
You glue leaves onto the shell
You roll the egg through fresh grass
You paint the leaves with watercolours
63252.e: Where the leaf lies, no dye gets through. So after dyeing a pale leaf print is left.
63252.m: A leaf under a stocking gives a lovely pattern on the egg.

63253.q: What does the Easter Bunny do according to custom?
63253.e: At Easter children look for the eggs and sweets the Easter Bunny is said to have hidden.
63253.m: The Easter Bunny hides the Easter eggs.

63254.q: Which animal used to bring the Easter eggs in the Emmental?
63254.e: As late as the 19th century, the cuckoo brought the eggs in parts of Switzerland such as the Emmental.
63254.m: In the Emmental the cuckoo used to bring the Easter eggs.

63255.q: On which day do children look for the eggs the Easter Bunny has hidden?
63255.e: On Easter Sunday many children search the garden or the house for hidden Easter eggs.
63255.m: Easter eggs are hunted on Easter Sunday.

63256.q: Roughly how long has the Easter Bunny been known?
63256.e: The Easter Bunny is first mentioned in a book in 1682.
63256.m: The Easter Bunny has been known for over 300 years.

63257.q: What are many Easter bunnies in the shops made of?
63257.e: Since sugar became cheaper, there have been lots of chocolate bunnies and eggs.
63257.m: Many Easter bunnies are made of chocolate.

63258.q: What do children often collect the Easter eggs they find in?
63258.e: The Easter nest is a little basket, often filled with hay or grass.
63258.m: Easter eggs are collected in an Easter nest.

63259.q: What has the hare long been a symbol of for Christians?
63259.e: Even the Church Father Ambrose saw the hare as an image of the resurrection.
63259.m: The hare is a symbol of the resurrection.

63260.q: According to an old belief, for example in France, who brings the Easter eggs?
63260.e: According to this belief, the bells come back on Easter night and drop eggs into the gardens.
63260.m: In France, according to old belief, the bells bring the eggs.

63261.q: How does Eiertütschen, the Swiss egg-knocking game, work?
a: Two people knock their eggs together
You roll eggs down a hill
You throw eggs high into the air
You hide eggs in the grass
63261.e: In Eiertütschen two people knock their hard-boiled Easter eggs against each other.
63261.m: In Eiertütschen you knock two eggs against each other.

a: The person whose egg stays whole
The person with the bigger egg
63262.e: The egg with the harder shell stays in one piece. Its owner has won.
63262.m: In Eiertütschen the egg that stays whole wins.

63263.q: According to old custom, what did the winner of Eiertütschen get?
63263.e: According to old custom, the winner could keep the other person's broken egg. Today everyone usually keeps their own egg.
63263.m: In the past the winner of Eiertütschen got the broken egg.

63264.q: Which part of the egg do you usually knock with first?
63264.e: You hold the egg in your fist and let only the pointed end peep out.
63264.m: In egg knocking you strike with the pointed end first.

63265.q: In which city do many people meet on the Kornhausplatz at Easter for Eiertütschen?
63265.e: On Easter Sunday many people knock eggs on the Kornhausplatz. The custom has been recorded there for over 100 years.
63265.m: In Bern people knock eggs on the Kornhausplatz at Easter.

63266.q: In the custom of Zwänzgerle, what do adults throw at a child's Easter egg?
63266.e: The custom has this name because you throw a Zwänzgi, which is a 20-centime coin.
63266.m: In Zwänzgerle you throw a 20-centime coin.

63267.q: In which city is Zwänzgerle a well-known Easter custom?
63267.e: Zwänzgerle takes place on Easter Monday in the old town near the Haus zum Rüden on the river Limmat.
63267.m: Zwänzgerle is an Easter custom from Zurich.

63268.q: When is the new Easter candle lit for the first time?
63268.e: On the night before Easter Sunday many churches hold a service in which the candle is lit anew.
63268.m: The Easter candle is first lit on Easter night.

63269.q: What is the Easter candle lit from?
63269.e: A fire is lit and blessed in front of the church. The candle is lit from it.
63269.m: The Easter candle is lit from the Easter fire.

63270.q: What do the Greek letters Alpha and Omega on the Easter candle mean?
63270.e: Alpha is the first and Omega the last letter of the Greek alphabet. They say: Christ is the beginning and the end of everything.
63270.m: Alpha and Omega mean beginning and end.

63271.q: Which number is written on the Easter candle?
63271.e: There is a new Easter candle every year. It shows the year in which it burns.
63271.m: The year is written on the Easter candle.

63272.q: Which symbol can be seen large on the Easter candle?
63272.e: The cross is a reminder of the death and resurrection of Jesus.
63272.m: There is a cross on the Easter candle.

63273.q: What do the five red nails on the Easter candle remind people of?
63273.e: The five nails or grains of incense stand for the wounds in the hands, feet and side of Jesus.
63273.m: The five nails are a reminder of the wounds of Jesus.

63274.q: What material is an Easter candle traditionally made of?
63274.e: Pure beeswax was considered especially valuable, so it is used for the Easter candle.
63274.m: The Easter candle is traditionally made of beeswax.

63275.q: What does the priest call out as he carries the Easter candle into the dark church?
63275.e: In Latin the call is “Lumen Christi”. The congregation answers “Thanks be to God”.
63275.m: As the Easter candle is carried in, the priest calls “Christ, the light”.

63276.q: At a baptism, what is the baptismal candle lit from?
63276.e: In this way the light of the Easter candle is passed on to the child.
63276.m: The baptismal candle is lit from the Easter candle.

63277.q: What do Christians celebrate on Ascension Day?
a: Jesus returns to God in heaven
Jesus is born in a stable
Jesus is baptised in the Jordan
63277.e: According to the Bible, Jesus was taken up into heaven before the eyes of the disciples.
63277.m: On Ascension Day Christians celebrate that Jesus returned to heaven.

63278.q: Roughly how many days after Easter is Ascension Day?
63278.e: According to the Acts of the Apostles, Jesus showed himself to his disciples for 40 days after Easter. That is why Ascension is celebrated about 40 days after Easter.
63278.m: Ascension Day is about 40 days after Easter.

63279.q: On which day of the week is Ascension Day always?
63279.e: Ascension Day is always exactly five weeks and four days after Easter Sunday. So it always falls on a Thursday, and many people take the Friday off too.
63279.m: Ascension Day is always on a Thursday.

63281.q: What do many people do in Beromünster LU on Ascension Day?
63281.e: In the Ascension ride, riders and clergy move in a long procession through the fields around Beromünster. The custom is very old.
63281.m: In Beromünster there is a procession on horseback on Ascension Day.

63282.q: What do people pray for during the Ascension ride?
a: For the fields and the harvest
For lots of snow in winter
63282.e: The ride is a request for protection and blessing for the fields.
63282.m: During the Ascension ride people ask for a blessing on the fields.

63283.q: According to the Bible, what hid Jesus from the disciples at the Ascension?
63283.e: The Acts of the Apostles says that Jesus was lifted up and a cloud took him out of sight.
63283.m: At the Ascension a cloud took Jesus up.

63284.q: According to the Bible, from which mountain did Jesus ascend into heaven?
63284.e: The Mount of Olives is right next to Jerusalem. From there the disciples then went back into the city.
63284.m: The Ascension happened on the Mount of Olives near Jerusalem.

63285.q: Where in Switzerland is Ascension Day a public holiday?
63285.e: Like Christmas, Ascension Day is a day off all over Switzerland.
63285.m: Ascension Day is a public holiday all over Switzerland.

63286.q: Whose birthday is Pentecost also called?
63286.e: At Pentecost the disciples began to tell everyone about Jesus. That is how the first community began.
63286.m: Pentecost is seen as the birthday of the Church.

63287.q: Who came to the disciples at Pentecost?
63287.e: Jesus had promised to send his friends a helper. He gave them courage and strength.
63287.m: At Pentecost the Holy Spirit came to the disciples.

63288.q: According to the Bible, what did the Holy Spirit look like at Pentecost?
63288.e: Something that looked like a small flame came to rest on each disciple.
63288.m: At Pentecost tongues as of fire appeared.

63289.q: What did the disciples hear from heaven at Pentecost?
63289.e: Suddenly there came a sound like a mighty wind that filled the whole house.
63289.m: At Pentecost there was a roar like a storm.

63290.q: What could the disciples suddenly do at Pentecost?
63290.e: People from many countries heard the disciples speaking in their own language.
63290.m: At Pentecost everyone understood the disciples in their own language.

63291.q: How many weeks after Easter is Pentecost celebrated?
63291.e: Pentecost is seven weeks after Easter, on the 50th day. The word Pentecost comes from the Greek word for “the fiftieth”.
63291.m: Pentecost is seven weeks after Easter.

63292.q: Which animal is a symbol of the Holy Spirit?
63292.e: At the baptism of Jesus the Spirit of God came down like a dove. Since then it has been its symbol.
63292.m: The dove is the symbol of the Holy Spirit.

63293.q: Which apostle gave a great sermon at Pentecost?
63293.e: He stood up with the other apostles and explained to the people what had happened.

63294.q: What colour does the priest wear at Pentecost?
63294.e: Red is a reminder of the fire of the Holy Spirit.
63294.m: At Pentecost the colour in church is red.

63295.q: In which Gospel is the Annunciation to Mary told in detail?
63295.e: The evangelist Luke tells in detail how the angel comes to Mary. That is why many churches read this story from his Gospel.
63295.m: Luke tells the Annunciation to Mary in detail.

63296.q: How did Mary react when the angel greeted her?
63296.e: Mary was startled by the angel's words. She wondered what this greeting could mean.
63296.m: Mary was startled when the angel greeted her.

63297.q: According to the angel, what will the child be called?
63297.e: The angel told Mary that her child would be great and would be called Son of the Most High. The Most High means God.
63297.m: According to the angel, the child will be called Son of the Most High.

63298.q: According to the angel, how long will the child's reign last?
63298.e: The angel said the child's kingdom would have no end. So it is to last for ever.
63298.m: According to the angel, the child's kingdom has no end.

63299.q: How did Mary finally answer the angel's message?
63299.e: Mary said: “Let it be to me as you have said.” With this she agreed to God's plan.
63299.m: Mary said yes to God's plan.

63300.q: What did the angel tell Mary about God?
a: God only lives in the Temple
God needs a lot of rest
63300.e: Mary was amazed at the message. The angel replied: “Nothing is impossible for God.”
63300.m: Nothing is impossible for God, said the angel.

63301.q: What do many Christians call Mary because she is the mother of Jesus?
63301.e: For many Christians Jesus is the Son of God. That is why they also call Mary the Mother of God.
63301.m: Many Christians call Mary the Mother of God.

63302.q: In which part of the Bible is the story of the Annunciation to Mary?
63302.e: The story is in one of the four Gospels. The Gospels belong to the New Testament.
63302.m: The Annunciation to Mary is in the New Testament.

63303.q: What is the well-known prayer called that begins with the angel's greeting to Mary?
63303.e: “Ave Maria” means “Hail Mary”. That is how the angel greeted Mary.
63303.m: The Ave Maria begins with the angel's greeting.

63304.q: What is Jesus often called, after the place where he grew up?
63304.e: Jesus grew up in Nazareth. That is why he is often called Jesus of Nazareth.

63305.q: How did the people of Nazareth react when Jesus preached in the synagogue there?
63305.e: The Gospel of Luke tells how the people in his home town became angry and drove him out of the town. Jesus said: A prophet is not accepted in his home town.
63305.m: In his home town of Nazareth Jesus was rejected.

63306.e: Galilee is a hilly region in the north of the country. Many stories about Jesus take place there.
63306.m: Nazareth is in the region of Galilee.

63307.q: In which present-day country is Nazareth?
63307.e: Today Nazareth is a city in the north of Israel.

63308.q: How big was Nazareth at the time of Jesus?
63308.e: Researchers estimate that only a few hundred people lived in Nazareth then. Today Nazareth is a large city.
63308.m: At the time of Jesus Nazareth was a small village.

63309.q: Which king did the family of Jesus have to flee from?
63309.e: King Herod was afraid of a new king. That is why Joseph had to flee with Mary and the child.
63309.m: The family fled from King Herod.

63310.q: Which language did Jesus speak in everyday life as a child in Nazareth?
63310.e: People in Galilee spoke Aramaic at that time. Jesus spoke this language too.
63310.m: In everyday life Jesus spoke Aramaic.

63311.q: Which large church stands in Nazareth today?
63311.e: The present basilica was consecrated in 1969. It is considered the largest church in the Middle East.
63311.m: The Basilica of the Annunciation stands in Nazareth.

63312.q: According to Luke, roughly how old was Jesus when he left Nazareth and began to preach?
63312.e: The Gospel of Luke says that Jesus was about 30 years old when he began his public ministry.

63313.q: What was the job of Joseph, Mary's husband?
63313.e: The Bible calls Joseph a carpenter. This means a craftsman who worked with wood and other building materials.

63314.q: Which animals did Joseph and Mary bring to the Temple as an offering when Jesus was still a baby?
63314.e: The Gospel of Luke tells how the parents offered two young doves. This was the offering for families who were not rich.
63314.m: Joseph and Mary offered two doves in the Temple.

63315.q: What did Joseph do after an angel had given him a task?
a: He did what the angel said
63315.e: In the Gospel of Matthew Joseph obeys straight away every time. He does what the angel told him.
63315.m: Joseph did what the angel told him.

63316.q: How does the Gospel of Matthew describe Joseph?
63316.e: Matthew calls Joseph a righteous man. He wanted to do the right thing and not shame Mary.
63316.m: According to Matthew, Joseph was a righteous man.

63317.q: How many of Joseph's sentences are written down word for word in the Bible?
63317.e: Joseph acts in the Bible, but not one of his words is quoted. That is why he is seen as a quiet helper.
63317.m: Joseph does not say a single word in the Bible.

63318.q: Which flower does Joseph hold in his hand in many pictures?
63318.e: In many pictures Joseph carries a white lily or a walking staff. The lily is a sign of purity.
63318.m: In pictures Joseph can often be recognised by the lily.

63319.q: In which story is Joseph last mentioned alive in the Bible?
a: When Jesus stayed behind in the Temple
63319.e: After the story of the Temple visit with the young Jesus, Joseph no longer appears in the accounts. Many think he died early.
63319.m: Joseph last appears in the story of the Temple visit.

63320.q: In the Gospel of Matthew, what do the people in his home town call Jesus?
63320.e: The people asked in surprise: “Isn't this the carpenter's son?” They knew Joseph and his job.
63320.m: The people called Jesus the carpenter's son.

63321.q: Who is Saint Joseph a patron saint of?
63321.e: Because he worked as a craftsman, Joseph is the patron saint of workers, especially carpenters.
63321.m: Joseph is the patron saint of workers and carpenters.

63322.q: How old was Jesus when he stayed behind in the Temple?
63322.e: The Gospel of Luke tells how Jesus was twelve years old when he travelled with his parents to the festival in Jerusalem.
63322.m: Jesus was twelve when he stayed in the Temple.

63323.q: For which festival did the family travel to Jerusalem every year?
63323.e: Jesus' family made a pilgrimage to Jerusalem every year for the Jewish festival of Passover.
63323.m: The family celebrated Passover in Jerusalem every year.

63324.q: When did Mary and Joseph notice that Jesus was missing?
63324.e: The parents thought Jesus was with the other travellers. Only after a day's journey did they notice he was missing.
63324.m: The parents only noticed after a day that Jesus was missing.

63325.q: After how many days did the parents find Jesus in the Temple?
63325.e: Mary and Joseph searched for Jesus and found him in the Temple after three days.
63325.m: After three days the parents found Jesus.

63326.q: Who did the twelve-year-old Jesus talk with in the Temple?
63326.e: Jesus sat among the teachers. He listened to them and asked them questions.
63326.m: In the Temple Jesus talked with the teachers.

63327.q: How did the people in the Temple react to the twelve-year-old Jesus?
63327.e: Everyone who heard him was amazed at his understanding and his answers.
63327.m: The people were amazed at the clever Jesus.

63328.q: What did Jesus call the Temple when his parents found him?
63328.e: Jesus said something like: “Didn't you know I had to be in my Father's house?” By Father he meant God.
63328.m: Jesus called the Temple his Father's house.

63329.q: Where did Jesus go with his parents after the story in the Temple?
63329.e: Jesus returned to Nazareth with Mary and Joseph and obeyed them.
63329.m: After the Temple Jesus went home to Nazareth with his parents.

63330.q: What did Mary do with everything that had happened with Jesus?
a: She treasured it in her heart
She wrote it in a book
63330.e: The Gospel of Luke tells how Mary treasured everything that had happened in her heart. She thought about it for a long time.
63330.m: Mary treasured everything in her heart.

63331.q: Because he preached in the desert, what else is John the Baptist called in the Bible?
a: A voice crying in the wilderness
63331.e: The prophet Isaiah had already spoken of a voice crying in the wilderness. The Gospels apply this to John.
63331.m: John is also called the voice crying in the wilderness.

63332.q: What was the name of John the Baptist's father?
63332.e: His father was the priest Zechariah. An angel announced the birth of John to him.

63333.q: What was the name of John the Baptist's mother?
63333.e: John's mother was called Elizabeth. She and her husband were already old when John was born.
63333.m: John the Baptist's mother was called Elizabeth.

63334.q: According to the Bible, what did John the Baptist eat?
63334.e: John lived very simply. He ate locusts and wild honey.
63334.m: John ate locusts and wild honey.

63335.q: What was John the Baptist's clothing made of?
63335.e: John wore clothing made of camel hair and a leather belt.
63335.m: John wore clothes of camel hair.

63336.e: John baptised people in the water of the river. That is why he is called the Baptist.
63336.m: John is called the Baptist because he baptised people.
