64032.m: The Festival of Sacrifice is called Eid al-Adha in Arabic.

64033.q: According to Islamic tradition, what was the name of the son Ibrahim was to sacrifice?
64033.e: Most Muslim scholars say it was Ismail. In the Bible the son in this story is called Isaac.
64033.m: According to Islamic tradition, Ibrahim was to sacrifice his son Ismail.

64034.q: Which animals are often sacrificed at the Festival of Sacrifice?
64034.e: For the Festival of Sacrifice a healthy animal is slaughtered, usually a sheep, a goat or a cow. In some countries it is also a camel.
64034.m: At the Festival of Sacrifice people often sacrifice a sheep, goat or cow.

64035.q: In Switzerland, what must always happen to mammals such as sheep before slaughter?
64035.e: In Switzerland it is forbidden to slaughter mammals without stunning them. This also applies to animals sacrificed for the Festival of Sacrifice.
64035.m: In Switzerland mammals must be stunned before slaughter.

64036.q: What are many Muslims doing in Mecca at the time of the Festival of Sacrifice?
64036.e: Every year millions of Muslims travel to Mecca. The Festival of Sacrifice falls during the days of this great pilgrimage, the Hajj.
64036.m: The Festival of Sacrifice is celebrated at the time of the pilgrimage to Mecca.

64037.q: What is the Festival of Sacrifice called in Turkish?
64037.e: Kurban means sacrifice and bayram means festival. Many Turkish families in Switzerland call the festival this.
64037.m: In Turkish the Festival of Sacrifice is called Kurban Bayramı.

64038.q: How long does the Festival of Sacrifice usually last?
64038.e: The Festival of Sacrifice begins on the tenth day of the pilgrimage month. It usually lasts four days.
64038.m: The Festival of Sacrifice usually lasts four days.

64039.q: When was the Festival of Sacrifice in 2026?
64039.e: In 2026 the Festival of Sacrifice began around 27 May. Because the festival follows the moon, it falls on a different date every year.
64039.m: In 2026 the Festival of Sacrifice was at the end of May.

64040.q: What does the story of Ibrahim at the Festival of Sacrifice stand for?
64040.e: Ibrahim trusted God completely. That is why Muslims see him as a model of faith.
64040.m: The story of Ibrahim shows great trust in God.

64041.q: What must be seen in the sky for a new Islamic month to begin?
64041.e: A new month begins when the first thin crescent moon can be seen after the new moon. That is why many people watch the sky carefully in the evening.
64041.m: An Islamic month begins with the new crescent moon.

64042.q: What is the new, thin crescent moon called in Arabic?
64042.e: The Arabic word hilal means crescent moon. When the hilal is seen, a new month begins.
64042.m: The crescent moon is called hilal in Arabic.

64043.q: What do you see in the sky at new moon?
64043.e: At new moon the moon is between the Earth and the sun. Its bright side faces away from us, so we can hardly see it.
64043.m: At new moon you can hardly see the moon.

64044.q: Roughly how long is it from one new moon to the next?
64044.e: The moon takes about 29 and a half days to look the same again. That is why a lunar month has 29 or 30 days.
64044.m: From new moon to new moon is about 29 and a half days.

64045.q: Which flag shows a white crescent moon and a star on a red background?
64045.e: The Turkish flag is red with a white crescent moon and a white star. Other countries also have a crescent moon on their flag.
64045.m: The Turkish flag shows a crescent moon and a star.

64046.q: What is the counterpart of the Red Cross called in many Muslim countries?
64046.e: The Red Cross was founded in Geneva. In many Muslim countries the same movement helps people under the sign of a red crescent.
64046.m: The Red Crescent helps people just like the Red Cross.

64047.q: Where can you see a crescent moon on many mosques?
a: Right at the top of the dome or minaret
64047.e: Many mosques have a golden crescent moon on top of the dome or minaret. It is a well-known symbol of Islam.
64047.m: Many mosques have a crescent moon on top.

64048.q: At what time of day do people look out for the new crescent moon?
64048.e: The new crescent moon is very thin and sets soon after the sun. You can only see it briefly at dusk.
64048.m: You look for the new crescent moon in the evening after sunset.

64049.q: In which direction do you see the new crescent moon in the evening?
64049.e: The new crescent moon is close to the sun in the sky. In the evening the sun sets in the west, and that is where you see the crescent too.
64049.m: In the evening you see the new crescent moon in the west.

64050.q: What happens if clouds hide the new crescent moon?
a: People wait for the full moon
64050.e: An Islamic month has at most 30 days. If the crescent cannot be seen, people simply count to 30 and then start the new month.
64050.m: If the crescent moon cannot be seen, the month has 30 days.

64051.q: What does the Islamic calendar follow?
64051.e: Every month in the Islamic calendar begins with a new moon. That is why it is called a lunar calendar.
64051.m: The Islamic calendar follows the moon.

64052.q: How many months does an Islamic year have?
64052.e: Like our calendar, the Islamic calendar has twelve months. But the months are shorter.
64052.m: An Islamic year has twelve months.

64053.q: How long is an Islamic year compared with our year?
64053.e: Twelve lunar months together are shorter than a solar year. An Islamic year has only about 354 days.
64053.m: An Islamic year is about 11 days shorter than our year.

64054.q: Is Ramadan in the same month of our calendar every year?
a: No, it moves through the year
64054.e: The Islamic calendar follows the moon and is shorter than our year. So Ramadan begins a little earlier in our calendar every year. That way it sometimes falls in summer and sometimes in winter.

64055.q: Which month of the Islamic calendar is Ramadan?
64055.e: Ramadan is the ninth of twelve months. It is the best-known month of the Islamic year.
64055.m: Ramadan is the ninth month of the Islamic calendar.

64056.q: What do Muslims celebrate on the first day of the Islamic year?
64056.e: The Islamic year begins with the month of Muharram. The first day is the Islamic New Year.
64056.m: The first day of the Islamic year is New Year.

64057.q: Why is the Islamic year number much smaller than ours?
a: Because every other year is left out
64057.e: The Islamic count of years only begins in the 7th century AD. That is why the number is smaller: in summer 2026, for example, the year 1448 began.
64057.m: The Islamic count of years started later than ours.

64058.q: When does a new day begin in the Islamic calendar?
64058.e: In the Islamic calendar the day begins in the evening. That is why some festivals are already celebrated the evening before.
64058.m: In the Islamic calendar the day begins at sunset.

64059.q: Which month is the month of the pilgrimage to Mecca?
64059.e: The great pilgrimage takes place in the last month of the Islamic year. It is called Dhu al-Hijjah.
64059.m: The pilgrimage is in the twelfth month of the Islamic year.

64060.q: Roughly how long does it take for Ramadan to move through all the seasons?
64060.e: Every year Ramadan moves by about eleven days. After roughly 33 years it is back in the same season.
64060.m: Ramadan moves through all the seasons in about 33 years.

64061.q: What is the colourful lantern that many children carry during Ramadan called?
64061.e: The fanous is a beautiful lantern with coloured windows. For many children it is part of Ramadan.
64061.m: The Ramadan lantern is called a fanous.

64062.q: In which country are Ramadan lanterns especially well known?
64062.e: In Egypt lanterns hang in the streets everywhere during Ramadan. Today they are popular in other Arab countries too.
64062.m: Ramadan lanterns are especially well known in Egypt.

64063.q: In which city is the tradition of Ramadan lanterns said to have begun?
64063.e: An old story tells that over 1,000 years ago the people of Cairo welcomed a ruler with lanterns. The custom is said to have grown from that.
64063.m: The custom of Ramadan lanterns is said to have begun in Cairo.

64064.q: What are traditional Ramadan lanterns made of?
64064.e: Craftspeople shape a frame from tin or copper. In between they set coloured panes of glass, through which the light shimmers.
64064.m: Traditional Ramadan lanterns are made of metal and coloured glass.

64065.q: What do children in Egypt often do with their lanterns during Ramadan?
a: They sing songs with them in the street
They throw them into the Nile
They bury them in the sand
64065.e: In the evening children walk through the lanes with their glowing lanterns. As they go, they sing cheerful Ramadan songs.
64065.m: Children sing Ramadan songs with their lanterns.

64066.q: What do the many lanterns and lights during Ramadan show?
a: The end of the school year
64066.e: The lights decorate houses and streets. They show that people are happy about the special month.
64066.m: The Ramadan lights show joy about the holy month.

64067.q: Where do Ramadan lanterns often hang in Egypt?
a: Across the lanes and on houses
64067.e: During Ramadan people stretch strings across the lanes. Lanterns and lights hang from them and glow in the evening.
64067.m: In Egypt the lanterns hang across the lanes.

64068.q: What were lanterns used for at night in the past?
64068.e: In the past there were no street lamps. With a lantern you could find your way to the mosque or home at night.
64068.m: In the past lanterns helped people find their way in the dark.

64069.q: What can some modern plastic Ramadan lanterns do?
64069.e: Today there are also plastic lanterns with batteries. They light up in colours, and some play Ramadan songs.
64069.m: Some modern Ramadan lanterns light up and play music.

64070.q: What shapes do many Ramadan lights on houses and windows have?
64070.e: Many families decorate their homes with lights during Ramadan. Crescent moons and stars are especially popular.
64070.m: Ramadan lights are often shaped like a crescent moon and star.

64071.q: Which green nuts are often found in baklava?
64071.e: Pistachios are small green nuts. They are often sprinkled over baklava or put between the layers of pastry.

64072.q: Which sweet pastry made of many paper-thin layers with syrup is often served at the festival?
64072.e: Baklava is made of many thin sheets of pastry. After baking, sweet syrup is poured over it.
64072.m: Baklava is a popular festival pastry.

64073.q: What is the filling of baklava usually made of?
64073.e: Chopped nuts are sprinkled between the thin sheets of pastry. This makes baklava crunchy.
64073.m: Baklava is usually filled with chopped nuts.

64074.q: What is lokum, which people like to give as a present at the festival?
64074.e: Lokum is a soft sweet in small cubes. It often tastes of rose or lemon and is dusted with icing sugar.
64074.m: Lokum is a soft, sweet treat.

64075.q: What do children often get from relatives at the festival?
64075.e: Children are given presents on the festival day. They often get some pocket money or sweets from relatives.
64075.m: Children often get money or sweets at the festival.

64076.q: Which date-filled biscuits are often baked in the Middle East for the festival?
64076.e: Maamoul are round biscuits made of semolina or flour. They are filled with dates or nuts and decorated with wooden moulds.
64076.m: Maamoul are festival biscuits with a date filling.

64077.q: Why do many people also call the festival of breaking the fast the Sugar Festival?
a: Because people eat and give lots of sweet things
Because sugar is harvested on this day
Because it is white as sugar outside
Because people only drink sugar water
64077.e: At the festival there are pastries, baklava and lots of sweets. Children are often given sweet things, so many people say Sugar Festival.
64077.m: At the Sugar Festival people eat and give lots of sweet things.

64078.q: What do many Muslims also give their neighbours at the festival?
64078.e: At the festival you share your joy with others. Many people bring their neighbours a plate of pastries, even if they have a different religion.
64078.m: At the festival many Muslims bring their neighbours sweets.

64079.q: What do some families send to friends and relatives for the festival?
64079.e: With a greetings card or a message you wish everyone a happy festival. They often have crescent moons and stars on them.
64079.m: People send greetings cards for the festival.

64080.q: What is halva, which people also like to eat at festivals?
64080.e: Halva is often made from sesame paste and sugar. It is sweet and crumbles easily in your mouth.
64080.m: Halva is a sweet made from sesame.

64081.q: Who do many Muslims visit on the festival day?
64081.e: On the festival day people are out and about a lot. They visit relatives and friends and celebrate together.
64081.m: On the festival day people visit relatives and friends.

64082.q: Who do younger people often visit first on the festival day?
a: The neighbour in the next village
64082.e: Older people are especially honoured on the festival day. That is why many people go to their parents and grandparents first.
64082.m: On the festival day you visit your parents and grandparents first.

64083.q: What do children in Turkey often do when they greet older relatives at the festival?
64083.e: The children kiss the older person's hand and raise it to their forehead. This is a sign of respect.
64083.m: In Turkey children kiss the hands of older people at the festival.

64084.q: What should you do on the festival day with people you have argued with?
64084.e: The festival is a time of peace. People shake hands and forgive each other.
64084.m: On the festival day you make up after an argument.

64085.q: Which places do some families visit on the festival day to remember those who have died?
64085.e: In many families people also go to the cemetery on the festival day. There they pray for relatives who have died.
64085.m: Some families visit their relatives' graves on the festival day.

64086.q: How do many families in Switzerland celebrate with relatives who live far away?
64086.e: Many Muslims in Switzerland have relatives in other countries. On the festival day they phone them and see each other by video.
64086.m: With relatives far away people celebrate by phone or video.

64087.q: What are guests often offered on a festival visit?
64087.e: Guests are very welcome on the festival day. Drinks and sweets are put on the table for them.
64087.m: At the festival guests are offered tea, coffee and sweet things.

64088.q: What do many families eat together after the festival prayer?
64088.e: After the morning prayer the family gets together. There is a rich breakfast with lots of treats.
64088.m: After the festival prayer the family eats a big breakfast.

64089.q: In many cantons, how can Muslim schoolchildren get the festival day off?
a: They never get the day off
All of Switzerland has the day off
64089.e: The festival is not an official public holiday in Switzerland. But in many cantons parents can apply for a day off for important religious festivals.
64089.m: In many cantons parents can submit a request for the festival day.

64090.q: What do guests often bring on a festival visit?
64090.e: People who come to visit like to bring something. Often it is a box of chocolates or pastries.
64090.m: Guests often bring a small present on a festival visit.

64091.q: What does the Arabic word “halal” mean?
64091.e: “Halal” means “allowed”. Halal is everything Muslims may eat and do according to their rules.

64092.q: What is the opposite of halal called?
64092.e: “Haram” means “forbidden”. Believing Muslims should not eat or do what is haram.
64092.m: Haram is the opposite of halal and means forbidden.

64093.q: Which drink is not halal for believing Muslims?
64093.e: Alcohol is forbidden in Islam. That is why believing Muslims do not drink wine or beer.
64093.m: Alcoholic drinks are not allowed in Islam.

64094.q: How can you often recognise halal food in a shop?
64094.e: Many halal products have a special symbol or seal on the packaging. That way you can quickly see that the food follows the rules.
64094.m: A halal symbol on the packaging helps when shopping.

64095.q: Are Muslims allowed to eat vegetables and fruit?
64095.e: Plant foods such as vegetables, fruit and grain are allowed in principle. So they are halal.

64096.q: Which meat do believing Muslims not eat?
64096.e: Pork is forbidden in Islam. Chicken, beef or lamb is halal if the animal was slaughtered according to Islamic rules.
64096.m: Believing Muslims do not eat pork.

64097.q: What may most Muslims eat even if it was not specially slaughtered?
64097.e: Most Muslims consider fish and other seafood halal, even without special slaughter. For mammals and poultry, however, there are rules.

64098.q: Where does a large share of the halal meat in Switzerland come from?
64098.e: In Switzerland it is forbidden to slaughter mammals without stunning them. That is why a lot of halal meat is imported from other countries.
64098.m: A lot of halal meat in Switzerland is imported.

64099.q: Are people of other religions allowed to eat halal food too?
64099.e: Halal food is perfectly normal food that meets certain rules. Everyone may eat it.

64100.q: What about alcohol in a sauce for believing Muslims?
64100.e: For many believing Muslims, alcohol in food such as sauces or cakes is also not allowed.
64100.m: Many Muslims also avoid alcohol in food.

64101.q: Which food comes from the pig?
64101.e: Bacon is made from pork. That is why believing Muslims do not eat bacon.

64102.q: Why do some Muslims not eat ordinary gummy bears?
64102.e: Many gummy bears contain gelatine, which is often made from pig skin. But there are also gummy bears without pork gelatine.

64103.q: Which ham may Muslims eat if the animal was slaughtered correctly?
64103.e: Turkey ham is made from turkey meat. If it is halal, Muslims may eat it.

64104.q: Which other religion also forbids pork?
64104.e: Pork is also forbidden in Judaism, where it is likewise part of the food laws. The rules of the two religions are similar here.
64104.m: Jews do not eat pork either.

64105.q: What is the rule about pork if someone would otherwise starve?
64105.e: Islamic rules make an exception: in great need you may eat forbidden food to survive. Life is more important.
64105.m: In great need, eating forbidden food is allowed.

64106.q: Which fat comes from the pig?
64106.e: Lard is melted-down fat from pigs. It is sometimes used for baking and frying.

64107.q: Does the ban also apply to meat from wild boar?
64107.e: A wild boar is a pig too. So the ban applies to wild boar meat as well.
64107.m: Wild boar meat is also forbidden for Muslims.

64108.q: What can a school kitchen offer Muslim children?
64108.e: Many schools and after-school clubs offer a meal without pork. That way all the children can eat together.
64108.m: A meal without pork suits Muslim children.

64109.q: Which sausage is usually not allowed for Muslims?
64109.e: Salami is often made from pork. But there are also halal sausages made from beef or poultry.
64109.m: Believing Muslims do not eat pork sausages.

64110.q: How do many Muslims greet each other?
64110.e: “Salam aleikum” is the well-known greeting of Muslims all over the world. Many people say it in Switzerland too.
64110.m: Muslims often greet each other with “Salam aleikum”.

64111.q: What does “Salam aleikum” mean in English?
64111.e: With this greeting you wish others peace. It is said when greeting someone.
64111.m: Salam aleikum means “peace be with you”.

64112.q: What do you reply to “Salam aleikum”?
64112.e: The reply is “Wa aleikum salam”. The other answers are different Arabic words and do not fit here.
64112.m: You reply to “Salam aleikum” with “Wa aleikum salam”.

64113.q: What does the reply “Wa aleikum salam” mean?
64113.e: You return the greeting of peace. That way both people wish each other peace.
64113.m: With the reply you wish the other person peace too.

64114.e: “Salam aleikum” is a greeting. You say it when you meet someone or enter a room.
64114.m: You say Salam aleikum when greeting someone.

64115.q: Which Jewish greeting is related to “Salam”?
64115.e: The Hebrew “Shalom” and the Arabic “Salam” have the same root. Both mean “peace”.
64115.m: Shalom and Salam both mean peace.

64116.q: What do Muslims say at the end of prayer when they turn their head to the right and left?
64116.e: At the end of prayer you turn your head to the right and to the left and say the greeting of peace. This is how the prayer is finished.
64116.m: Prayer ends with the greeting of peace.

64117.q: How can you say the greeting “Salam aleikum” in short?
64117.e: Among friends many people simply say “Salam”. That is the short form of the greeting.
64117.m: Salam is the short form of the greeting.

64118.e: Before eating many Muslims say “Bismillah”, which means “In the name of God”. So they begin the meal in the name of God.
64118.m: Many Muslims say Bismillah before eating.

64119.q: What do almost all surahs, the chapters of the Quran, begin with?
64119.e: Almost every surah begins with the sentence “In the name of God, the Most Merciful, the Most Gracious”. It stands at the start, before the first verse.
64119.m: Almost every surah begins with Bismillah.

64120.q: How does the whole sentence go on: “In the name of God, the Most ...”?
64120.e: The whole sentence is “In the name of God, the Most Merciful, the Most Gracious”. Merciful means that God has compassion and is kind.
64120.m: The sentence calls God the Most Merciful.

64121.q: What is another name for the Bismillah sentence?
64121.e: The sentence is also called the “Basmala”. That is its name in books about Islam.
64121.m: The Bismillah sentence is also called the Basmala.

64122.q: A Muslim child is starting their homework. What can they say first?
64122.e: Many Muslims say “Bismillah” at the start of a task. So they begin the work in the name of God.
64122.m: You say Bismillah at the start of a task.

64123.q: What do many Muslims say after eating?
64123.e: “Alhamdulillah” means “thank God” or “praise be to God”. After eating, people use it to give thanks for the meal.
64123.m: Many Muslims say Alhamdulillah after eating.

64124.e: The tasbih is a string of beads. Muslims use it to count words of prayer.
64124.m: The tasbih is a string of prayer beads.

64125.q: How many beads does a long Muslim string of prayer beads often have?
64125.e: A long tasbih often has 99 beads. There are usually also dividing beads and a longer end bead.
64125.m: A long string of prayer beads often has 99 beads.

64126.q: What do the beads of a long string of prayer beads remind people of?
64126.e: In Islam people speak of the 99 most beautiful names of God, for example “the Most Merciful”. The beads are a reminder of them.
64126.m: The beads are a reminder of the beautiful names of God.

64127.q: How many beads does a short string of prayer beads often have?
64127.e: A short tasbih often has 33 beads. You then go through it three times.
64127.m: A short string of prayer beads often has 33 beads.

64128.q: A child counts 33 beads three times. How many beads is that?
64128.e: 33 + 33 + 33 = 99. You can also work it out like this: 3 times 33 makes 99.

64129.q: What do Muslims use prayer beads for?
64129.e: With each bead you say a short word of praise for God. That way you do not lose track while counting.
64129.m: Prayer beads are used to count words of prayer.

64130.e: “Subhanallah” is a word of praise for God. Many Muslims say it 33 times with their prayer beads.

64131.q: What can the beads of a string of prayer beads be made of?
64131.e: Prayer beads are often made of wood, stone, glass or plastic. These materials are hard and last a long time.
64131.m: Prayer beads are often made of wood or stone.

64132.q: Which string of prayer beads do many Christians know?
64132.e: Catholic Christians pray with the rosary. It too has beads for counting prayers.
64132.m: The rosary is the string of prayer beads of many Christians.

64133.q: What else can you count the words of praise with if you have no prayer beads?
64133.e: Many Muslims count the words of praise on their fingers. The Prophet Muhammad himself is said to have counted like this.
64133.m: You can also count the words of praise on your fingers.

64134.q: What do many Muslim women wear as a sign of their faith?
64134.e: Many Muslim women wear a headscarf. For them it is a sign of their faith.
64134.m: For many Muslim women the headscarf is a sign of faith.

64135.q: What is the Muslim women's headscarf called in Arabic?
64135.e: The Arabic word “hijab” means “cover” or “curtain”. Today it usually means the headscarf.
64135.m: The headscarf is called hijab in Arabic.

64136.q: What does a headscarf mainly cover?
64136.e: The headscarf covers the hair and often the neck too. The face stays uncovered.

64137.q: Do all Muslim women wear a headscarf?
a: No, some do not wear one
64137.e: Muslim women make different choices. Some wear a headscarf, others do not.
64137.m: Not all Muslim women wear a headscarf.

64138.q: Where do many women usually take off their headscarf?
64138.e: The headscarf is worn mainly outside and in front of men who are not family. At home with the family it is usually not needed.
64138.m: At home with the family the headscarf is often taken off.

64139.q: When do many Muslim women who do not wear a headscarf every day also cover their hair?
64139.e: Women cover their hair when praying. Many who do not otherwise wear a headscarf do this too.
64139.m: Women cover their hair when praying.

64140.q: What has FIFA, the world football association, allowed since 2014?
64140.e: Since 2014 female footballers have been allowed to wear a headscarf in official matches. There are special sports headscarves for this.
64140.m: Since 2014 female footballers have been allowed to play in a headscarf.

64141.q: Which Christian women often wear a veil on their head?
64141.e: Many nuns wear a veil over their hair. In Christianity too, a head covering can be a sign of faith.
64141.m: Many nuns also cover their hair.

64142.q: Do headscarves only come in black?
64142.e: Headscarves come in many colours and patterns. Every woman can choose what she likes.

64143.q: What do some Muslim men wear on their head when praying?
a: A woolly hat with a bobble
64143.e: Some men wear a small round cap when praying. It is not a must, but a custom.
64143.m: Some men wear a prayer cap when praying.

64144.q: What is the shared prayer on the most important prayer day of the week called?
64144.e: Friday prayer is the most important shared prayer of the week. It takes place in the mosque.
64144.m: Friday prayer is the most important shared prayer of the week.

64145.q: At what time of day does Friday prayer take place?
64145.e: On Fridays the Friday prayer replaces the midday prayer. So it takes place around midday.

64146.q: What does the Arabic name for Friday mean?
64146.e: Friday is called “Yawm al-Jumu'a” in Arabic. That means “day of gathering”, because people meet to pray.
64146.m: Friday in Arabic means “day of gathering”.

64147.q: What do you take off before entering the prayer hall?
64147.e: You take your shoes off in the prayer hall. That keeps the carpet you pray on clean.
64147.m: You take your shoes off before the prayer hall.

64148.q: Who calls people to prayer from the tower of a mosque?
64148.e: The muezzin calls people to prayer. He often has a beautiful, loud voice.
64148.m: The muezzin calls people to prayer.

64149.q: How do the men stand during shared prayer in the mosque?
a: One behind the other on their own
64149.e: During shared prayer the worshippers stand shoulder to shoulder in straight rows. Everyone makes the movements at the same time.
64149.m: During shared prayer people stand in straight rows.

64150.q: What is the compulsory donation for the poor in Islam called?
64150.e: Zakat is a compulsory donation. Anyone who has enough money gives part of it to the poor.
64150.m: The compulsory donation in Islam is called zakat.

64151.q: Zakat is one of the pillars of Islam. How many pillars are there?
64151.e: There are five pillars of Islam. They include, for example, prayer, fasting and zakat.
64151.m: Zakat is one of the five pillars of Islam.

64152.q: For the compulsory donation you give 1 franc out of every 40 francs. How much do you give out of 80 francs?
64152.e: 80 francs is twice 40 francs. So you give 1 franc twice, which makes 2 francs.
64152.m: Out of every 40 francs you give 1 franc.

64153.q: What is a voluntary donation called in Islam?
64153.e: Besides the compulsory donation there is the voluntary donation “sadaqa”. You can give it as often as you like.
64153.m: A voluntary donation is called sadaqa.

64154.q: Who receives the money from the compulsory donation?
64154.e: The money is meant for the poor and people in need. That way what people have is shared.
64154.m: The compulsory donation is for poor people.

64155.q: When is the special donation “Zakat al-Fitr” given?
a: At the end of the month of fasting
At the beginning of the year
64155.e: At the end of the month of fasting people give a donation, usually food or money. That way poor people can celebrate the festival too.
64155.m: Zakat al-Fitr is given at the end of the month of fasting.

64156.q: Roughly what does the word “zakat” mean?
64156.e: “Zakat” means roughly “purification” or “growth”. By giving, people are meant to purify their wealth, so to speak.

64157.q: According to a well-known saying of Muhammad, what also counts as a good gift?
64157.e: A well-known saying tells us that even a smile for another person is a good gift. So you can do good without money too.
64157.m: A smile can also be a good gift.

64158.q: How often is the compulsory donation given?
64158.e: The compulsory donation is worked out and given once a year. It depends on how much you have saved.
64158.m: The compulsory donation is given once a year.

64159.q: Do very poor people have to give the compulsory donation too?
a: No, only those who have enough
64159.e: Only people who own more than a certain amount have to give the compulsory donation. Poor people receive it.
64159.m: Only those who own enough give the compulsory donation.

64160.e: Calligraphy is the art of writing letters especially beautifully. In Islam it is a very important art.
64160.m: Calligraphy is the art of beautiful writing.

64161.q: Why do you see lots of writing and no pictures of people in mosques?
a: Pictures of people are not usual there
64161.e: In mosques there are no pictures of people or animals. Instead the rooms are decorated with beautiful writing and patterns.
64161.m: Mosques are decorated with writing instead of pictures of people.

64162.q: What do calligraphers traditionally write with?
64162.e: Traditionally a reed is cut at a slant and dipped in ink. This pen is called a “qalam”.

64163.q: What is often written in Islamic calligraphy?
64163.e: Calligraphers often write verses from the Quran or the names of God. That is why this art is especially precious to Muslims.
64163.m: Calligraphy often shows verses from the Quran.

64165.e: “Inshallah” means “God willing” or “if God wills”. People say it when talking about the future.

64166.e: “Inshallah” is said about plans for the future. “Tomorrow I'm going swimming” is a plan for the future.
64166.m: Inshallah fits plans for the future.

64167.q: Which Spanish word is related to “Inshallah”?
64167.e: The Spanish “ojalá” means “hopefully”. It comes from the Arabic “law sha'a llah”, which means “if God wills”. Many Muslims used to live in Spain.
64167.m: The Spanish word “ojalá” comes from Arabic.

64168.q: What do many Muslims say when they admire something beautiful?
64168.e: “Mashallah” means roughly “what God has willed”. People say it, for example, when a baby is healthy or something has turned out well.
64168.m: You say Mashallah when you admire something beautiful.

64169.q: What does someone show when they say “Inshallah”?
a: That the future is in God's hands
64169.e: With “Inshallah” you say that you cannot decide everything yourself. You trust that God guides the future.
64169.m: Whoever says Inshallah entrusts the future to God.

64170.q: Do only people in Arab countries say “Inshallah”?
a: No, Muslims all over the world
64170.e: Muslims in many countries say “Inshallah”, for example in Turkey, in Bosnia or in Switzerland.
64170.m: Muslims all over the world say Inshallah.

64171.q: How many Arabic words make up “Inshallah”?
64171.e: “Inshallah” is made up of “in” (if), “sha'a” (wills) and “Allah” (God). Together that makes three words.
64171.m: Inshallah is made up of three words.

64172.q: A friend says: “I'll come round to yours tomorrow, inshallah.” What does he mean?
a: He wants to come if nothing gets in the way
64172.e: The friend plans to come. With “inshallah” he says it will work out if God wills it.
64172.m: With inshallah you express an intention for the future.

64173.q: Which word do you often hear when a Muslim sneezes?
64173.e: Whoever sneezes praises God with it. The others reply with a blessing.
64173.m: After sneezing many Muslims say Alhamdulillah.

64174.q: What is food called that Jews may eat according to their food laws?
64174.e: In Judaism, permitted food is called “kosher”. It is similar to halal in Islam, but the rules are not quite the same.
64174.m: In Judaism permitted food is called kosher.

64175.q: What is Friday in many Islamic countries?
64175.e: In many Islamic countries schools and offices are closed on Fridays. In Switzerland Friday is a normal working day.
64175.m: In many Islamic countries Friday is a day off.

64176.q: What is a veil that also covers the face except for the eyes called?
64176.e: The niqab covers the face; only the eyes stay uncovered. Only a few Muslim women wear it.
64176.m: The niqab leaves only the eyes uncovered.

64177.q: What do many Muslims hand out to poor people at the Festival of Sacrifice?
64177.e: At the Festival of Sacrifice an animal is slaughtered. Part of the meat is given to the poor.
64177.m: At the Festival of Sacrifice people share meat with the poor.

64178.q: What does the Arabic farewell “Ma'a salama” mean?
64178.e: “Ma'a salama” literally means “with peace”. You say it when leaving, just like “goodbye”.
64178.m: You say Ma'a salama when saying goodbye.

64179.q: What do almost all surahs of the Quran begin with?
a: With the sentence “In the name of God”
64179.e: Almost every surah begins with the sentence “In the name of God, the Most Merciful, the Most Gracious”. Only the 9th surah begins without this sentence.
64179.m: Almost all surahs begin with “In the name of God”.

64180.e: “Bismillah” means “In the name of God”. Many Muslims say it before eating or before starting work.
64180.m: Bismillah means “In the name of God”.

64181.q: What is another name for the Muslim string of prayer beads?
64181.e: Depending on the country, the prayer beads are called tasbih or misbaha. Both words come from Arabic.
64181.m: The prayer beads are also called misbaha.

64182.q: What do you call an artist who writes letters especially beautifully?
64182.e: A calligrapher is a master of beautiful writing. In the Islamic world calligraphers were highly respected.
64182.m: A calligrapher is an artist of beautiful writing.

64183.q: What did Arabic calligraphers use to write with in the past?
64183.e: Calligraphers wrote with a reed that they sharpened at a slant. This produced thick and thin lines.

64184.q: What do calligraphers sometimes form out of letters?
64184.e: Some calligraphers write words so that together they form the shape of a bird, a lion or a ship. That way writing becomes a picture.
64184.m: You can form pictures out of letters.

64185.q: Which book do Muslim calligraphers copy especially beautifully?
64185.e: The Quran is the holy book for Muslims. That is why calligraphers write it with great care and especially beautifully.
64185.m: Calligraphers write the Quran especially beautifully.

64186.q: How did people learn the art of calligraphy in the past?
a: For many years with a master
In a few days on their own
In a month from a book
64186.e: Calligraphy pupils practised for many years with a master. Only when the master was satisfied were they allowed to sign their own work.
64186.m: People learned calligraphy for many years with a master.

64187.q: What do many Muslims do at home on Friday before prayer?
a: They shower or have a bath
64187.e: On Friday you should wash your whole body before prayer and put on clean, nice clothes. This is an old custom.
64187.m: Before Friday prayer many Muslims wash their whole body.

64188.q: For whom is Friday prayer at the mosque a duty?
64188.e: Friday prayer is a duty for adult men. Women, children, people who are ill and travellers may take part but do not have to.
64188.m: Friday prayer is a duty for adult men.

64189.q: How many units of prayer does the shared Friday prayer have?
64189.e: The shared Friday prayer has two units of prayer. Before it, people listen to the sermon.
64189.m: Friday prayer has two units of prayer.

64190.q: What should people do during the Friday sermon?
64190.e: During the sermon you should be quiet and listen carefully. According to one tradition, you should not even tell off a neighbour then.
64190.m: During the sermon you listen quietly.

64191.q: What is Abraham called in Islam?
64191.e: In the Quran Abraham is called Ibrahim. He is one of the most important prophets in Islam.
64191.m: In Islam Abraham is called Ibrahim.

64192.q: According to the Quran, which building in Mecca did Ibrahim build with his son?
64192.e: According to the Quran, Ibrahim and his son Ismail built the Kaaba in Mecca. Muslims turn towards it when they pray.
64192.m: Ibrahim and Ismail built the Kaaba.

64193.q: What was the name of the son with whom Ibrahim built the Kaaba?
64193.e: The Quran says that Ibrahim and Ismail raised the foundations of the Kaaba. Ismail was the son of Ibrahim and Hajar.
64193.m: Ismail helped his father Ibrahim build the Kaaba.

64194.q: According to the Quran, what happened to the fire into which Ibrahim was thrown?
64194.e: People wanted to burn Ibrahim because he rejected their idols. God commanded the fire to be cool and harmless.
64194.m: The fire became cool and harmless for Ibrahim.

64195.q: In the story, which animal did God send to be sacrificed instead of Ibrahim's son?
64195.e: Ibrahim was ready to sacrifice his son, but God gave him a ram instead. The Festival of Sacrifice is a reminder of this.
64195.m: A ram was sacrificed instead of the son.

64196.q: At which festival do Muslims remember Ibrahim's sacrifice?
a: At the breaking of the fast
64196.e: The Festival of Sacrifice is called Eid al-Adha in Arabic. It recalls Ibrahim's willingness to obey God.
64196.m: The Festival of Sacrifice is a reminder of Ibrahim.

64197.q: What title of honour does Ibrahim have in Islam?
64197.e: In the Quran Ibrahim is called “Khalil Allah”. That means “friend of God”.
64197.m: Ibrahim is called the friend of God.

64198.q: What is the name of the spring in Mecca that, according to tradition, gushed out for Hajar and Ismail?
64198.e: Hajar was looking for water in the desert for her son Ismail. Then the Zamzam spring bubbled up, and pilgrims still drink from it today.
64198.m: The Zamzam spring gave Hajar and Ismail water.

64199.q: Which three religions honour Abraham as an important forefather?
64199.e: Judaism, Christianity and Islam see Abraham as the forefather of their faith. That is why they are called Abrahamic religions.
64199.m: Judaism, Christianity and Islam are Abrahamic religions.

64200.q: What is Noah called in the Quran?
64200.e: In the Quran Noah is called Nuh. He is a prophet the Bible also tells about.
64200.m: In the Quran Noah is called Nuh.

64201.q: What did Nuh build at God's command?
64201.e: God commanded Nuh to build a large ship, the ark. That way he could save himself from the great flood.

64202.q: What did the ark save Nuh and his family from?
64202.e: According to the Quran, God sent a mighty flood. Whoever was in the ark was saved.
64202.m: The ark saved people from the great flood.

64203.q: How many animals of each kind did Nuh take into the ark?
64203.e: God told Nuh to take a pair of every kind. That way the animals could live on after the flood.
64203.m: Nuh took a pair of every kind of animal.

64204.q: In the Quran, who refused to get into the ark?
64204.e: A son of Nuh preferred to save himself on a mountain. He died in the waves.
64204.m: A son of Nuh did not get into the ark.

64205.q: Where did the ark come to rest after the flood?
a: On an island in the sea
In the middle of a desert
64205.e: When the water went down, the ark came to rest on a mountain. The Quran calls it al-Judi, the Bible the mountains of Ararat.
64205.m: The ark came to rest on a mountain.

64206.q: How did many people react when Nuh was building the ark?
64206.e: According to the Quran, many people mocked Nuh when they saw the ship on dry land. They did not listen to his warning.

64207.q: What is the surah of the Quran named after Noah called?
64207.e: The 71st surah of the Quran is called Nuh. It tells how Nuh warned his people.
64207.m: A whole surah bears the name Nuh.

64208.q: According to the Quran, how long did Nuh live among his people?
64208.e: The Quran says Nuh stayed with his people for 1,000 years less 50 years. That is 950 years.
64208.m: In the Quran Nuh lived among his people for 950 years.

64209.q: What is Moses called in the Quran?
64209.e: In the Quran Moses is called Musa. He is a very important prophet.
64209.m: In the Quran Moses is called Musa.

64210.q: According to the Quran, what did Musa's mother put her baby in on the water?
64210.e: In the Quran God tells the mother to put Musa in a chest and set him on the water. She wanted to protect him from Pharaoh. In the Bible it is a little basket.
64210.m: Baby Musa floated on the water in a chest.

64211.q: On which river did baby Musa float?
64211.e: Musa was born in Egypt. The great river of Egypt is the Nile.
64211.m: As a baby Musa floated on the Nile.

64212.q: Who found baby Musa and took him in?
64212.e: Pharaoh's wife found the child and wanted to keep him. So Musa grew up in the palace.

64213.q: What did Musa's staff become when he threw it down at God's command?
64213.e: The staff turned into a snake. That was a sign that God had sent Musa.

64214.q: What happened to the sea when Musa led his people out?
64214.e: Musa struck the sea with his staff, and it parted. So his people could walk through on dry ground.
64214.m: The sea parted for Musa and his people.

64215.q: According to Islam, which holy scripture did Musa receive?
64215.e: According to Islam, God revealed the Torah to Musa, called Tawrat in Arabic. It is also the holy scripture of Judaism.

64216.q: What was the name of Musa's brother who helped him?
64216.e: Musa asked God for help, and his brother Harun was allowed to go with him. In the Bible Harun is called Aaron.

64217.q: Which prophet is mentioned by name most often in the Quran?
64217.e: Musa is mentioned by name more than a hundred times in the Quran. No other prophet appears so often.
64217.m: Musa is the prophet mentioned most often in the Quran.

64218.q: What is Jesus called in the Quran?
64218.e: In the Quran Jesus is called Isa. For Muslims he is an important prophet.
64218.m: In the Quran Jesus is called Isa.

64219.e: In Islam Isa is a great prophet and messenger of God. Unlike in Christianity, he is not seen as the Son of God.
64219.m: For Muslims Isa is a prophet.

64220.q: Who is the mother of Isa?
64220.e: In the Quran Isa's mother is called Maryam. That is why he is often called “Isa, son of Maryam”.

64221.q: According to Islam, which scripture did Isa receive from God?
64221.e: According to Islam, Isa received the Gospel, called Injil in Arabic. The Torah belongs to Musa and the Quran to Muhammad.

64222.q: According to the Quran, what could Isa already do as a baby in the cradle?
64222.e: The Quran tells that baby Isa spoke in the cradle. In this way he defended his mother Maryam.
64222.m: Isa already spoke as a baby in the cradle.

64223.q: According to the Quran, what did Isa shape out of clay?
64223.e: Isa shaped birds out of clay and breathed on them. With God's permission they became living birds.
64223.m: With God's permission Isa shaped living birds out of clay.

64224.q: According to the Quran, whom did Isa heal with God's permission?
64224.e: The Quran tells that Isa healed the blind and the sick. He always did this with God's permission.
64224.m: Isa healed blind people with God's permission.

64225.q: Which title of honour does Isa have in the Quran?
64225.e: In the Quran Isa is called “al-Masih”. That means Messiah, the anointed one.
64225.m: In the Quran Isa has the title Messiah.

64226.q: What do Muslims believe about Isa's future?
a: He will become King of Rome
He is sleeping in a cave
64226.e: Many Muslims believe that Isa will return at the end of time. This teaching comes from tradition.

64227.q: What is Mary called in the Quran?
64227.e: Mary, the mother of Jesus, is called Maryam in the Quran. Muslims hold her in very high regard.
64227.m: In the Quran Mary is called Maryam.

64228.q: Which woman is the only one mentioned by name in the Quran?
64228.e: Maryam is the only woman whose name appears in the Quran. Other women are only described.
64228.m: Maryam is the only woman named in the Quran.

64229.q: Which woman has her own surah in the Quran bearing her name?
64229.e: The 19th surah is called Maryam. It is the only surah named after a woman and tells of the birth of Isa.
64229.m: One surah in the Quran is called Maryam.

64230.q: According to the Quran, under which tree did Maryam give birth to Isa?
64230.e: The Quran tells that Maryam leaned against the trunk of a date palm. Isa was born there.
64230.m: Isa was born under a date palm.

64231.q: According to the Quran, what was Maryam to eat from the palm?
64231.e: God told Maryam to shake the palm. Then fresh dates fell down for her.
64231.m: Maryam ate fresh dates from the palm.

64232.q: Who brought Maryam the news that she would have a child?
64232.e: The angel Jibril, Gabriel in English, came to Maryam. He announced the birth of Isa to her.
64232.m: An angel brought Maryam the news.

64233.q: According to the Quran, which prophet looked after the young Maryam?
64233.e: Zakariya was responsible for the young Maryam. He was also the father of the prophet Yahya.

64234.q: According to the Quran, where did the food Maryam received in the temple come from?
64234.e: Whenever Zakariya came to Maryam, he found food with her. Maryam said the food came from God.
64234.m: Maryam received her food from God.

64235.q: How is Maryam described in Islam?
64235.e: In the Quran Maryam is honoured as a pure and God-fearing woman. She is seen as one of the best women.
64235.m: Maryam is greatly honoured in Islam.

64236.q: Muhammad came to Medina in 622 and died there in 632. How many years did he live in Medina?
64236.e: 632 minus 622 makes 10. So Muhammad lived in Medina for about ten years.
64236.m: Muhammad lived in Medina for about ten years.

64237.q: What is Medina often also called?
64237.e: Muhammad lived the last years of his life in Medina. That is why Muslims often call it the City of the Prophet.
64237.m: Medina is also called the City of the Prophet.

64238.q: Where did Muhammad move to from Mecca in the year 622?
64238.e: In 622 Muhammad emigrated with his followers from Mecca to Medina. In Medina they were welcomed warmly.

64239.q: What is Muhammad's emigration to Medina called?
64239.e: The emigration from Mecca to Medina is called the Hijra. The word means emigration.
64239.m: The emigration to Medina is called the Hijra.

64240.q: Which mosque near Medina is considered the first mosque of Islam?
64240.e: On the way to Medina, Muhammad founded the Quba Mosque. It is considered the first mosque of Islam.
64240.m: The Quba Mosque is considered the first mosque of Islam.

64241.q: Which mosque stands in the centre of Medina?
64241.e: The Prophet's Mosque was founded by Muhammad. It is one of the largest mosques in the world.
64241.m: The Prophet's Mosque stands in Medina.

64242.q: What colour is the famous dome over Muhammad's tomb in Medina?
64242.e: The Green Dome rises over the Prophet's tomb in the Prophet's Mosque. It is a well-known landmark of Medina.
64242.m: The Green Dome stands over Muhammad's tomb.

64243.e: Muhammad died in Medina in the year 632. His tomb is in the Prophet's Mosque.

64244.q: What does the Arabic word “Medina” mean?
64244.e: In Arabic Medina simply means “the city”. It refers to the City of the Prophet, which used to be called Yathrib.

64245.q: In which city is the Dome of the Rock?
64245.e: The Dome of the Rock stands in the Old City of Jerusalem. It is one of the most famous buildings in the city.
64245.m: The Dome of the Rock is in Jerusalem.

64246.q: What colour is the dome of the Dome of the Rock?
64246.e: The dome of the Dome of the Rock is covered in gold. It shines far over the city.
64246.m: The Dome of the Rock has a golden dome.

64247.q: How many corners does the floor plan of the Dome of the Rock have?
64247.e: The Dome of the Rock is an octagon. Each of the eight outer walls is the same length.
64247.m: The Dome of the Rock has eight corners.

64248.q: What lies under the dome of the Dome of the Rock?
64248.e: The building stands over a large, holy rock. That is where it gets its name.
64248.m: A holy rock lies under the dome.

64249.q: On which hill in Jerusalem does the Dome of the Rock stand?
64249.e: The Dome of the Rock stands on the Temple Mount, which Muslims call Haram al-Sharif. The Jewish Temple used to stand there.
64249.m: The Dome of the Rock stands on the Temple Mount.

64250.q: Roughly how old is the Dome of the Rock in Jerusalem?
64250.e: The caliph Abd al-Malik had the Dome of the Rock built. It was finished around the year 691, which makes it over 1,300 years old.
64250.m: The Dome of the Rock is over 1,300 years old.

64251.q: According to tradition, which journey of Muhammad is linked to the rock?
64251.e: According to tradition, on his night journey Muhammad rose to heaven from this rock. This journey to heaven is called the Miraj.
64251.m: The rock is a reminder of Muhammad's journey to heaven.

64252.q: For how many major religions is Jerusalem a holy city?
64252.e: Jerusalem is holy for Jews, Christians and Muslims. That is why the city is very important to many people.
64252.m: Jerusalem is holy to three religions.

64253.q: Which colour dominates the tiles on the outer walls of the Dome of the Rock?
64253.e: The outer walls are decorated with lots of blue tiles. They show patterns and writing.
64253.m: The walls of the Dome of the Rock are covered in blue tiles.

64254.q: In which canton is the mosque of Wangen bei Olten with its minaret?
64254.e: Wangen bei Olten is a municipality in the canton of Solothurn. The mosque's minaret was put up in 2009.
64254.m: Wangen bei Olten is in the canton of Solothurn.

64255.q: What was the Mahmud Mosque in Zurich when it opened in 1963?
a: The first mosque with a minaret in Switzerland
The largest mosque in the world
64255.e: The Mahmud Mosque was the first mosque building with a minaret in Switzerland. It opened in 1963.
64255.m: The first mosque with a minaret in Switzerland is in Zurich.

64256.q: In which Swiss city is the Great Mosque that opened in 1978?
64256.e: The mosque in Geneva opened in 1978. It has a minaret and is one of the largest mosques in Switzerland.
64256.m: A large mosque from 1978 stands in Geneva.

64257.q: What may no longer be built in Switzerland since the vote of 2009?
64257.e: In 2009 the voters accepted the minaret initiative. Since then the Federal Constitution has said that no new minarets may be built.
64257.m: Since 2009 no new minarets may be built in Switzerland.

64258.q: How many mosques in Switzerland have a minaret?
64258.e: In the whole of Switzerland there are only four mosques with a minaret: in Zurich, Geneva, Winterthur and Wangen bei Olten.
64258.m: Only four mosques in Switzerland have a minaret.

64259.q: Apart from Zurich, in which town in the canton of Zurich is there a mosque with a minaret?
64259.e: Winterthur also has a mosque with a small minaret. It was built before the minaret ban.
64259.m: Winterthur has a mosque with a minaret.

64260.q: What is a building where Muslims pray together called?
64260.e: Muslims pray together in a mosque. There are many mosques in Switzerland, but only a few have a minaret.

64261.q: Where are most Muslim prayer rooms in Switzerland?
a: In converted buildings without a minaret
64261.e: Only a few mosques in Switzerland were built as mosques. Most prayer rooms are in converted flats, shops or halls.
64261.m: Most prayer rooms in Switzerland are in converted buildings.

64262.q: What is the niche in the mosque wall that shows the direction of prayer called?
64262.e: The mihrab is a niche in the wall. It shows in which direction Mecca lies.
64262.m: The mihrab shows the direction of prayer.

64263.q: In which city in Morocco is the Hassan II Mosque, with one of the tallest minarets in the world?
64263.e: The Hassan II Mosque stands in Casablanca right by the sea. Its minaret is over 200 metres tall.
64263.m: The Hassan II Mosque is in Casablanca.

64264.q: What is the famous building in Istanbul with a huge dome that used to be a church called?
64264.e: Hagia Sophia was built as a church and later became a mosque. Its huge dome was a model for many mosques.
64264.m: Hagia Sophia has a huge dome.

64265.q: How many times a day is the call to prayer traditionally made?
64265.e: Muslims pray five times a day. Before each prayer the call to prayer rings out.
64265.m: The call to prayer is made five times a day.

64266.e: A dome is a round, curved part of a roof. It looks like half a ball.
64266.m: A dome looks like half a ball.

64267.q: How many minarets does the Blue Mosque in Istanbul have?
64267.e: The Sultan Ahmed Mosque, also called the Blue Mosque, has six minarets. When it was built, that was something very special.
64267.m: The Blue Mosque has six minarets.

64268.q: Why is the Sultan Ahmed Mosque in Istanbul also called the Blue Mosque?
a: Because it stands by the sea
Because of blue carpets at the door
64268.e: Inside the mosque the walls are covered with lots of blue and white tiles. That is where the name Blue Mosque comes from.
64268.m: Blue tiles gave the Blue Mosque its name.

64269.q: In which country is the Taj Mahal with its great white dome?
64269.e: The Taj Mahal stands in Agra in India. It is a tomb with a large dome and four minarets.
64269.m: The Taj Mahal is in India.

64270.q: What is the advantage of a dome inside a building?
a: More room for windows in the floor
64270.e: A dome can span a large room. So no supports are needed in the middle.
64270.m: A dome spans large rooms without pillars.

64271.q: Which language does the word “minaret” come from?
64271.e: “Minaret” comes from the Arabic word “manara”. It means roughly “place of light” or “lighthouse”.
64271.m: The word minaret comes from Arabic.

64272.q: In which country is the Alhambra?
64272.e: The Alhambra is in Spain. For a long time Muslim kings ruled there.

64273.e: The name comes from the Arabic “al-hamra”, which means “the red one”. The walls glow reddish in the sun.

64274.e: The Alhambra is a large complex of fortress and palaces. The Muslim rulers of Granada lived there.
64274.m: The Alhambra is a fortress with palaces.

64276.q: How many lions hold up the fountain in the Court of the Lions?
64276.e: The fountain rests on twelve marble lions. They stand in a circle around the water basin.
64276.m: Twelve lions hold up the fountain.

64277.q: What can you see especially often in the Alhambra?
64277.e: The Alhambra has lots of fountains, channels and pools. The water cools the air and splashes soothingly.
64277.m: There is a lot of water in the Alhambra.

64278.e: The Alhambra was built by Muslim rulers in Spain. They lived there with their court in splendid palaces.
64278.m: Muslim rulers had the Alhambra built.

64280.q: What are mosques often decorated with?
64280.e: In mosques there are usually no pictures of people or animals. Instead patterns, twining plants and beautiful writing decorate the walls.
64280.m: Mosques are decorated with patterns and writing.

64281.q: What do you call a pattern whose left and right halves look the same?
64281.e: If you can mirror a pattern down the middle and both sides are the same, it is symmetrical. Islamic ornaments are often very symmetrical.
64281.m: A symmetrical pattern has two matching halves.

64282.q: What are intertwining plant tendrils used as decoration called?
64282.e: Arabesques are patterns of tendrils, leaves and flowers. They seem to grow on endlessly.
64282.m: Arabesques are patterns of plant tendrils.

64283.q: Which shape appears especially often in Islamic patterns?
64283.e: Many Islamic patterns are built up from stars with six, eight or more points. In between there are polygons.
64283.m: Stars are common in Islamic patterns.

64284.q: Which tools do you use to draw geometric patterns accurately?
64284.e: With compasses and a ruler you can draw circles and straight lines accurately. Stars and polygons are made from them.
64284.m: Geometric patterns are drawn with compasses and a ruler.

64285.q: What are many patterns on mosque walls made of?
64285.e: Many walls are covered with tiles of fired clay. The tiles are painted and glazed.
64285.m: Colourful tiles make up many patterns in mosques.

64286.q: What is typical of geometric patterns in Islamic art?
64286.e: The patterns repeat and could go on for ever. This is meant to remind people of God's infinity.

64287.q: What are the honeycomb-like decorations on ceilings and arches, for example in the Alhambra, called?
64287.e: Muqarnas are many small niches stacked on top of each other. They look like honeycombs or stalactites.
64287.m: Muqarnas look like honeycombs on the ceiling.

64288.q: What are pictures made of many small coloured stones called?
64288.e: A mosaic is made of lots of small stones or pieces of glass. The Dome of the Rock also has magnificent mosaics.
64288.m: A mosaic is made of lots of small stones.

64289.q: Which shapes make up an eight-pointed star, as often seen in mosques?
64289.e: If you lay two squares of the same size on top of each other and turn one by half a corner, you get a star with eight points. This shape is very popular in Islamic art.
64289.m: Two turned squares make an eight-pointed star.

64290.q: What is the holy scroll called that is read aloud in the synagogue?
64290.e: The Torah scroll contains the most important texts of Judaism. It is read aloud during the service.
64290.m: The Torah scroll is the holy scroll of Judaism.

64291.q: What material is a Torah scroll written on?
64291.e: A Torah scroll is written on parchment. Parchment is made from animal skin and lasts a very long time.
64291.m: The Torah scroll is made of parchment.

64292.q: How many books of Moses are there in the Torah?
64292.e: The Torah is made up of the five books of Moses. That is why it is also called the “five books”.

64293.q: What do people use to point at the lines of the Torah scroll while reading?
64293.e: The holy scripture should not be touched with the fingers. That is why a pointer called a yad is used, which often looks like a little hand.
64293.m: A pointer called a yad helps with reading the Torah.

64294.q: How is a Torah scroll made?
64294.e: A specially trained scribe writes every letter by hand. A whole scroll often takes him many months.
64294.m: A Torah scroll is written entirely by hand.

64295.q: Where is the Torah scroll kept in the synagogue?
64295.e: The Torah ark is a beautiful cupboard on the wall of the synagogue. The Torah scroll stands in it when it is not being read.
64295.m: The Torah scroll lives in the Torah ark.

64296.q: Around how many wooden rods is a Torah scroll wound?
64296.e: The scroll is attached to two wooden rods. While reading, you roll it from one rod onto the other.
64296.m: A Torah scroll has two wooden rods.

64297.q: At what age does a Jewish boy read from the Torah for the first time at his Bar Mitzvah?
64297.e: At 13 a boy celebrates his Bar Mitzvah. From then on he counts as an adult in his religion and may read from the Torah.
64297.m: At 13 a Jewish boy celebrates his Bar Mitzvah.

64298.q: On which evening does the Sabbath begin?
64298.e: A Jewish day begins in the evening. That is why the Sabbath starts on Friday evening at sunset.
64298.m: The Sabbath begins on Friday evening.

64299.e: The Sabbath lasts a whole day. It ends on Saturday evening when the first stars appear in the sky.
64299.m: The Sabbath ends on Saturday evening.

64300.q: What do people not do on the Sabbath?
64300.e: The Sabbath is a day of rest. People do not work and have time for family, prayer and relaxing.
64300.m: On the Sabbath people rest from work.

64301.q: According to the creation story, on which day did God rest?
64301.e: In the creation story God creates the world in six days. On the seventh day he rests, and the Sabbath remembers this.
64301.m: The Sabbath remembers God's day of rest.

64302.q: How many candles are usually lit for the Sabbath?
64302.e: Usually two Sabbath candles burn on the table. Some families also light an extra candle for each child.
64302.m: Usually two candles shine for the Sabbath.

64303.q: When are the Sabbath candles lit?
64303.e: The candles are lit on Friday shortly before sunset. In this way the Sabbath begins in light.
64303.m: The Sabbath candles are lit shortly before sunset.

64304.q: Which greeting do people use to wish each other a good Sabbath?
64304.e: On the Sabbath people greet each other with “Shabbat Shalom”. It means something like “a peaceful Sabbath”.
64304.m: On the Sabbath people say “Shabbat Shalom”.

64305.q: Over which drink is a blessing said on Friday evening?
64305.e: On Friday evening a blessing is said over a cup of wine or grape juice. This blessing is called Kiddush.
64305.m: Kiddush is a blessing over wine or grape juice.

64306.q: What is the plaited bread eaten on the Sabbath called?
64306.e: Challah is a fine, plaited bread. It is part of every Sabbath meal.
64306.m: On the Sabbath people eat challah.

64307.q: Which Swiss bread does challah look very much like?
64307.e: Like the Swiss Sunday Zopf, challah is plaited from strands of dough. Both breads are soft and light.

64308.q: How many plaited loaves are on the table on the Sabbath?
64308.e: For the Sabbath meal two plaited loaves, the challot, are placed on the table. A blessing is said over these loaves.
64308.m: On the Sabbath there are two loaves on the table.

64309.q: Which food from the desert do the Sabbath loaves remind people of?
64309.e: According to the Bible, God gave the people manna to eat in the desert. The loaves on the Sabbath table are a reminder of this.
64309.m: The Sabbath loaves are a reminder of the manna in the desert.

64310.q: What are the loaves covered with before the blessing?
64310.e: The challot are covered with a beautiful, often embroidered cloth. The cloth is only taken off for the blessing.
64310.m: The challah lies under a beautiful cloth.

64311.q: What shape is challah often for the Jewish New Year?
64311.e: For the New Year festival, Rosh Hashanah, challah is often baked round. The round shape stands for the year turning in a circle.
64311.m: At New Year challah is often round.

64312.q: What do people like to dip challah in for the Jewish New Year?
64312.e: At New Year people dip bread and apples in honey. It is a wish for a sweet new year.
64312.m: Honey wishes for a sweet new year.

64313.q: How many candles does a Hanukkah candlestick have, including the helper candle?
64313.e: The Hanukkah candlestick has eight candles for the eight evenings and one helper candle. That makes nine altogether.
64313.m: The Hanukkah candlestick has nine places for candles.

64314.q: What is the candle called that is used to light the other Hanukkah candles?
64314.e: The helper candle is called the shamash, which means “servant”. It often stands a bit higher or to one side.
64314.m: The shamash lights the other candles.

64315.q: How many days does Hanukkah last?
64315.e: Hanukkah is celebrated for eight days. Each evening another candle is added.

64316.q: How many candles burn on the first evening of Hanukkah, not counting the helper candle?
64316.e: On the first evening one candle is lit, on the second two, and so on. On the last evening they all burn.
64316.m: Each Hanukkah evening one more candle is added.

64317.e: At Hanukkah lights are lit every evening. That is why it is also called the Festival of Lights.
64317.m: Hanukkah is the Jewish Festival of Lights.

64318.q: In which season is Hanukkah celebrated?
64318.e: Hanukkah usually falls in December. Then the days are short and the lights shine especially beautifully.

64319.q: What do people especially like to eat at Hanukkah?
64319.e: At Hanukkah people like to eat doughnuts and potato pancakes. They are fried in oil because oil is important in the Hanukkah story.
64319.m: At Hanukkah people like to eat food fried in oil.

64320.q: Where is the Hanukkah candlestick often placed?
64320.e: Many people put the candlestick in the window. That way people outside can also see the lights.
64320.m: The Hanukkah candlestick often stands in the window.

64321.q: What kind of toy is a dreidel?
64321.e: A dreidel is a small spinning top. You spin it and see which side it lands on.
64321.m: A dreidel is a spinning top.

64322.q: How many sides with letters does a dreidel have?
64322.e: A dreidel has four sides. On each side there is a Hebrew letter.

64323.q: At which festival do Jewish children play with a dreidel?
64323.e: The dreidel game belongs to the winter evenings when the lights are burning. It is the typical Hanukkah game.
64323.m: The dreidel is played at Hanukkah.

64324.q: What do children often play for with the dreidel?
64324.e: People often play for chocolate coins or nuts. If you are lucky, you win lots of them.
64324.m: With the dreidel people often play for chocolate coins.

64325.q: What do the letters on the dreidel mean together?
64325.e: The four letters are the first letters of four Hebrew words. They mean “A great miracle happened there”.
64325.m: The dreidel tells of a great miracle.

64326.q: In the dreidel game, what happens when the top lands on gimel?
64326.e: Gimel is the best spin. Whoever spins it gets everything in the middle.
64326.m: Gimel wins everything in the dreidel game.

64327.q: In the dreidel game, what happens when the top lands on nun?
64327.e: With nun nothing happens. It is the next player's turn.
64327.m: With nun the game simply carries on.

64328.q: How many cups of wine or grape juice are drunk on Seder night?
64328.e: During the Seder people drink four cups of wine or grape juice. Each cup stands for a promise of freedom.
64328.m: On Seder night people drink four cups.

a: A plaited yeast loaf with raisins
64329.e: Matzah is a thin, crispy bread. The dough must not rise, so it contains no yeast and no sourdough.
64329.m: Matzah is a flat bread without yeast.

64330.q: Why do people eat matzah at Passover?
a: The dough had no time to rise
64330.e: When the people left Egypt, everything had to happen very quickly. The bread dough had no time to rise.
64330.m: Matzah is a reminder of the hurried departure.

64331.q: What is the festive evening at the start of Passover called?
64331.e: On Seder night the family sits together and tells the story of the exodus. Seder means “order”.

64332.q: Who asks the well-known questions on Seder night?
64332.e: The youngest child asks why this night is different from all other nights. The adults answer with the story of the exodus.
64332.m: On Seder night the youngest child asks.

64333.q: In which season is Passover celebrated?
64333.e: Passover is in March or April. It often falls close to Easter.

64334.q: What do the bitter herbs at the Seder remind people of?
64334.e: The bitter herbs taste sharp. They are a reminder of the bitter time when the people were slaves in Egypt.
64334.m: Bitter herbs are a reminder of slavery.

64335.q: At which Jewish festival do children dress up?
64335.e: At Purim children and adults dress up. It is a cheerful festival with games and plays.

64336.q: Which queen is the heroine of the Purim story?
64336.e: Queen Esther saved her people from an evil plan. Her story is in the Book of Esther.
64336.m: Esther is the heroine of Purim.

64337.q: What is the villain in the Purim story called?
64337.e: Haman wanted to harm all the Jews in the land. Queen Esther was able to stop his plan.
64337.m: Haman is the villain of the Purim story.

64338.q: What do children do when the name Haman is read out?
64338.e: When the name Haman is read out, everyone makes noise with rattles and stamping. This is to drown out his name.
64338.m: At Haman's name everyone makes noise.

64339.q: What shape are hamantaschen, a pastry eaten at Purim?
64339.e: Hamantaschen are triangular pastries. They are often filled with poppy seeds, jam or chocolate.

64340.q: What do people give each other at Purim?
64340.e: At Purim people bring friends and neighbours small parcels of food and sweets. They also give gifts to the poor.
64340.m: At Purim people give each other food.

64341.q: In which country does the Purim story take place?
64341.e: The story of Esther takes place at the court of the king of Persia. Today Persia is called Iran.
64341.m: The Purim story takes place in Persia.

64342.q: Which Swiss custom does Purim, with its costumes, remind people of?
64342.e: As at carnival, many people wear costumes at Purim. Both festivals are fun and loud.
64342.m: Purim is a bit like carnival.

64343.q: What do people build for the festival of Sukkot?
64343.e: For Sukkot people build a small hut in the garden or on the balcony. That is why it is called the Feast of Tabernacles.
64343.m: For Sukkot people build a leafy hut.

64344.q: What is the roof of the sukkah covered with?
64344.e: The roof is made of branches, leaves or reeds. It must not be solid and closed.
64344.m: The roof of the sukkah is made of branches.

64345.q: What should you be able to see through the roof of the sukkah at night?
64345.e: The roof is built so loosely that you can see the stars at night. Even so, it should give more shade than sun.
64345.m: Through the sukkah roof you can see the stars.

64346.q: What does the Feast of Tabernacles remember?
64346.e: After leaving Egypt the people wandered through the desert for a long time. There they lived in simple huts.
64346.m: Sukkot remembers the huts in the desert.

64347.q: How many days does Sukkot last?
64347.e: Sukkot lasts seven days. It is followed straight away by more festival days such as Simchat Torah.

64348.q: In which season is Sukkot celebrated?
64348.e: Sukkot is in September or October. It is also a festival to give thanks for the harvest.

64349.q: Which fruit is part of the festive bundle at Sukkot?
64349.e: The etrog is a yellow citrus fruit that looks like a big lemon. Together with branches, it is part of the festive bundle.
64349.m: The etrog is part of the Sukkot bundle.

64350.q: What do people mainly do in the sukkah during the festival?
64350.e: During Sukkot people eat their meals in the hut. Some even sleep in it.
64350.m: In the sukkah people eat together.

64351.q: What does Yom Kippur mean in English?
64351.e: Yom Kippur is the Day of Atonement. People think about their mistakes and make peace with God and with other people.
64351.m: Yom Kippur is the Day of Atonement.

64352.q: What do most adults do on Yom Kippur?
64352.e: On Yom Kippur adults do not eat or drink anything all day. They pray a lot in the synagogue.

64353.q: Roughly how long does the fast on Yom Kippur last?
64353.e: The fast begins the evening before, before sunset. It ends the next evening, so it lasts about 25 hours.
64353.m: The Yom Kippur fast lasts about 25 hours.

64354.q: Who does not have to fast on Yom Kippur?
64354.e: Small children and sick people do not have to fast. Health is more important.
64354.m: Children and sick people do not have to fast.

64355.q: Which instrument is blown at the end of Yom Kippur?
64355.e: At the end of the day the shofar sounds in the synagogue. This marks the end of the Day of Atonement.

64356.q: What is a shofar usually made from?
64356.e: A shofar is usually a hollowed-out ram's horn. It is one of the oldest musical instruments.
64356.m: A shofar is usually made from a ram's horn.

64357.q: What colour do many people wear on Yom Kippur?
64357.e: Many people wear white clothes on Yom Kippur. White stands for purity and a new beginning.
64357.m: On Yom Kippur people often wear white.

64358.q: With which festival do the ten days that end with Yom Kippur begin?
64358.e: The Jewish New Year, Rosh Hashanah, is on the first day of the month of Tishri. Yom Kippur follows on the tenth day.
64358.m: Yom Kippur comes soon after the Jewish New Year.

64359.e: The mezuzah is a small case on the doorpost. You find it on many Jewish homes.
64359.m: The mezuzah hangs on the doorpost.

64360.e: Inside the case there is a small handwritten scroll. It has verses from the Torah on it.
64360.m: Inside the mezuzah there is a small scroll.

64361.q: On which side of the door does the mezuzah hang as you go in?
a: At the top in the middle
64361.e: The mezuzah hangs on the right-hand doorpost as you go into the room. It is fixed in the upper third of the post.
64361.m: The mezuzah hangs on the right of the door.

64362.q: On which houses is there often a mezuzah on the door?
64362.e: The mezuzah is a small case on the doorpost. You find it on many Jewish flats and houses.
64362.m: A mezuzah hangs on Jewish houses.

64363.q: What do many people do with the mezuzah as they go through the door?
64363.e: Many people touch the mezuzah with their fingers and then kiss their fingers. This shows respect for God's word.
64363.m: Many people touch the mezuzah as they go through.

64364.q: In which language are the verses in the mezuzah written?
64364.e: The small scroll in the mezuzah is written in Hebrew. That is the language of the Torah.
64364.m: The mezuzah is written in Hebrew.

64365.q: What does the word mezuzah mean?
64365.e: The Hebrew word mezuzah means “doorpost”. The case is named after the place where it hangs.

64366.q: With which words does the prayer in the mezuzah begin?
64366.e: In Hebrew the prayer is called “Shema Yisrael”. It is one of the most important prayers in Judaism.
64366.m: The Shema Yisrael begins with “Hear, O Israel”.

64367.q: In which direction is Hebrew written?
64367.e: Hebrew is written from right to left. That is why a Hebrew book begins on the side that is the back for us.
64367.m: Hebrew is read from right to left.

64368.q: What is the first letter of the Hebrew alphabet called?
64368.e: The first letter is called aleph. It is a silent letter with no sound of its own.
64368.m: Aleph is the first Hebrew letter.

64369.q: What is the second letter of the Hebrew alphabet called?
64369.e: After aleph comes bet. The word “alphabet” comes from the similar Greek letters alpha and beta.
64369.m: Bet is the second Hebrew letter.

64370.q: How many letters does the Hebrew alphabet have?
64370.e: The Hebrew alphabet has 22 letters. That is fewer than in our alphabet.

64371.q: What is usually missing in Hebrew writing?
64371.e: In Hebrew usually only consonants are written. Vowels can be shown with small dots and dashes, for example in children's books.
64371.m: Hebrew is usually written without vowels.

64372.q: In which country is Hebrew the main language?
64372.e: In Israel people speak Hebrew in everyday life. Street signs there are in Hebrew too.

64373.q: Which number does the letter aleph also stand for?
64373.e: Hebrew letters can also be numbers. The letter aleph stands for the number 1.
64373.m: Aleph also stands for the number 1.

64374.q: On which page do you start reading a Hebrew book?
a: On the page that is the last one for us
On the page that is the first one for us
In the middle of the book
64374.e: Hebrew is written from right to left. That is why a Hebrew book begins where our books end.
64374.m: A Hebrew book begins on our last page.

64375.q: What is the teacher and leader of a Jewish community called?
64375.e: The rabbi teaches and advises the Jewish community. He knows the holy scriptures very well.
64375.m: A rabbi leads a Jewish community.

64376.q: What does the word rabbi mean?
64376.e: Rabbi is Hebrew and means “my teacher” or “my master”. This is how scholars were addressed.

64377.q: In which building does a rabbi often work?
64377.e: The synagogue is the Jewish place of worship. The rabbi preaches and teaches there.
64377.m: The rabbi often works in the synagogue.

64378.q: What does a rabbi mainly explain to the community?
64378.e: A rabbi has studied the Torah and other Jewish writings for a long time. He explains them to the people in the community.

64379.q: What does a Jewish man such as the rabbi often wear on his head?
64379.e: The kippah is a small round cap. Many Jewish men wear it as a sign of respect for God.
64379.m: Jewish men often wear a kippah.

64380.q: May a rabbi marry and have a family?
64380.e: Rabbis may marry and have children. Many rabbis are married.

64381.q: Who do people often ask whether food is kosher?
64381.e: Kosher means that food is allowed under the Jewish food laws. Rabbis know these rules and check them.
64381.m: A rabbi checks whether food is kosher.

64382.q: What does the Hebrew word shalom mean?
64382.e: Shalom means peace. It is one of the best-known Hebrew words.

64383.q: When do people say shalom in Israel?
64383.e: People say shalom when they arrive and when they leave. It is like “hello” and “bye” at the same time.
64383.m: Shalom is said when coming and going.

64384.q: Which Arabic word is related to shalom?
64384.e: Hebrew and Arabic are related languages. The Arabic salam also means peace.
64384.m: Salam and shalom are related words.

64385.q: Which language does the word shalom come from?
64385.e: Shalom is a Hebrew word. Jewish people all over the world know and use it.

64386.q: What does the greeting “Shalom Aleichem” mean?
64386.e: “Shalom Aleichem” is a friendly greeting. It wishes peace to others.

64387.q: Apart from peace, what else do you wish someone when you say shalom?
64387.e: Shalom does not just mean no quarrelling. It also wishes that the other person is well.
64387.m: With shalom you wish that the other person is well.

64388.q: What is the song “Hevenu Shalom Aleichem” about?
64388.e: “Hevenu Shalom Aleichem” is a well-known Hebrew song. In it, people wish peace to everyone.
64388.m: Hevenu Shalom Aleichem is a song of peace.

64389.e: At Diwali people light lots of lights. That is why it is called the Festival of Lights.
64389.m: Diwali is the Hindu Festival of Lights.

64390.q: What do many families share and give at Diwali?
64390.e: At Diwali families give sweets and small presents. People visit each other.
64390.m: At Diwali people like to give sweets.

64391.q: What are the little clay lamps at Diwali called?
64391.e: Diyas are small clay bowls with oil and a wick. At Diwali they stand everywhere at windows and doors.
64391.m: The little clay lamps at Diwali are called diyas.
