64780.e: Ra is often shown as a man with the head of a falcon. On his head he wears a sun disc.
64780.m: In pictures Ra often has a falcon's head with a sun disc.

64781.q: What does Ra usually wear on his head in pictures?
64781.e: A round sun disc floats above his head. It is often surrounded by a snake.
64781.m: The sun disc on his head shows that Ra is the sun god.

64782.q: According to Egyptian belief, where did Ra travel at night?
64782.e: In the evening the sun went down. The Egyptians believed that Ra then travelled through the underworld and rose again in the morning.
64782.m: At night Ra travelled through the underworld.

64783.q: Which creature did Ra have to fight at night?
64783.e: The evil snake Apophis wanted to stop the solar barque. Ra and his helpers defeated it every night.
64783.m: Ra defeated the snake Apophis every night.

64784.q: As which animal did the Egyptians show the morning sun?
64784.e: The morning sun was called Khepri and was shown as a scarab. A scarab is a beetle that rolls a ball in front of it.
64784.m: The morning sun was shown as a scarab beetle.

64785.q: What did the pharaohs call themselves to show they were close to the sun god?
64785.e: The kings of Egypt bore the title “Son of Ra”. In this way they showed that they were connected to the sun god.
64785.m: A pharaoh called himself “Son of Ra”.

64786.q: Which animal's head does the Egyptian god Anubis have?
64786.e: Anubis is shown as a man with the head of a jackal. A jackal looks rather like a dog.
64786.m: Anubis has the head of a jackal.

64787.q: What was Anubis in charge of for the ancient Egyptians?
64787.e: Anubis was the god of the dead and of cemeteries. He protected the tombs.
64787.m: Anubis was the god of the dead and of tombs.

64788.q: According to Egyptian belief, which work did Anubis help with?
64788.e: Anubis was seen as the god of mummification. The priests who embalmed the dead sometimes wore an Anubis mask.
64788.m: Anubis helped with embalming the dead.

64789.q: What colour is Anubis usually in Egyptian pictures?
64789.e: Anubis is usually painted black. Black reminded people of the fertile soil by the Nile and of new life.
64789.m: In pictures Anubis is usually black.

64790.q: According to Egyptian belief, what did Anubis weigh at the judgement of the dead?
64790.e: The dead person's heart was placed on a pair of scales. On the other side lay a feather, which stood for truth.
64790.m: At the judgement of the dead the heart was weighed against a feather.

64791.q: Why was Anubis probably given a jackal's head?
64791.e: In Egypt jackals often wandered around the tombs at the edge of the desert. That is why the jackal became the animal of the god of the dead.
64791.m: Jackals roamed around the tombs, so the jackal became Anubis's animal.

64792.q: According to Egyptian belief, who did Anubis accompany?
64792.e: Anubis led the dead into the afterlife. He watched over them on the way.
64792.m: Anubis led the dead into the afterlife.

64793.q: According to Egyptian belief, what did Anubis watch over?
64793.e: Anubis was seen as the lord of the cities of the dead, that is, the large cemeteries. He was meant to protect the tombs from disturbance.

64794.q: Who was the goddess Isis for the ancient Egyptians?
64794.e: Isis was one of the most important goddesses of Egypt. She was seen as a loving mother and a protector.
64794.m: Isis was the great mother goddess of Egypt.

64795.q: What was the name of the goddess Isis's husband?
64795.e: Isis was married to the god Osiris. Osiris later became the ruler of the realm of the dead.
64795.m: Isis was the wife of Osiris.

64796.q: What was the name of Isis's son with the falcon's head?
64796.e: Horus was the son of Isis and Osiris. He is often shown with the head of a falcon.
64796.m: Horus was the son of Isis.

64797.q: What does Isis often wear on her head in old pictures?
64797.e: Isis often wears the sign for a throne on her head. Her name also means “throne” or “seat”.
64797.m: Isis wears a throne as a sign on her head.

64798.q: According to the legend, what did Isis do when her husband was killed?
64798.e: The evil Seth killed Osiris and scattered his body. Isis searched for all the pieces and brought Osiris back to life with magic.
64798.m: Isis brought her husband back to life with magic.

64799.q: What was Isis especially famous for?
64799.e: Isis was seen as a great sorceress. People asked her for protection and healing.

64800.q: By which river do the great temples of the goddess Isis stand in Egypt?
64800.e: The ancient Egyptians built their temples by the Nile. A famous temple of Isis stands on the Nile island of Philae.
64800.m: The temples of Isis stand by the Nile.

64801.q: Where else, apart from Egypt, was Isis later worshipped?
64801.e: The worship of Isis spread all around the Mediterranean. The Romans also built temples for her, for example in Pompeii.
64801.m: The Romans also worshipped the goddess Isis.

64802.q: Who were the great pyramids in Egypt built for?
64802.e: The pyramids were tombs for the kings of Egypt, the pharaohs. They were meant to rest in them for eternity.
64802.m: The pyramids were tombs for pharaohs.

64803.q: Why did the Egyptians put food in the tombs of the dead?
64803.e: The Egyptians believed in life after death. There the dead person was meant to have everything they needed.
64803.m: Grave goods were meant to help the dead in the afterlife.

64804.q: Why did the ancient Egyptians put small servant figures in tombs?
a: They were meant to work in the afterlife
They were meant to scare off robbers
They showed the way out of the tomb
64804.e: The small servant figures are called shabtis. They were meant to do the work for the dead person in the afterlife.
64804.m: Servant figures were meant to work for the dead in the afterlife.

64805.q: What did the ancient Egyptians keep in special jars next to the mummy?
64805.e: During mummification some organs were taken out. They were placed in special jars called canopic jars.
64805.m: Canopic jars held the mummy's organs.

64806.q: What was found in a pit next to the Pyramid of Cheops?
64806.e: In 1954 a dismantled wooden boat was found next to the Pyramid of Cheops. It is over 40 metres long.
64806.m: A large wooden boat lay next to the Pyramid of Cheops.

64807.q: Which scroll of magic spells did the ancient Egyptians often put in tombs?
64807.e: The Book of the Dead contained sayings and magic spells. They were meant to help the dead person on the way into the afterlife.
64807.m: The Book of the Dead helped the dead on the way into the afterlife.

64808.q: Who often stole the treasures from the pyramids?
64808.e: Almost all the pyramids were robbed by tomb robbers in ancient times. That is why hardly any treasures were found in them later.
64808.m: Tomb robbers plundered most of the pyramids.

64809.q: Which tomb with a golden mask was discovered in 1922?
64809.e: In 1922 Howard Carter found the tomb of the young pharaoh Tutankhamun in the Valley of the Kings. It was full of treasures, including a golden death mask.
64809.m: A golden mask lay in the tomb of Tutankhamun.

64810.q: Which god was the king of the Greek gods?
64810.e: Zeus ruled over all gods and humans. He was the most powerful god of the Greeks.
64810.m: Zeus was the king of the Greek gods.

64811.q: What does Zeus hurl when he is angry?
64811.e: Zeus was the god of the sky and the weather. When he was angry, he threw lightning bolts down to earth.
64811.m: Zeus hurls lightning bolts from the sky.

64812.e: The eagle was the sacred animal of Zeus. As king of the birds it suited the king of the gods.
64812.m: The eagle is the bird of Zeus.

64813.q: What was the name of Zeus's wife?
64813.e: Hera was the queen of the gods and the wife of Zeus. She was the goddess of marriage.
64813.m: Hera was the wife of Zeus.

64814.q: In honour of which god were the first Olympic Games held?
64814.e: The ancient Olympic Games were celebrated in Olympia for Zeus. A large temple for him also stood there.
64814.m: The ancient Olympic Games honoured Zeus.

64815.q: What was the name of Zeus's father?
64815.e: Zeus was the son of the Titan Cronus and of Rhea. Zeus defeated his father and became king.
64815.m: Cronus was the father of Zeus.

64816.q: Where did the statue of Zeus that was one of the Seven Wonders of the World stand?
64816.e: In Olympia there stood a huge figure of Zeus made of gold and ivory. It was one of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World.
64816.m: The statue of Zeus at Olympia was a wonder of the world.

64817.q: Which bird is the symbol of the goddess Athena?
64817.e: The owl was Athena's sacred animal. It was seen as a sign of cleverness.

64818.q: What was the goddess Athena best known for?
64818.e: Athena was the goddess of wisdom and of clever plans. She also helped craftspeople.
64818.m: Athena was the goddess of wisdom.

64819.q: Which city is named after the goddess Athena?
64819.e: The city of Athens bears the name of its protecting goddess. Today Athens is the capital of Greece.
64819.m: Athens is named after the goddess Athena.

64820.q: According to the legend, how was Athena born?
64820.e: The legend tells that Athena sprang from the head of Zeus. She was already wearing armour.
64820.m: Athena sprang from her father's head.

64821.q: According to the legend, which tree did Athena give to the people of Athens?
64821.e: Athena and another god argued over the city. Athena gave an olive tree and won.
64821.m: Athena gave people the olive tree.

64822.q: What is the famous temple of Athena in Athens called?
64822.e: The Parthenon stands on the Acropolis, a hill in Athens. It was built for Athena.
64822.m: The Parthenon is the temple of Athena.

64823.q: What does Athena wear on her head in many pictures?
64823.e: Athena is often shown with a helmet, shield and spear. She protected the city in war.
64823.m: Athena often wears a helmet and carries a shield.

64824.q: Which animal can be seen on the Greek 1-euro coin?
64824.e: The Greek 1-euro coin shows an owl. The picture comes from an old coin from Athens.
64824.m: The Greek 1-euro coin shows an owl.

64825.q: Which realm did the Greek god Poseidon rule over?
64825.e: Poseidon was the god of the sea. Sailors asked him for calm water.
64825.m: Poseidon was the god of the sea.

64826.q: What does Poseidon usually hold in his hand in pictures?
64826.e: Poseidon's weapon is the trident, a spear with three points. With it he could make waves and storms.

64827.q: What was Poseidon called by the Romans?
64827.e: The Romans took over many Greek gods with new names. Poseidon was called Neptune by them.

64828.q: Apart from sea creatures, which animal belongs especially to Poseidon?
64828.e: Poseidon was also seen as the god of horses. He is said to have given the Greeks the first horse.
64828.m: Poseidon was also the god of horses.

64829.q: According to Greek belief, what could Poseidon cause on land?
64829.e: The Greeks also called Poseidon the “Earth-Shaker”. When he struck the ground with his trident, the earth shook.
64829.m: Poseidon could make the earth shake.

64830.q: Who was one of Poseidon's brothers?
64830.e: Poseidon, Zeus and Hades were brothers. They divided the world between them.
64830.m: Poseidon was a brother of Zeus.

64831.q: What is the name of Poseidon's son who has a fish's tail instead of legs?
64831.e: Triton is a sea god, half human and half fish. He blows on a conch shell and can calm the waves with it.
64831.m: Triton is Poseidon's son with a fish's tail.

64832.q: According to the legend, where did Poseidon live?
a: In a palace in the sea
In a cave in the forest
In a tower in the desert
In a hut on a mountain
64832.e: Poseidon had a golden palace deep down in the sea. From there he drove over the waves in a chariot.
64832.m: Poseidon lived in a palace in the sea.

64833.q: What job did Hermes have among the Greek gods?
a: He was the messenger of the gods
64833.e: Hermes brought the messages of the gods, especially from Zeus. He was very fast.
64833.m: Hermes was the messenger of the gods.

64834.q: What does Hermes have on his feet?
64834.e: Hermes wears sandals with wings. With them he could fly quickly through the air.

64835.q: What was Hermes called by the Romans?
64835.e: The Romans called the messenger of the gods Mercury. There too he looked after traders and travellers.

64836.q: According to the legend, which animals did Hermes steal when he was still a baby?
64836.e: On the day he was born, Hermes stole the cattle of his brother Apollo. He was a clever trickster.
64836.m: Even as a baby Hermes stole cattle.

64837.q: According to the legend, from which animal's shell did Hermes build an instrument?
64837.e: Hermes made a lyre from a tortoise shell. The lyre is a stringed instrument.
64837.m: Hermes invented the lyre from a tortoise shell.

64838.e: Hermes was the god of roads and of trade. That is why travellers and merchants prayed to him.

64839.q: What does Hermes often wear on his head?
64839.e: Hermes often wears a flat travelling hat with small wings. It shows that he is a fast traveller.
64839.m: Hermes wears a hat with wings.

64840.q: What does Hermes often carry in his hand?
64840.e: The staff of Hermes is called the caduceus. Two snakes wind around it, and it often has small wings at the top.
64840.m: Hermes carries a staff with two snakes.

64841.q: Who was the king of the gods for the Romans?
64841.e: Jupiter was the highest god of the Romans. He matched the Greek Zeus.
64841.m: Jupiter was the king of the Roman gods.

64842.q: Which planet is named after Jupiter?
64842.e: The planet Jupiter is the largest planet in our solar system. That suits the king of the gods.
64842.m: The largest planet is called Jupiter.

64843.q: What does the Roman god Jupiter hurl in old pictures?
64843.e: Jupiter was the god of the sky and the weather. He often holds a bundle of lightning bolts in his hand.

64844.q: Which Greek goddess did the Roman goddess Minerva match?
64844.e: For the Romans Minerva was the goddess of wisdom. Together with Jupiter and Juno she was one of the most important gods of Rome.
64844.m: Minerva is the Roman name of Athena.

64845.q: What was the Roman god Mars in charge of?
64845.e: Mars was the war god of the Romans. Soldiers especially worshipped him.
64845.m: Mars was the Roman god of war.

64846.q: Which month is named after the god Mars?
64846.e: In Latin March is called “Martius”, the month of Mars. For the Romans the year used to begin with it.
64846.m: March is named after the god Mars.

64847.q: Which planet is named after the war god Mars?
64847.e: Mars shines reddish like blood. That is why it was given the name of the war god.
64847.m: The red planet is named after the war god Mars.

64848.q: According to Roman legend, who were the sons of Mars?
64848.e: The twins Romulus and Remus were said to be the sons of Mars. Romulus is said to have later founded Rome.
64848.m: Romulus and Remus were the sons of Mars.

64849.q: According to the legend, which animal fed the sons of Mars with its milk?
64849.e: The abandoned twins were found by a she-wolf. She gave them milk. The wolf was also the animal of Mars.
64849.m: A she-wolf saved the twins Romulus and Remus.

64850.q: Which Greek god did Mars match?
64850.e: The Greeks called their war god Ares. But the Romans honoured Mars much more than the Greeks honoured Ares.

64851.q: What is the weapon of the Norse god Thor?
64851.e: Thor fights with a mighty hammer. The hammer comes back to him after every throw.

64852.q: What was Thor in charge of for the Germanic peoples?
64852.e: Thor was the thunder god. When it thundered, people believed Thor was riding across the sky.
64852.m: Thor was the god of thunder.

64853.e: Thor rides in a chariot pulled by two billy goats. People imagined that the rolling of his chariot sounded like thunder.
64853.m: Two billy goats pull Thor's chariot.

64854.q: What was Thor called by the southern Germanic peoples?
64854.e: Among the Germanic peoples in the south the thunder god was called Donar. The name is related to “Donner”, the German word for thunder.
64854.m: The southern Germanic peoples called Thor Donar.

64855.q: Which monster does Thor fight in the Norse legends?
64855.e: The Midgard Serpent is so long that it reaches around the whole world. Thor is its greatest enemy.

64856.q: What is the name of Thor's father in the Norse legends?
64856.e: Thor is a son of the one-eyed god with the two ravens. He is one of the strongest gods.

64857.q: What position did Odin have among the Norse gods?
a: He was the father of the gods
He was the messenger of the gods
64857.e: Odin was the highest god of the Norsemen. He was clever and wise.
64857.m: Odin was the father of the gods in the North.

64858.q: Which birds sit on Odin's shoulders?
64858.e: Odin's ravens are called Huginn and Muninn. Every day they fly through the world and tell him everything.
64858.m: Odin's ravens are called Huginn and Muninn.

64859.q: What is the name of the hall to which Odin brought fallen warriors?
64859.e: According to the belief of the Norsemen, brave warriors went to Valhalla. There they feasted with Odin.
64859.m: Fallen warriors went to Odin in Valhalla.

64860.q: What was Odin called by the southern Germanic peoples?
64860.e: Among the Germanic peoples in the south the father of the gods was called Wodan or Wotan.
64860.m: The southern Germanic peoples called Odin Wodan.

64861.e: Odin's spear is called Gungnir. It is said never to miss its target.

64862.q: According to the legend, which writing symbols is Odin said to have discovered?
64862.e: The legend tells that Odin hung on a tree for nine days. After that he knew the runes, the old writing of the Germanic peoples.
64862.m: Odin is said to have discovered the runes.

64863.q: Which Germanic god is the English “Tuesday” named after?
64863.e: “Tuesday” is the day of the god Tiw, called Tyr in the North. He was a god of battle and of law.
64863.m: The English Tuesday is the day of the god Tyr.

64864.q: Which day of the week is named after Wodan in English?
64864.e: “Wednesday” comes from “Woden's day”, the day of Wodan. In German it is called Mittwoch.
64864.m: The English Wednesday is the day of Wodan.

64865.q: Which goddess is Friday named after?
64865.e: Friday is named after the Germanic goddess Frija, who was called Frigg in the North. She was Odin's wife.
64865.m: Friday is the day of the goddess Frigg.

64866.q: Which heavenly body is Sunday named after?
64866.e: The Romans already named the day after the sun. The name is still in the word “Sunday” today.
64866.m: Sunday is the day of the sun.

64867.q: Which day of the week is called “mardi” in French?
64867.e: “Mardi” comes from the war god Mars. It is Tuesday.
64867.m: The French mardi is the day of Mars.

64868.q: Which god is the French “jeudi” named after?
64868.e: “Jeudi” means the day of Jupiter. In English it is Thursday.
64868.m: The French jeudi is the day of Jupiter.

64869.q: Which day of the week is called “mercredi” in French?
64869.e: “Mercredi” is the day of the god Mercury. In English it is Wednesday.
64869.m: The French mercredi is the day of Mercury.

64870.q: Which god is the English “Saturday” named after?
64870.e: “Saturday” is the day of the Roman god Saturn.
64870.m: The English Saturday is the day of Saturn.

64871.q: Which heavenly body is Monday named after?
64871.e: Monday means the day of the moon. In French too, “lundi” reminds us of the moon.
64871.m: Monday is the day of the moon.

64872.q: Which goddess is the French “vendredi” named after?
64872.e: “Vendredi” is the day of the Roman goddess Venus. In English it is Friday.
64872.m: The French vendredi is the day of Venus.

64873.q: Why do many religions celebrate festivals of light in winter?
a: Because the days are short and dark
64873.e: In winter it gets dark early. Candles and lamps bring light and hope into the dark season.
64873.m: Festivals of light bring light into the dark winter.

64874.q: Which two festivals do Jews and Christians celebrate in winter with lots of candles?
64874.e: At Hanukkah Jews light one more candle each evening. During Advent Christians light one more candle on the wreath each week.
64874.m: Hanukkah and Advent are winter festivals of light.

64875.q: What is the great Hindu festival of light called?
64875.e: Diwali is celebrated in autumn, usually in October or November. People decorate their houses with lots of lights.
64875.m: Diwali is the Hindu festival of light.

64876.q: What do Hindus light in and in front of their houses at Diwali?
64876.e: At Diwali people set out lots of small clay oil lamps. They stand for the victory of light over darkness.
64876.m: At Diwali lots of small oil lamps shine.

64877.q: How many candles does an Advent wreath usually have?
64877.e: There are four Advent Sundays before Christmas. On each Sunday one more candle is lit.
64877.m: The Advent wreath usually has four candles.

64878.q: Whose birth do Christians celebrate at Christmas?
64878.e: Christmas is the festival of the birth of Jesus. The many lights on the tree remind people that for Christians Jesus is the light of the world.
64878.m: At Christmas Christians celebrate the birth of Jesus.

64879.q: What does the Jewish festival of light Hanukkah remember?
a: A miracle of oil in the Temple
64879.e: According to tradition, the oil in the Temple in Jerusalem, enough for one day, lasted much longer. The lights of Hanukkah remember this.
64879.m: Hanukkah remembers the miracle of the oil in the Temple.

64880.q: Which festival of light is celebrated in Sweden on 13 December with a crown of candles?
64880.e: On St Lucy's Day a girl in a white dress wears a wreath of candles on her head. The festival remembers Saint Lucy.
64880.m: On St Lucy's Day a girl wears a crown of candles.

64881.q: What do all winter festivals of light have in common?
a: Light as a sign of hope
Looking for eggs in the garden
64881.e: Whether Hanukkah, Advent or St Lucy's Day: the light stands for hope and for the good that is stronger than the darkness.
64881.m: At festivals of light, light stands for hope.

64882.q: What is the Jewish New Year festival called?
64882.e: Rosh Hashanah means “head of the year”. It is celebrated in autumn, in September or early October.
64882.m: Rosh Hashanah is the Jewish New Year.

64883.q: What do Jews eat at Rosh Hashanah for a sweet new year?
64883.e: People dip pieces of apple in honey. In this way they wish for a good and sweet year.
64883.m: Apple with honey stands for a sweet new year.

64884.q: Which instrument is blown in the synagogue at the Jewish New Year?
64884.e: The ram's horn is called a shofar. Its loud sound is meant to wake people up and make them think.
64884.m: At the Jewish New Year the ram's horn is blown.

64885.q: Which heavenly body does the Islamic calendar follow?
64885.e: A lunar year is about 11 days shorter than a solar year. That is why the Islamic New Year falls about 11 days earlier every year.
64885.m: The Islamic calendar follows the moon.

64886.q: What does the Christian church year begin with?
64886.e: The church year does not begin on 1 January. It starts with the first Sunday of Advent, four Sundays before Christmas.
64886.m: The church year begins with the first Sunday of Advent.

64887.q: Which New Year festival is celebrated at the start of spring, for example in Iran?
64887.e: Nowruz means “new day”. It is celebrated around 21 March, when spring begins.
64887.m: Nowruz is a New Year festival at the start of spring.

64888.q: Who is Silvester, the German name for the last day of the year, named after?
64888.e: Pope Sylvester I died on 31 December 335. That is why his feast day, and so the last day of the year, is called Silvester in German-speaking countries.
64888.m: Silvester is named after Pope Sylvester.

64889.q: At which New Year festival in Thailand do people splash each other with water?
64889.e: Songkran is the Thai New Year in April. Water stands for cleansing and good luck.
64889.m: At Songkran people in Thailand celebrate New Year with water.

64890.q: With which journey of the Prophet Muhammad does the Islamic calendar begin?
a: The migration from Mecca to Medina
64890.e: In the year 622 Muhammad moved with his followers from Mecca to Medina. The Islamic calendar begins with this year.
64890.m: The Islamic calendar begins with the migration to Medina.

64891.q: What is the Muslim month of fasting called?
64891.e: During Ramadan many Muslims fast for a month. It is the ninth month of the Islamic calendar.
64891.m: Ramadan is the Muslim month of fasting.

64892.q: When do fasting Muslims not eat or drink during Ramadan?
64892.e: People fast from dawn until sunset. In the evening the families then eat together.
64892.m: During Ramadan Muslims fast while it is light.

64893.q: What do many Muslims break their fast with in the evening?
64893.e: After sunset many Muslims first eat a date and drink water. The Prophet Muhammad is said to have done the same.
64893.m: Many Muslims break the fast with dates.

64894.q: Which festival do Muslims celebrate at the end of Ramadan?
a: The Festival of Breaking the Fast
64894.e: After Ramadan Muslims often celebrate for three days. The festival is also called the Sugar Festival because there are lots of sweets.
64894.m: After Ramadan Muslims celebrate the Festival of Breaking the Fast.

64895.q: How many days does the Christian season of fasting before Easter last?
64895.e: Lent lasts 40 days; the Sundays are not counted. It recalls the 40 days that Jesus fasted in the desert.
64895.m: The Christian season of fasting lasts 40 days.

64896.q: On which day does the Christian season of fasting begin?
64896.e: On Ash Wednesday, in Catholic churches the priest draws a cross of ashes on people's foreheads. This begins Lent.

64897.q: Which colourful festival is celebrated in many places in Switzerland just before the Christian season of fasting?
64897.e: Before Lent people used to celebrate and eat well one last time. This is where Fasnacht, the carnival with masks and music, came from.

64898.q: What is the Jewish Day of Atonement, on which Jews fast for a whole day, called?
64898.e: Yom Kippur is the most important fast day in Judaism. People think about their mistakes and ask for forgiveness.
64898.m: On Yom Kippur Jews fast for a whole day.

64899.q: What do fasting during Ramadan and during the Christian season of fasting have in common?
a: You celebrate a festival every day
You are not allowed to speak
64899.e: In both religions people go without food or habits for a while. In this way they want to come closer to God and think of others.
64899.m: Fasting means deliberately going without something.

64900.q: On which day of the week do Muslims especially meet for communal prayer in the mosque?
64900.e: The Friday prayer at midday is the most important communal prayer of the week. Christians, on the other hand, usually go to church on Sunday.
64900.m: Muslims pray together in the mosque on Friday.

64901.q: What is the large main church in the old town of Bern called?
64901.e: Bern Minster is a Reformed church. Its tower, about 100 metres high, is the tallest church tower in Switzerland.
64901.m: Bern Minster has the tallest church tower in Switzerland.

64902.q: What is a Buddhist tower with many roofs on top of each other, as seen in China and Japan, called?
64902.e: A pagoda has several storeys with curved roofs. Precious Buddhist objects are often kept inside.
64902.m: A pagoda is a Buddhist tower with many roofs.

64903.q: What is the place of worship of the Sikhs called?
64903.e: Gurdwara means “door to the Guru”. After the prayers there, all guests get a free meal.

64904.q: What do you take off before you go into a mosque?
64904.e: In the mosque people pray on carpets on the floor. That is why you take your shoes off at the entrance, so that everything stays clean.
64904.m: You do not wear shoes in the mosque.

64905.q: In which direction does the prayer niche in a mosque point?
64905.e: Muslims pray facing Mecca in Saudi Arabia. The niche in the wall shows everyone this direction.
64905.m: The prayer niche points towards Mecca.

64906.q: In which Swiss city do several religions share the “House of Religions”?
64906.e: In the House of Religions in Bern different religions have their rooms under one roof, for example a Hindu temple and a mosque. It opened in 2014.
64906.m: In the House of Religions in Bern many religions live under one roof.

64907.q: Which sign is the most important symbol of Christians?
64907.e: The cross reminds people that Jesus died on the cross. For Christians it is also a sign of hope.
64907.m: The cross is the sign of Christians.

64908.q: Which star is a sign of Judaism?
64908.e: The Star of David is named after King David. It can also be seen on the flag of Israel.
64908.m: The Star of David is a sign of Judaism.

64909.q: How many points does the Star of David have?
64909.e: The Star of David is made of two triangles lying on top of each other. Together they make 6 points.
64909.m: The Star of David has six points.

64910.q: Which sign is often seen on the top of mosques?
64910.e: The crescent moon, often with a star, has become a well-known sign of Islam. It can be seen on many minarets.
64910.m: The crescent moon is a well-known sign of Islam.

a: A crescent moon with a star
64911.e: The wheel of teaching reminds people of the Buddha's teachings. The eight spokes stand for the Eightfold Path.
64911.m: The wheel with eight spokes is a sign of Buddhism.

64912.q: Which animal was a secret sign used by the first Christians to recognise each other?
64912.e: The Greek word for fish is “Ichthys”. Its letters are the first letters of the words “Jesus Christ, Son of God, Saviour”.
64912.m: The fish was a secret sign of the first Christians.

64913.q: Which bird stands for the Holy Spirit and for peace in Christianity?
64913.e: In the Bible the Spirit of God comes down like a dove when Jesus is baptised. Today the dove is a sign of peace all over the world.
64913.m: The dove is a sign of peace.

64914.q: How many branches does the menorah, the lampstand from the Temple in Jerusalem, have?
64914.e: The menorah is an ancient lampstand with seven branches. It is one of the oldest signs of Judaism.

64915.q: Which sign does the Red Cross use in many Muslim countries?
64915.e: The movement was founded by Henri Dunant from Geneva. In many Muslim countries it is called the Red Crescent.
64915.m: In many Muslim countries the Red Crescent helps.

64916.q: What is the holy book of Christians called?
64916.e: The word Bible comes from the Greek word for “books”. The Bible is in fact made up of many separate books.
64916.m: The Bible is the holy book of Christians.

64917.q: What is the holy book of Muslims called?
64917.e: For Muslims the Quran contains the words of God to the Prophet Muhammad. It is divided into 114 chapters.
64917.m: The Quran is the holy book of Muslims.

64918.q: What is the holy scripture of the Jews called?
64918.e: The Torah tells the story from the creation of the world to the death of Moses. It also stands at the beginning of the Christian Bible.
64918.m: The Torah is the most important book of the Jews.

64919.q: In which language was the Quran written down?
64919.e: The Quran was written down in Arabic. That is why many Muslims all over the world learn to read Arabic.
64919.m: The Quran is written in Arabic.

64920.q: Which two large parts make up the Christian Bible?
64920.e: The Old Testament tells the story before Jesus. The New Testament tells of the life of Jesus and of the first Christians.
64920.m: The Bible has an Old and a New Testament.

64921.q: What are the oldest holy scriptures of the Hindus called?
64921.e: The Vedas are over 3000 years old. For a long time they were only passed on by word of mouth.
64921.m: The Vedas are the oldest scriptures of the Hindus.

64922.q: In which language was the Torah written down?
64922.e: The Torah is written in Hebrew. Hebrew is read from right to left.
64922.m: The Torah is written in Hebrew.

64923.q: How many Gospels about the life of Jesus are there in the Bible?
64923.e: The four Gospels are named after Matthew, Mark, Luke and John. They tell of the life, death and resurrection of Jesus.
64923.m: There are four Gospels in the Bible.

64924.q: Which reformer had the Bible translated into German in Zurich?
64924.e: Under Huldrych Zwingli, scholars in Zurich translated the Bible into German. In 1531 the complete Zurich Bible was printed.
64924.m: The Zurich Bible was made under Zwingli.

64925.q: What does the Golden Rule say?
a: Treat others as you want to be treated
Always be first in the queue
64925.e: The Golden Rule asks you to put yourself in other people's shoes. What I wish for myself, I should also give to others.
64925.m: I treat others the way I want to be treated myself.

64926.q: A German saying begins: “What you do not want done to you ...”. How does it end?
a: do not do to anyone else
leave it alone in the evening
tell only your friend about it
64926.e: This is a well-known saying in German. It is a simple form of the Golden Rule.
64926.m: What I do not want to happen to me, I do not do to others.

64927.q: In which religions can you find a form of the Golden Rule?
64927.e: Similar sayings exist in Judaism, Christianity, Islam, Hinduism, Buddhism and also without religion. That is why the Golden Rule connects many people.
64927.m: The Golden Rule exists in many religions.

64928.q: Who says in the Bible: “Do to others what you would have them do to you”?
64928.e: Jesus says this in the Sermon on the Mount in the Gospel of Matthew. It is the Christian form of the Golden Rule.
64928.m: In the Bible Jesus teaches the Golden Rule.

64929.q: Which Chinese teacher said something similar to the Golden Rule about 2500 years ago?
64929.e: Confucius taught: what you do not wish for yourself, do not do to others. He lived in China.
64929.m: Confucius also knew the Golden Rule.

64930.q: Which Jewish teacher said the Golden Rule is the whole Torah and the rest is explanation?
64930.e: Rabbi Hillel lived about 2000 years ago in Jerusalem. He said: what is hateful to you, do not do to your neighbour.
64930.m: Rabbi Hillel summed up the Torah with the Golden Rule.

64931.q: You do not want to be laughed at. What follows from this according to the Golden Rule?
a: I do not laugh at others either
I laugh at the others first
I only play on my own
64931.e: The Golden Rule asks you to treat others the way you want to be treated yourself. If you do not want to be laughed at, you do not laugh at others.
64931.m: What hurts me, I do not do to others.

64932.q: A child is new in the class. What fits the Golden Rule best?
a: Greet them in a friendly way
64932.e: Someone who is new is glad of a friendly welcome. That is how you would want to be greeted yourself.
64932.m: I greet others as kindly as I would like to be greeted.

64933.q: Why is the Golden Rule called “golden”?
a: Because it is as valuable as gold
Because it was written on gold
Because it was found in gold
64933.e: Gold is very valuable. The rule got this name because it is seen as an especially valuable rule for living together.
64933.m: The Golden Rule is as valuable as gold for living together.

64934.q: How do many people in Switzerland who have no religion celebrate Christmas?
a: As a family celebration with presents
64934.e: Christmas is a Christian festival. Many people without a religion still celebrate it as a family festival with a tree and presents.
64934.m: Many people without a religion also celebrate Christmas with their family.

64935.q: What does the Greek word “theos”, found in the word atheist, mean?
64935.e: “Theos” means God, and the prefix “a” means without. So an atheist is a person without God.

64936.q: What are people called who say: “I do not know whether there is a God”?
64936.e: Agnostics think that you cannot know for certain whether God exists. The word comes from Greek and means roughly “not knowing”.
64936.m: Agnostics say you cannot know whether God exists.

64937.q: What does it mean if someone has no religious affiliation?
a: They do not belong to any religious community
They go to church every day
64937.e: People with no religious affiliation are not members of a church or religious community. Some still believe in something, others do not.
64937.m: People with no religious affiliation belong to no religious community.

64938.q: How many people in Switzerland do not belong to any religious community (as of 2024)?
64938.e: According to the Federal Statistical Office, in 2024 about 37 per cent of people aged 15 and over had no religious affiliation. That is more than one person in three.
64938.m: In Switzerland more than one person in three has no religious affiliation.

64939.q: How has the number of people with no religious affiliation in Switzerland changed since 1970?
a: It has stayed exactly the same
64939.e: In 1970 only about 1 per cent of people had no religious affiliation. Today it is a large part of the population.
64939.m: In Switzerland there are many more people with no religious affiliation today than in the past.

64940.q: What is the name of a Swiss association of people without religion?
64940.e: The Freethinkers' Association of Switzerland stands up for people who live without religion. It wants a clear separation of state and church.
64940.m: People without religion meet in the Freethinkers' Association.

64941.q: What is a world view called that puts people and their dignity at the centre, even without God?
64941.e: The word comes from the Latin “humanus”, which means human. Many people without religion call themselves humanists.
64941.m: Humanists put people at the centre.

64942.q: What do humanists who do not believe in God base their lives on?
64942.e: Humanists want to make good decisions using their own reason. In doing so they think about the well-being of all people.
64942.m: Humanists live by reason and compassion.

64943.q: Where is freedom of religion laid down in Switzerland?
64943.e: Article 15 of the Federal Constitution protects this basic right. It applies to everyone in Switzerland.
64943.m: The Federal Constitution protects freedom of religion.

64944.q: What does the Swiss Federal Constitution call freedom of religion?
64944.e: In Article 15 this right is called freedom of religion and conscience. Your conscience is the inner voice that tells you what is right.
64944.m: In the Federal Constitution freedom of religion is called freedom of religion and conscience.

64945.q: In Switzerland, is anyone allowed to force someone to believe in a particular god?
64945.e: The Federal Constitution says clearly: no one may be forced to join or belong to a religion.
64945.m: No one may be forced into a religion.

64946.q: What is it called when someone no longer wants to be a member of their church and leaves it?
64946.e: Anyone who wants to leave the church can do so. In Switzerland a written statement to the parish is usually enough.
64946.m: Someone who leaves their church formally withdraws from it.

64947.q: Are you allowed to change your religion in Switzerland?
a: Yes, you may choose it freely
64947.e: The Federal Constitution allows everyone to choose their religion freely. That includes changing it.
64947.m: You may freely choose and change your religion.

64948.q: From what age can you decide about your own religion in Switzerland?
64948.e: According to the Civil Code, young people aged 16 and over decide about their religious faith themselves. Before that, the parents decide.
64948.m: From 16 you decide about your own religion.

64949.q: In which UN document from 1948 is freedom of religion written?
a: Convention on the Rights of the Child
64949.e: Article 18 of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights contains freedom of belief. It applies to all people in the world.
64949.m: Freedom of religion is a human right.

64950.q: In Switzerland, may you show and celebrate your faith together with others?
a: No, only all alone at home
64950.e: The Federal Constitution allows people to profess their faith alone or together with others. That is why there are church services and religious festivals.
64950.m: You may also celebrate your faith together with others.

64951.q: A classmate does not eat pork because of her religion. What is respectful?
64951.e: Everyone may live by their own food rules. Respect means respecting such decisions.
64951.m: Respect means respecting other people's rules.

64952.q: Your friend celebrates a festival you do not know. What fits respect and tolerance?
64952.e: If you ask and listen, you learn something new. That is how understanding grows between people of different religions.
64952.m: If you ask and listen, you get to know other religions.

64953.q: What are conversations between people of different religions called?
64953.e: In interfaith dialogue people of different religions learn from each other. They look for things in common and respect differences.
64953.m: In interfaith dialogue religions talk to each other.

64954.q: What is the week in November called when people of different religions meet in Switzerland?
64954.e: The Week of Religions takes place every year in the first week of November. There are over 100 events all over Switzerland for getting to know each other.
64954.m: In the Week of Religions different religions get to know each other.

64955.q: What is polite when you visit someone else's place of worship?
a: Be quiet and follow the rules
64955.e: A place of worship is a holy place for many people. That is why you behave quietly and follow the rules.
64955.m: In a place of worship you behave quietly and respectfully.

a: An opinion about others without knowing them
64956.e: With a prejudice you judge people before you know them. If you get to know others, you can break down prejudices.
64956.m: Getting to know others breaks down prejudices.

64957.q: A child is being laughed at because of their religion. What is right?
a: Stand by them and get help
64957.e: No one may be laughed at or left out because of their faith. Anyone who helps or fetches a teacher shows courage and respect.
64957.m: I stand by others when they are laughed at because of their faith.

64958.q: What is the tall, pointed hat of a Catholic bishop called?
64958.e: The bishop wears the mitre at solemn church services. It has a point at the front and at the back.

64959.q: Which religious community is known for men wearing a turban?
64959.e: Sikh men do not cut their hair and wear it under the turban. The turban is an important sign of their faith.

64960.q: What do some Muslim women wear over their hair?
64960.e: Many Muslim women wear a headscarf, others do not. Whether they wear it is a personal and religious decision.
64960.m: Some Muslim women wear a headscarf.

64961.q: What is the long robe of a Christian monk called?
64961.e: Monks in monasteries wear a simple habit, often with a hood. Its colour shows which order a monk belongs to.

64963.q: What do Reformed ministers often wear during the church service?
64963.e: The gown is a long black robe. In many Reformed churches in Switzerland the ministers wear it during the service.
64963.m: Reformed ministers often wear a black gown.

64964.q: What colour are the Pope's clothes usually?
64964.e: In everyday life the Pope wears a white robe with a white cap. You can recognise him at once by it.

64965.q: What is the prayer shawl that Jewish men wear at morning prayer called?
64965.e: The tallit is a shawl with fringes at its four corners. It reminds people of God's commandments.
64965.m: Jewish men wear a tallit when they pray.

64966.q: Why do people in many religions cover their heads when they pray?
a: As a sign of respect for God
So that they do not get cold
64966.e: In Judaism, Islam and Sikhism a head covering during prayer is a sign of respect. Christian men, on the other hand, take their hats off in church.
64966.m: A head covering during prayer shows respect for God.

64967.q: Which birds can be seen on the coat of arms of Einsiedeln?
64967.e: A legend tells of two ravens that lived with the hermit Meinrad. That is why the coats of arms of the monastery and the village show two ravens.
64967.m: Two ravens fly on the coat of arms of Einsiedeln.

64968.q: What was the name of the hermit who lived in the forest of Einsiedeln before the monastery?
64968.e: Meinrad lived alone in the forest more than 1100 years ago and prayed. Later the monastery was built where he had lived.
64968.m: Saint Meinrad lived as a hermit in the dark forest.

64969.q: Where does the village of Einsiedeln get its name from?
64969.e: A hermit is a person who lives alone; in German a hermit is called an “Einsiedler”. Because Meinrad lived there alone, the place is called Einsiedeln.
64969.m: Einsiedeln is named after a hermit.

64970.q: Which animals have the monks of Einsiedeln been breeding for many hundreds of years?
64970.e: The monastery has a stud farm with horses. It is said to be the oldest stud farm in Europe that still exists.
64970.m: Einsiedeln Abbey has a very old horse stud.

64971.q: Why do many pilgrims come to Einsiedeln every year?
64971.e: Einsiedeln is the largest place of pilgrimage in Switzerland. Pilgrims come to pray in the church.
64971.m: Einsiedeln is the largest place of pilgrimage in Switzerland.

64972.q: What is the head of a monastery of monks called?
64972.e: A monastery for men such as Einsiedeln is led by an abbot. The monks elect him.
64972.m: The abbot leads a monastery of monks.

64973.q: Which sweet bake from Einsiedeln is shaped like an animal?
64973.e: The Einsiedeln Schafbock is a gingerbread bake in the shape of a ram. Pilgrims like to take one home as a souvenir.
64973.m: The Einsiedeln Schafbock is a well-known bake.

64974.q: In which building in Einsiedeln does the Black Madonna stand?
64974.e: The figure stands in a small chapel inside the abbey church. This chapel is called the Chapel of Grace.
64974.m: The Black Madonna stands in the abbey church of Einsiedeln.

64975.q: Who does the Black Madonna show?
64975.e: Madonna is another word for Mary. The figure shows Mary carrying the baby Jesus in her arm.
64975.m: The Madonna is Mary with the baby Jesus.

64976.q: Why did the Madonna of Einsiedeln become dark?
64976.e: For centuries candles and lamps burned in front of the figure. Their soot made the Madonna dark.
64976.m: Candle smoke turned the Madonna black.

64977.q: What is regularly changed on the Black Madonna?
64977.e: The Madonna wears a splendid fabric dress. It is changed according to the time of the church year.
64977.m: The Black Madonna gets a different dress again and again.

64978.q: What does the Black Madonna wear on her head?
64978.e: Mary is honoured as the Queen of Heaven. That is why she and the baby Jesus wear golden crowns.
64978.m: The Madonna wears a crown like a queen.

64979.q: Who took the Black Madonna of Einsiedeln to safety from French soldiers in 1798?
64979.e: When French soldiers came, the monks took the Madonna away and hid her. In this way she was saved.
64979.m: The monks saved the Madonna from the soldiers.

64980.q: What did a painter do when he found the Madonna's light colour under the soot?
64980.e: Under the soot the figure was originally light. The painter Adam Fuetscher still painted the skin black, and in 1803 she came back to Einsiedeln.
64980.m: The Madonna was deliberately painted black again.

64981.q: What do pilgrims often light in front of the Black Madonna?
64981.e: Pilgrims light a candle and say a prayer. The candle stands for a request or a thank you.
64981.m: Many candles burn in front of the Madonna.

64982.q: In which city is the famous Abbey Library?
64982.e: The Abbey Library belongs to the old monastery in St Gallen. It is one of the oldest libraries in the world.
64982.m: The Abbey Library is in St Gallen.

64983.q: What do visitors have to put on over their shoes in the Abbey Library of St Gallen?
64983.e: The wooden floor is very old and valuable. Felt slippers protect it.
64983.m: In the Abbey Library you walk in felt slippers.

64984.q: How were the oldest books in the Abbey Library made?
64984.e: The oldest books are more than 1000 years old. Monks wrote them by hand, letter by letter.
64984.m: Monks wrote the old books by hand.

64985.q: What did monks write their books on in the past?
64985.e: Parchment is made from animal skin. It lasts a very long time.
64985.m: Parchment is a writing material made from animal skin.

64986.q: Which special guest lies in the Abbey Library of St Gallen?
64986.e: The mummy of a woman from Egypt lies in the library. Her name is Shepenese.
64986.m: An Egyptian mummy lies in the Abbey Library.

64987.q: How is the Greek inscription above the door of the Abbey Library often translated?
64987.e: A Greek saying is written above the door. It means roughly “pharmacy for the soul”.
64987.m: Above the door of the Abbey Library are the words pharmacy for the soul.

64988.q: Which famous list does the Abbey precinct of St Gallen belong to?
a: The Seven Wonders of the World
64988.e: Since 1983 the Abbey precinct with its church and library has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
64988.m: The Abbey precinct of St Gallen is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

64989.q: In which architectural style is the great hall of the Abbey Library decorated?
64989.e: The hall has lots of wood, gold and painted ceilings. That is typical of the Baroque.
64989.m: The library hall in St Gallen is Baroque.

64990.q: According to the legend, what did the bear bring the monk Gallus?
64990.e: Gallus asked the bear to fetch wood for the fire. The bear obeyed and brought wood.
64990.m: The bear brought Gallus wood for the fire.

64991.q: What did the bear get from Gallus as a reward?
64991.e: To thank it, Gallus gave the bear some bread. Then he sent it away into the mountains.
64991.m: Gallus rewarded the bear with bread.

64992.q: According to the old tradition, which country did the monk Gallus come from?
64992.e: Old accounts of his life name Ireland as the home of Gallus. He travelled with the monk Columbanus to Lake Constance.
64992.m: According to tradition, Gallus came from Ireland.

64993.q: Which town is named after the monk Gallus?
64993.e: A monastery was built where Gallus lived. It grew into the town of St Gallen.
64993.m: St Gallen bears the name of the monk Gallus.

64994.q: By which river did Gallus build himself a cell?
64994.e: Gallus settled in the forest by the Steinach. Today the town of St Gallen stands there.

64995.e: Gallus was a monk. He lived for God and spread the Christian faith.

64996.q: When is St Gall's Day celebrated?
64996.e: The feast day of Saint Gallus is 16 October. In St Gallen it is a special day.
64996.m: St Gall's Day is on 16 October.

64997.q: According to the legend, what happened when Gallus fell into a thorn bush in the forest?
64997.e: Gallus saw the fall as a sign from God. That is why he stayed in that place.
64997.m: Gallus stayed where he had fallen.

64998.q: What was Brother Klaus's real name?
64998.e: Brother Klaus was really called Niklaus von Flüe. He lived more than 500 years ago.
64998.m: Brother Klaus was called Niklaus von Flüe.

64999.q: What is the gorge where Brother Klaus lived as a hermit called?
64999.e: Brother Klaus lived in a small cell in the Ranft gorge. He prayed there for many years.
64999.m: Brother Klaus lived as a hermit in the Ranft.

65000.q: What was Brother Klaus before he became a hermit?
65000.e: Niklaus von Flüe had a farm, a wife and ten children. Only after that did he become a hermit.
65000.m: Brother Klaus was first a farmer and father.

65001.q: What is Brother Klaus especially known for in Swiss history?
65001.e: In 1481 the members of the Confederation were quarrelling fiercely. His advice helped them reach an agreement in Stans.

65002.q: What is said about Brother Klaus and food?
a: He is said to have eaten almost nothing
He ate five times a day
65002.e: It is said that Brother Klaus lived for many years without food. Many people were amazed by this.
65002.m: Brother Klaus is said to have lived without food.

65003.q: What has Brother Klaus been for the Catholic Church since 1947?
65003.e: Pope Pius XII declared Brother Klaus a saint in 1947. He is the patron saint of Switzerland.

65004.q: Which country is Brother Klaus the patron saint of?
65004.e: Brother Klaus is seen as the patron saint of Switzerland. Many people pray to him for peace.
65004.m: Brother Klaus is the patron saint of Switzerland.

65005.q: Who sings or calls the Alpine blessing on the alp?
65005.e: In summer the Senn looks after the cows on the alp. In the evening he calls the Alpine blessing.
65005.m: The Senn calls the Alpine blessing.

65006.q: At what time of day is the Alpine blessing usually called?
65006.e: The Senn calls the Alpine blessing every evening after work, when it is getting dark.
65006.m: The Alpine blessing rings out in the evening.

65007.q: What does the Senn use to make his voice louder during the Alpine blessing?
65007.e: The Senn calls through a milk funnel made of wood or tin. That way his voice carries far across the alp.
65007.m: For the Alpine blessing you call through a milk funnel.

65008.q: Who is the Alpine blessing meant to protect?
a: People and animals on the alp
65008.e: With the Alpine blessing people ask God and the saints to protect the people and animals on the alp.
65008.m: The Alpine blessing protects people and animals on the alp.

65009.e: The Alpine blessing is half sung and half called. The Senn asks God for protection.
65009.m: The Alpine blessing is a prayer call.

65011.q: What is the Alpine blessing meant to protect the alp from?
65011.e: On the alp there is the danger of thunderstorms, falling rocks and accidents. The Alpine blessing asks for protection from them.
65011.m: The Alpine blessing asks for protection from misfortune.

65012.q: In which parts of Switzerland can you mainly hear the Alpine blessing?
65012.e: The Alpine blessing is a Catholic custom. You hear it mainly in Central Switzerland, but also in Eastern Switzerland and in Upper Valais.
65012.m: The Alpine blessing is called on Catholic alps.

65013.q: On which day of the week is Corpus Christi celebrated?
65013.e: Corpus Christi is always on a Thursday. It falls 60 days after Easter.
65013.m: Corpus Christi is always on a Thursday.

65014.e: In a procession many people walk through the streets praying and singing.
65014.m: A procession is a solemn parade.

65015.q: What do people sometimes lay on the streets at Corpus Christi?
65015.e: People lay colourful pictures made of flower petals on the route. The procession walks over them.
65015.m: At Corpus Christi carpets of flowers decorate the streets.

65016.q: What does the priest carry in the Corpus Christi procession?
65016.e: The monstrance is a golden vessel that shows the host in the middle. The priest carries it solemnly.
65016.m: The monstrance is carried in the procession.

65017.q: What is carried above the priest at Corpus Christi?
65017.e: A canopy is a fabric roof on poles. Four men carry it above the priest.
65017.m: A canopy is a fabric roof above the priest.

65018.e: Corpus Christi is a festival of the Catholic Church. In Catholic cantons it is a public holiday.
65018.m: Corpus Christi is a Catholic festival.

65019.q: Which men march along in old uniforms at Corpus Christi in the Lötschental?
65019.e: In the Lötschental in Valais the Herrgottsgrenadiere accompany the procession in old uniforms and tall hats.
65019.m: In the Lötschental the Herrgottsgrenadiere march along.

65020.q: Where does the Corpus Christi procession stop along the way to pray?
65020.e: Along the way there are decorated altars outdoors. People stop there, pray and receive the blessing.
65020.m: The procession stops at outdoor altars.

65021.q: On which Sunday is the Federal Day of Prayer in most cantons?
a: On the third Sunday in September
On the first Sunday in May
On the last Sunday in December
On the second Sunday in July
65021.e: The Day of Prayer is on the third Sunday in September almost everywhere. Only Geneva has its own date.
65021.m: The Day of Prayer is on the third Sunday in September.

65022.q: What do people traditionally do on the Day of Prayer?
65022.e: On the Day of Prayer people give thanks for the good things and pray for the country.
65022.m: On the Day of Prayer people give thanks and pray.

65023.q: Who is the Federal Day of Prayer meant for?
65023.e: The Day of Prayer brings together people of different religions and denominations in Switzerland.
65023.m: The Day of Prayer is for people of all religions.

65024.q: Which tart is eaten in many families on the Day of Prayer?
65024.e: In the past people cooked simple meals on the Day of Prayer. That is why there was often a plum tart, because plums are ripe in September.
65024.m: On the Day of Prayer people like to eat plum tart.

65025.q: Which canton celebrates its own Day of Prayer on a Thursday?
65025.e: Geneva celebrates the Geneva Fast on the Thursday after the first Sunday in September. In French it is called “Jeûne genevois”.
65025.m: Geneva has its own Day of Prayer on a Thursday.

65026.q: What is the full name of the Day of Prayer?
a: Day of Thanksgiving, Repentance and Prayer
Day of Thanksgiving, Celebration and Prayer
Day of Praise, Repentance and Prayer
Day of Thanksgiving, Fasting and Prayer
65026.e: The full name is the Federal Day of Thanksgiving, Repentance and Prayer. People give thanks, think about their mistakes and pray.
65026.m: The Day of Prayer is called the Day of Thanksgiving, Repentance and Prayer.

65027.q: What does the word “Federal” mean in the name Federal Day of Prayer?
65027.e: Federal means that it concerns the whole of Switzerland. The Day of Prayer is a holiday for the whole country.
65027.m: Federal means for all of Switzerland.

65028.q: Which season begins at roughly the time of the Day of Prayer?
65028.e: The Day of Prayer falls shortly before the start of autumn. It is harvest time, and people give thanks for the harvest.
65028.m: The Day of Prayer falls at the time when autumn begins.

65029.e: The bells hang high up in the church tower. That way they can be heard in the whole village.
65029.m: The bells hang in the church tower.

65030.q: What are children told in Catholic areas when the bells are silent before Easter?
a: The bells sleep in the forest
The bells are in the snow
The bells bathe in the lake
65030.e: From Maundy Thursday until the Easter Vigil the bells are silent. People say they have flown to Rome.
65030.m: Before Easter the bells fly to Rome.

65031.q: What is the bell-ringing on Saturday evening before Sunday called?
65031.e: On Saturday evening the bells ring for longer. People say they are ringing in Sunday.
65031.m: On Saturday evening Sunday is rung in.

65032.q: When do the bells ring for midday in many villages?
65032.e: In many villages the midday bell rings at 11 or 12 o'clock. In the past it told the farmers: time to eat.
65032.m: The midday bell rings at 11 or 12 o'clock.

65033.q: What does it often mean when a single bell rings slowly?
65033.e: The death knell tells the village that a person has died.
65033.m: The death knell remembers a person who has died.

65034.e: A chapel is a small place of worship. It often has only a few benches.
65034.m: A chapel is a small church.

65035.q: Where in Switzerland are there especially many small chapels?
65035.e: In the mountains people built chapels along paths and on alps. There they could pray.
65035.m: There are many small chapels in the mountains.

65036.q: Why did mountain farmers in the past build chapels in dangerous places?
65036.e: In the mountains there were avalanches, falling rocks and thunderstorms. In the chapel people asked for protection.
65036.m: Mountain chapels are places to ask for protection.

65037.q: Which well-known chapel on Lake Uri remembers a Swiss hero?
65037.e: Tell's Chapel stands on the shore of Lake Uri. William Tell is said to have jumped out of the boat there.

65038.q: What does a small mountain chapel normally not have?
65038.e: Mountain chapels are small and remote. A priest only comes now and then for a Mass.
65038.m: A mountain chapel usually has no priest of its own.

65039.q: What did people in the past hang up in chapels as a thank you?
65039.e: When someone had been saved, they often hung up a painted thank-you picture. It is called a votive picture.
65039.m: Votive pictures in chapels say thank you.

65040.q: What can be seen on the roof of many mountain chapels?
65040.e: Many chapels have a little turret with a small bell on the roof. It is called a ridge turret.
65040.m: Many chapels have a small bell turret.

a: A small pillar with a picture of a saint
65041.e: A wayside shrine is like a tiny chapel. It carries a picture of Jesus, Mary or a saint.
65041.m: A wayside shrine is a small holy place by the path.

65042.q: Where does a summit cross stand?
a: On the highest point of a mountain
On the shore of a lake
65042.e: A summit cross stands right at the top of a mountain. It marks the highest point.
65042.m: The summit cross stands on the mountain top.

65043.q: What materials are summit crosses usually made of?
65043.e: Summit crosses have to withstand wind and weather. That is why they are made of wood or metal.
65043.m: Summit crosses are made of wood or metal.

65044.q: What do you often find in a box by the summit cross?
65044.e: Climbers write their name and the date in the summit book.
65044.m: You write your name in the summit book.

65045.q: What does a summit cross show hikers?
a: That they have reached the top
What the weather will be like
65045.e: Anyone who reaches the summit cross is standing at the highest point. The cross is a goal for hikers.
65045.m: At the summit cross you have reached your goal.

65046.q: What is a summit cross a sign of?
65046.e: The cross is the sign of Christianity. With the summit cross people give thanks for protection in the mountains.
65046.m: The summit cross is a Christian sign.

65047.q: How are heavy summit crosses often brought up the mountain today?
65047.e: In the past people carried the crosses up. Today a helicopter often flies the heavy parts to the summit.
65047.m: A helicopter often brings heavy summit crosses up.

65048.q: What do you not do at a summit cross, out of respect?
65048.e: For many people a summit cross is a holy sign. That is why you do not climb around on it.
65048.m: You do not climb on a summit cross.

65049.q: Why is it dangerous to stand by the summit cross in a thunderstorm?
65049.e: A summit cross is the highest point far and wide. Lightning often strikes there.
65049.m: In a thunderstorm you keep away from the summit cross.

65050.q: What is a woman who lives in a convent called?
65050.e: Women who give their lives to God and live in a convent are called nuns.
65050.m: A woman in a convent is a nun.

65051.q: What does the monastery motto “ora et labora” mean?
65051.e: The Latin motto means “pray and work”. This is how the Benedictines live.
65051.m: Ora et labora means pray and work.

65052.q: What is the robe of a nun or a monk called?
65052.e: The robe of a religious order is called a habit. Each order has its own colour and shape.
65052.m: The robe of a religious order is called a habit.

65053.q: What do many nuns wear on their heads?
65053.e: Many nuns wear a veil. It is part of their habit.

65054.q: What do nuns and monks often grow in the monastery garden?
65054.e: Herbs, vegetables and flowers grow in the monastery garden. In the past the herbs were used to make medicines.
65054.m: Medicinal herbs grow in the monastery garden.

65055.q: What is the walkway around a courtyard in a monastery called?
65055.e: The cloister surrounds a garden inside the monastery. Nuns and monks walk there to pray and think.
65055.m: The cloister runs around the monastery courtyard.

65056.q: Which convent lies near the city of Zurich on the river Limmat?
65056.e: Fahr Convent is a convent of Benedictine nuns on the Limmat. It belongs to Einsiedeln Abbey.
65056.m: Benedictine nuns live in Fahr Convent.

65057.q: How often a day do nuns in a convent pray together?
65057.e: Nuns meet several times a day for prayer. This is called the Liturgy of the Hours.
65057.m: In the convent people pray several times a day.

65058.q: Where was the ship Jonah fled on supposed to sail to?
65058.e: In Joppa, Jonah boarded a ship to Tarshish. It lay far away in the other direction.
65058.m: Jonah wanted to flee by ship to Tarshish.

65059.q: What did Jonah do while the storm was raging?
65059.e: The sailors were very afraid and prayed. But Jonah lay below deck and slept deeply.
65059.m: Jonah slept in the middle of the storm.

65060.q: What did the sailors throw into the sea first to make the ship lighter?
65060.e: The sailors threw the cargo overboard. They hoped that the ship would not sink.
65060.m: The sailors first threw the cargo into the sea.

65061.q: How did the sailors find out who had caused the storm?
65061.e: The sailors cast lots. The lot fell on Jonah.
65061.m: The lots showed that the storm came because of Jonah.

65062.q: According to the text of the Bible, which animal swallowed Jonah?
65062.e: The Bible says “a great fish”. Many people simply call it a whale.
65062.m: In the Bible, a great fish swallows Jonah.

65063.q: Where did the great fish spit Jonah out again?
a: In the middle of the sea
65063.e: God spoke to the fish, and the fish spat Jonah out onto dry land. So Jonah was saved.
65063.m: The fish spat Jonah out on land.

65064.q: According to Jonah's warning, after how many days would Nineveh be destroyed?
65064.e: Jonah called out in the city: “In 40 days Nineveh will be destroyed.” This warning frightened the people.
65064.m: Jonah warned Nineveh of its end in 40 days.

65065.q: Apart from the people, who else had to fast in Nineveh?
65065.e: The king ordered that people and animals should not eat or drink anything. Even cattle and sheep had to fast.
65065.m: In Nineveh even the animals fasted.

65066.q: How did Jonah feel when God spared the city of Nineveh?
65066.e: Jonah had wanted the city to be punished. That is why he was annoyed at God's kindness.
65066.m: Jonah was annoyed that God spared Nineveh.

65068.q: Which of his father's sons was David?
65068.e: David was the youngest of several brothers. The older brothers were soldiers.

65069.q: Why did David come to the soldiers' camp?
a: He brought food for his brothers
He wanted to become a soldier
He was looking for a lost sheep
He brought the king a message
65069.e: His father sent David with bread and cheese to his brothers. There David heard Goliath mocking the Israelites.
65069.m: David brought food to his brothers in the camp.

65070.q: Which animals had David already defeated as a shepherd?
65070.e: David told how he had saved his sheep from lions and bears. That is why he was not afraid of the giant.
65070.m: David had protected his sheep from lions and bears.

65071.q: What did David trust in during the fight against Goliath?
65071.e: David told Goliath that he came in the name of God. He trusted that God would help him.
65071.m: David trusted in God during the fight.

65072.q: Where did David's stone hit the giant Goliath?
65072.e: The stone hit Goliath on the forehead. Then the giant fell down.
65072.m: The stone hit Goliath on the forehead.

65073.q: For how many days did Goliath challenge the Israelites to fight?
65073.e: According to the Bible, Goliath stood there every morning and evening for 40 days. No one from Israel dared to fight him.

65074.q: What did the Philistines do when Goliath had fallen?
65074.e: The Philistines saw that their strongest fighter was dead. Then they ran away, and the Israelites chased them.
65074.m: After Goliath's fall, the Philistines fled.

65075.q: What was the name of David's best friend, a son of the king?
65075.e: Jonathan was the king's son. He and David liked each other very much and became close friends.

65076.q: What was Daniel at the king's court?
65076.e: The king had made Daniel one of his highest officials. Daniel was clever and reliable.
65076.m: Daniel was a high official of the king.

65077.e: Other officials were jealous of Daniel. They looked for a reason to accuse him.
65077.m: Jealous officials wanted to harm Daniel.

65078.q: For how long was nobody allowed to pray to anyone except the king?
65078.e: The officials persuaded the king to make a law. For 30 days, people could only ask the king for anything.
65078.m: The ban on prayer lasted 30 days.

65079.q: How did Daniel pray at home?
65079.e: Daniel knelt down, prayed and gave thanks to God. That is how he had always done it.
65079.m: Daniel prayed to God on his knees.

65080.q: What did the king use to seal the stone in front of the lions' den?
65080.e: The king pressed his signet ring onto the stone. That way nobody could secretly change anything.
65080.m: The king sealed the den with his ring.

65081.q: When did the king go back to the lions' den?
65081.e: The king got up at first light and hurried to the den. He called out for Daniel.
65081.m: The king hurried to the den early in the morning.

65082.q: How was Daniel in the morning?
65082.e: The lions had not harmed Daniel. He did not have a single wound.
65082.m: Daniel came out of the lions' den unhurt.

65083.q: What happened to the men who had accused Daniel?
a: They were thrown to the lions themselves
65083.e: The king had the accusers thrown into the lions' den themselves. So they received the punishment they had planned for Daniel.
65083.m: Daniel's accusers were thrown to the lions themselves.

65084.q: What did the king order all people to do after Daniel was saved?
65084.e: The king was amazed at the rescue. He wrote to all peoples that they should honour the God of Daniel.
65084.m: After the rescue, the king had Daniel's God honoured.

65085.q: What did the people in Babel want to build?
65085.e: The people wanted to build a city with a tower. Its top was to reach up to heaven.
65085.m: In Babel, people wanted to build a tower reaching to heaven.

65086.q: What did the people build the Tower of Babel from?
65086.e: The people baked bricks from clay. For mortar they used tar.
65086.m: The Tower of Babel was built from bricks.

65087.q: How many languages did people speak before the tower was built?
65087.e: The Bible says that at that time all people had the same language. So they could work well together.
65087.m: Before the tower was built, all people had one language.

65088.q: What did God do so that people would not keep building?
a: He set the tower on fire
65088.e: God made sure that people could no longer understand each other. That is why they could not keep building.

65089.q: What happened to the people of Babel after that?
a: They all stayed in the city
65089.e: The people no longer understood each other and went their separate ways. In this way they spread out over the whole earth.
65089.m: After the tower, people spread out over the earth.

65090.q: Why did the people want to build the tall tower?
65090.e: The people said they wanted to make a name for themselves. So they wanted to be great and famous.
65090.m: The people wanted to become famous with the tower.

65091.q: Babel is another name for Babylon. In which present-day country was this city?
65091.e: The ancient city of Babylon was on the River Euphrates. Its ruins are in Iraq today.
65091.m: The ruins of Babylon are in Iraq.

65092.q: What do people mean today by a “babel” of languages?
65092.e: The expression comes from the story of Babel. People use it when many languages are being spoken all mixed up together.
65092.m: A babel of languages is a muddle of many languages.

65093.q: Who were the parents of Cain and Abel?
65093.e: According to the Bible, Cain and Abel were the first sons of Adam and Eve.
65093.m: Cain and Abel were sons of Adam and Eve.

65094.e: Abel kept sheep. That is why he brought an animal from his flock as his gift.

65095.e: Cain worked the fields. That is why he brought produce from the field as his gift.

65096.q: What did Cain and Abel both bring to God?
65096.e: Both brothers wanted to thank God. Each brought him something from what he had worked for.
65096.m: Cain and Abel brought God an offering.

a: God looked kindly on Abel's gift
65097.e: God was pleased with Abel's gift, but not with Cain's. Then Cain became jealous and furious.
65097.m: Cain became angry out of jealousy of his brother.

65098.q: What did God ask Cain after his evil deed?
65098.e: God knew what had happened. But he asked Cain anyway, so that he would tell the truth.
65098.m: God asked Cain about his brother.

65099.q: What did Cain answer to God's question?
65099.e: Cain did not want to admit what he had done. He answered cheekily with another question.

65100.q: What did God give Cain so that nobody would kill him?
65100.e: God put a mark on Cain. It is called the mark of Cain. It was meant to protect him.
65100.m: The mark of Cain protected Cain from other people.

65101.q: How were Jacob and Esau related?
65101.e: Jacob and Esau were born on the same day as twins. Esau was born shortly before Jacob.
65101.m: Jacob and Esau were twin brothers.

65102.q: What were the names of Jacob and Esau's parents?
65102.e: Isaac was Abraham's son. With his wife Rebekah he had the twins Jacob and Esau.
65102.m: Isaac and Rebekah were the parents of Jacob and Esau.

65103.q: What did Esau especially like doing?
65103.e: Esau was a skilful hunter and spent a lot of time outdoors. Jacob preferred to stay by the tents.

65104.q: What did Esau sell his right as the firstborn for?
65104.e: Esau came back hungry from hunting. For a plate of lentils he gave his birthright to Jacob.
65104.m: Esau sold his birthright for lentils.

65105.q: What did Jacob disguise himself with so that his blind father would think he was Esau?
65105.e: Esau had a lot of hair on his body. So Jacob put goatskins on his hands and neck.
65105.m: Jacob tricked his father with goatskins.

65106.q: Who helped Jacob with the trick to get the blessing?
65106.e: His mother loved Jacob especially. She cooked the food and gave Jacob Esau's clothes.
65106.m: Jacob's mother helped him with the trick.

65107.q: What did Jacob see in a dream while he was fleeing?
65107.e: Jacob slept on a stone and dreamed of a ladder. Angels were going up and down on it.
65107.m: Jacob dreamed of a ladder to heaven.

65108.q: How does the story of Jacob and Esau end?
a: They never see each other again
65108.e: After many years the brothers met again. Esau hugged Jacob and they made peace.
65108.m: In the end, Jacob and Esau made peace.

65109.q: What was the name of Samuel's mother?
65109.e: Samuel's mother was called Hannah. Her husband was called Elkanah.

65110.q: What had Samuel's mother asked God for for a long time?
65110.e: His mother was sad because she had no child. She prayed, and God gave her the son Samuel.

65111.q: With which priest did Samuel grow up in the sanctuary?
65111.e: His mother brought Samuel to the priest Eli. There he helped in the sanctuary.
65111.m: Samuel grew up with the priest Eli.

65112.q: What did young Samuel hear in the night?
65112.e: Samuel was lying asleep in the sanctuary. Then he heard a voice calling “Samuel”.
65112.m: In the night a voice called Samuel by name.

65113.q: How many times did Samuel run to the priest before the priest realised that God was calling?
65113.e: Each time Samuel thought the priest had called. The third time, the priest realised that God was calling Samuel.
65113.m: Samuel ran to the priest three times.

65114.q: What was Samuel supposed to answer if the voice called again?
65114.e: The priest told Samuel to listen to God. Samuel was to answer: “Speak, Lord, for your servant is listening.”
65114.m: Samuel learned to listen to God.

65115.q: What did Samuel become when he grew up?
65115.e: Samuel became an important prophet in Israel. He told the people what God wanted from them.

65116.q: Whom did Samuel anoint as the first king of Israel?
65116.e: The people wanted to have a king. Samuel anointed Saul with oil as the first king.
65116.m: Samuel anointed Saul as Israel's first king.

65117.q: Which country did Ruth come from?
65117.e: Ruth was a Moabite. So she was not an Israelite.
65117.m: Ruth came from the land of Moab.

65118.q: What was the name of Ruth's mother-in-law?
65118.e: Naomi was the mother of Ruth's husband. In German Bibles she is also called Noomi.

65119.e: Ruth's husband died young. Naomi's other son and her husband had also died.

65120.q: What did Ruth promise her mother-in-law?
a: “I am going back to my mother”
“I will look for a new family”
65120.e: Ruth did not want to leave her mother-in-law alone. She stayed loyally with her.
65120.m: Ruth stayed loyal to her mother-in-law.

65121.q: Which town did Ruth and her mother-in-law go to?
65121.e: The two women went to Bethlehem. The mother-in-law's family came from there.
65121.m: Ruth moved to Bethlehem with her mother-in-law.

65122.q: What did Ruth collect in the field?
65122.e: Poor people were allowed to pick up the leftover ears of grain after the harvest. That way Ruth and her mother-in-law got grain to eat.
65122.m: Ruth gathered leftover ears of grain in the field.

65123.q: Who owned the field where Ruth gathered grain?
65123.e: The field belonged to Boaz, a rich relative of the family. He was kind to Ruth.

65124.q: Which famous king was a great-grandson of Ruth?
65124.e: Ruth's son was called Obed. Obed's grandson was David, who later became king of Israel.

65125.e: The king of Persia chose Esther as his wife. So she became queen.

65126.q: How was Mordecai related to Esther?
65126.e: Esther's parents had died. Her cousin Mordecai took her in and brought her up like a daughter.
65126.m: Esther grew up with her cousin Mordecai.

65127.q: In the Book of Esther, who wanted to have all the Jews in the empire killed?
65127.e: Haman was a powerful minister of the king. He hated the Jews and planned evil against them.
65127.m: Haman wanted to destroy the Jews.

65128.q: Why was Haman so angry with Mordecai?
a: He did not bow down to him
65128.e: Everyone had to bow down to Haman. Mordecai did not, and said that he was a Jew.
65128.m: Mordecai did not bow down to Haman.

65129.q: Why was it dangerous for Esther to go to the king?
a: It was the middle of the night
65129.e: Anyone who went to the king without being summoned could be killed. Esther went anyway, to save her people.
65129.m: Esther bravely went to the king without being summoned.

65130.q: What did Esther invite the king and Haman to?
65130.e: Esther invited the king and Haman to a banquet. There she asked the king to save her people.
65130.m: Esther invited the king to a banquet.

65131.e: At Purim, Jewish people celebrate the rescue told in the story of Esther. Many children dress up in costumes.
65131.m: The festival of Purim remembers Queen Esther.

65132.q: How long did Esther and her people fast before she went to the king?
65132.e: Esther asked all the Jews in the city to fast for her for three days. She fasted too.
65132.m: Esther fasted for three days before going to the king.

65133.q: Which birds brought the prophet Elijah bread and meat by the brook?
65133.e: Elijah hid by a brook. God sent ravens that brought him bread and meat morning and evening.

65134.q: What never ran out at the home of the poor widow who took Elijah in?
65134.e: The widow had only a little flour and oil left. Because she helped Elijah, the flour jar and the oil jug did not run empty.
